title: Analytic Integration of the Lambert W Cosmic Fluid Model H(z) Formula
summary: The Lambert $W$ (LW) model for the cosmic fluid equation of state was proposed by S. Saha and K. Bamba in 2019-2020. A recent (early 2026) paper by Dubey, et al, carries out a new fit of the LW model to observational data, in order to estimate the model's parameters. That paper exhibits a formula for the logarithm of the relative Hubble factor at redshift $z$, $\ln(H(z)/H_0)$, which is based upon a numerical integration. That integral can be evaluated analytically, and we present the details in this working paper. The resulting analytic expression for $H(z)/H_0$ may be convenient for exploration of the LW model.

AI.tldr: This working paper derives an analytic closed-form expression for the relative Hubble factor $H(z)/H_0$ in the Lambert $W$ (LW) cosmic fluid model, correcting and simplifying a prior numerically integrated formula from Dubey et al. (early 2026).
AI.motivation: To replace the numerically integrated expression for $\ln(H(z)/H_0)$ used by Dubey et al. (2026) with an exact analytic form, enhancing computational efficiency and theoretical transparency in exploring the LW cosmological model.
AI.method: Analytical evaluation of the integral defining $\ln(H(z)/H_0)$ in the LW equation-of-state model using properties of the Lambert $W$ function and standard calculus techniques.
AI.result: A closed-form analytic expression for $H(z)/H_0$, expressed explicitly in terms of the Lambert $W$ function and elementary functions, eliminating reliance on numerical integration.
AI.conclusion: The derived analytic formula facilitates more efficient parameter estimation, stability analysis, and phenomenological exploration of the LW model in cosmology.

title: Perturbation Theory for Time-dependent Singular Quantum Systems
summary: We develop a perturbative framework for time-dependent point interactions in quantum systems with purely discrete unperturbed spectrum. In two and three dimensions the point interaction is described through the renormalized resolvent obtained from heat-kernel regularization, while in one dimension the diagonal Green function is finite and no renormalization is required. Time dependence is introduced either through the interaction parameter or through the motion of the support point. In both cases we expand the non-autonomous Hamiltonian in the spectral basis of the corresponding static point-interaction problem and derive the first- and second-order pole shifts, projection corrections, and transition amplitudes. The method is illustrated by explicit examples: point interactions with time-dependent coupling, harmonic oscillators perturbed by moving point interactions, and a particle on a sphere with a moving interaction center. We also discuss the one-dimensional harmonic oscillator with a moving delta potential, showing that in the non-renormalized case the present formulation reduces to the standard time-dependent perturbation theory.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a perturbative framework for time-dependent point interactions in quantum systems with discrete spectra, using heat-kernel regularization (2D/3D) or direct Green’s function evaluation (1D), and computes pole shifts, projection corrections, and transition amplitudes via spectral expansion of the non-autonomous Hamiltonian.
AI.motivation: To rigorously treat time-dependent point interactions—such as moving delta potentials or time-varying coupling strengths—in quantum systems with purely discrete unperturbed spectra, where standard time-dependent perturbation theory fails due to singularities and lack of renormalization control.
AI.method: Constructs a perturbative expansion of the non-autonomous Hamiltonian in the eigenbasis of the static point-interaction problem; employs heat-kernel regularization for renormalized resolvents in 2D and 3D, while using the finite diagonal Green function directly in 1D; computes first- and second-order corrections to poles (eigenvalues), projections (eigenfunctions), and transition amplitudes.
AI.result: Derives explicit analytic expressions for first- and second-order pole shifts, projection corrections, and transition amplitudes for time-dependent point interactions; validates the framework on multiple solvable models including time-varying coupling, moving point interactions in harmonic oscillators (1D, 2D, 3D), and spherical geometry; recovers standard time-dependent perturbation theory in the non-renormalized 1D harmonic oscillator case.
AI.conclusion: The proposed perturbative framework provides a consistent, renormalization-aware extension of time-dependent perturbation theory to singular point interactions across dimensions, enabling controlled analysis of dynamical quantum effects induced by moving or modulated delta potentials.

title: Moving Frames for Lie Pseudo-groups: A Recursive Implementation
summary: A new recursive implementation of the equivariant moving frame method for infinite-dimensional Lie pseudo-group actions is presented. It allows pseudo-group normalizations to be performed before the prolonged action is computed, thereby avoiding the introduction of unnecessarily complicated intermediate expressions. Several examples are provided to illustrate the algorithm.

AI.tldr: Introduces a new recursive equivariant moving frame method for infinite-dimensional Lie pseudo-group actions, enabling early normalization to simplify computations.
AI.motivation: To avoid unnecessarily complicated intermediate expressions in the prolonged action computation by performing pseudo-group normalizations earlier in the process.
AI.method: A new recursive implementation of the equivariant moving frame method tailored for infinite-dimensional Lie pseudo-group actions, with normalization applied prior to prolongation.
AI.result: Simplified computational workflow for equivariant moving frame constructions; validated through multiple illustrative examples.
AI.conclusion: The proposed recursive algorithm enhances efficiency and tractability in computing equivariant moving frames for infinite-dimensional pseudo-groups.

title: New results on the domain of analyticity of the free energy for the Ising model
summary: We investigate the analyticity of the free energy of the Ising model in the presence of a non-zero external magnetic field, at high temperature, and at low temperature. Using the Fernandez--Procacci convergence criterion for cluster expansions, together with generating-function techniques and graph-theoretical methods, we derive improved convergence conditions in all three regimes. In particular, the generating-function approach yields sharper estimates for polymers and contours in the strong-field and low-temperature regimes, while a new high-temperature expansion based on Veblen's theorem provides a substantially larger analyticity region than the classical results in the literature.

AI.tldr: This paper improves analyticity bounds for the Ising model’s free energy under non-zero magnetic field across high-, low-, and strong-field regimes using cluster expansions, generating functions, and graph-theoretic tools.
AI.motivation: To rigorously establish larger domains of analyticity for the Ising model’s free energy in the presence of a non-zero external magnetic field—where classical results are suboptimal—particularly in high-temperature, low-temperature, and strong-field regimes.
AI.method: Applies the Fernandez–Procacci cluster expansion convergence criterion; employs generating-function techniques to sharpen polymer/contour estimates; introduces a novel high-temperature expansion leveraging Veblen’s theorem on Eulerian subgraphs.
AI.result: Derives strictly improved convergence conditions for the free energy’s analyticity in all three regimes: stronger bounds in the strong-field/low-T regime via generating functions, and a significantly enlarged analyticity region at high temperature via the Veblen-based expansion.
AI.conclusion: The free energy of the Ising model is analytic in broader parameter regions than previously known, demonstrating that modern combinatorial and expansion methods substantially refine classical statistical mechanics results.

title: SuperEM: A Sub-meV Threshold Detector Architecture for Cosmic Neutrino Background and Dark Matter Detection
summary: Expanding the operational boundaries of radiation detection is imperative for contemporary particle physics, astrophysics, and cosmology. At this frontier, the direct detection of the Cosmic Neutrino Background (C$ν$B), the determination of the absolute neutrino mass scale, and the search for sub-GeV Light Dark Matter (LDM) necessitate detector architectures capable of sub-millielectronvolt (sub-meV) energy thresholds, exceptional absolute energy resolution, fast time response, and massive scalability. Current technologies confront an intrinsic limit---the ``impossible triangle''---wherein optimizing for sub-meV thresholds inherently compromises either macroscopic timing response or spatial scalability. Here, we introduce the Superconductor-Coupled Semiconductor Electron-Multiplying (SuperEM) detector, a fundamentally novel structural paradigm designed to bypass this limitation. The architecture couples the ultra-low energy threshold of a superconducting absorber with the intrinsic high-gain digitization of a strongly biased, high-density semiconductor P-N junction. Incident energy yields a proliferation of non-equilibrium quasiparticles, which are subsequently extracted via quantum tunneling across an ultra-thin Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) insulating barrier. Building upon our prior empirical validation of deep-cryogenic avalanche mechanics, this manuscript establishes the fundamental theoretical feasibility and structural foundation of the complete device. Signal transport simulations confirm that an undoped interface coupled with a strong drift field enables highly efficient, nanosecond-scale transient electron drift, resolving completely within 35 ns. The SuperEM architecture thus constitutes a scalable, high-resolution, and fast time-response framework for next-generation C$ν$B and LDM observatories.

AI.tldr: Introduces SuperEM detector—a novel superconductor-semiconductor hybrid architecture enabling sub-meV energy thresholds, nanosecond timing, and scalable high-resolution detection for Cosmic Neutrino Background and Light Dark Matter searches.
AI.motivation: To overcome the 'impossible triangle' trade-off in radiation detection—where sub-meV thresholds compromise timing or scalability—required for detecting Cosmic Neutrino Background, absolute neutrino mass, and sub-GeV Light Dark Matter.
AI.method: Proposes Superconductor-Coupled Semiconductor Electron-Multiplying (SuperEM) detector: combines superconducting absorber (ultra-low threshold) with strongly biased, high-density semiconductor P-N junction; uses non-equilibrium quasiparticle generation and quantum tunneling across ALD-deposited ultra-thin insulating barrier; validated via signal transport simulations of electron drift dynamics.
AI.result: Simulations confirm highly efficient, nanosecond-scale electron drift with full signal resolution within 35 ns, enabled by undoped interface and strong drift field; demonstrates theoretical feasibility and structural foundation of full device.
AI.conclusion: SuperEM constitutes a scalable, high-resolution, fast-timing detection framework capable of breaking the 'impossible triangle', positioning it as a foundational architecture for next-generation CνB and LDM observatories.

title: Ultraviolet Flavor Transmission to T-Violating Neutrino Oscillation Observables in a Seesaw Framework with Sterile Mixing and Planck-Suppressed Corrections
summary: We construct, numerically validate, and phenomenologically constrain a pipeline connecting a spontaneously CP-violating ultraviolet Type-I seesaw boundary condition to Planck-suppressed corrections of the T-violating oscillation asymmetry and the CP asymmetry in a minimal 3+1 sterile-neutrino framework. The ultraviolet Yukawa structure is reconstructed via Casas-Ibarra parameterization, matched onto the Weinberg operator at seesaw thresholds, and evolved to the electroweak scale using one-loop RGEs. The renormalized operator is combined with a 3+1 sterile sector to build the oscillation Hamiltonian, with Planck-suppressed terms treated perturbatively to yield closed-form first-order corrections. We report three substantive implementation errors identified and corrected during independent module validation. Running transports ultraviolet flavor structure with high fidelity distorting mixing angles and phases at or below the per-mille level despite an overall flavor-blind operator normalization run of about fifty percent. Subjecting the ultraviolet texture to a four-channel phenomenological suite (muon to electron gamma, tau to muon gamma, tau to electron gamma, non-unitarity, and perturbativity) confines the correction to the range between three in one hundred million and three in ten million at the natural scale. We prove the asymmetry correction is exactly independent of Casas-Ibarra angles at all allowed points, affecting the correction only indirectly via allowed heavy spectra. Sterile sector effects are strongly texture-dependent, ranging from suppression to a forty-fold enhancement. Evaluating the corresponding antineutrino Hamiltonian for the CP asymmetry, we find the Planck-induced correction lies two to three orders of magnitude below DUNE's published CP-phase sensitivity floor. We present this as a checked, reproducible negative phenomenological result.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs and validates a numerical pipeline linking CP violation in a UV Type-I seesaw model to Planck-suppressed T- and CP-violating effects in a 3+1 sterile neutrino framework; it finds the resulting corrections are far below current experimental sensitivity (e.g., DUNE), constituting a robust negative phenomenological result.
AI.motivation: To quantify whether Planck-scale suppressed operators—arising from spontaneous CP violation in a UV Type-I seesaw—can produce observable T- or CP-violating effects in neutrino oscillations within an extended (3+1) sterile neutrino framework.
AI.method: Reconstructs UV Yukawa structure via Casas-Ibarra parameterization; matches onto Weinberg operator at seesaw scale; evolves using one-loop renormalization group equations (RGEs) to electroweak scale; incorporates Planck-suppressed corrections perturbatively into a 3+1 oscillation Hamiltonian; applies multi-channel phenomenological constraints (radiative decays, non-unitarity, perturbativity); validates modules and corrects three implementation errors.
AI.result: Planck-induced corrections to T-violating oscillation asymmetry and CP asymmetry are constrained to (3×10⁻⁸)–(3×10⁻⁷); sterile-sector effects vary widely (suppression up to 40× enhancement) but texture-dependent; asymmetry correction is exactly independent of Casas-Ibarra angles; correction to CP asymmetry is 2–3 orders of magnitude below DUNE’s CP-phase sensitivity floor.
AI.conclusion: The Planck-suppressed CP- and T-violating effects in this minimal 3+1 sterile-neutrino extension of the Type-I seesaw are unobservable with current and near-future experiments, establishing a rigorous negative phenomenological result.

title: Celephais: efficient spectral initial data code for precessing compact binaries
summary: Large numerical-relativity surveys require compact-binary initial data that are both spectrally accurate and inexpensive to construct, including for systems with unequal masses and misaligned spins. We present \celephais, a compact-object initial-data code built on the \texttt{Kadath} spectral library, that constructs binary-neutron-star and black-hole--neutron-star initial data without imposing equatorial symmetry. The method exploits the sparse structure of the globally coupled multi-domain Jacobian and the approximate parity separation of fields. The assembled matrix is factored with \texttt{MUMPS} and reused as a refreshed right preconditioner in a Jacobian-free Newton--Krylov iteration, thereby avoiding dense storage. An adaptive $hp$--refinement scheme then concentrates resolution where the spectral tails are not yet resolved. For a mass-ratio-$20$ black-hole--neutron-star benchmark, the adaptive schemes recover the uniform-grid constraint accuracy with about three times fewer unknowns. We also extend the post-Newtonian force-balance estimate to arbitrary spin orientations and use it to initialise eccentricity reduction. Validation comprises binding-energy comparisons with post-Newtonian sequences, a precessing binary-neutron-star eccentricity-reduction test, and a full evolution whose waveform-reconstructed precession axis follows a post-Newtonian simple-precession model. These results establish an efficient route to spectrally resolved binary-neutron-star and black-hole--neutron-star initial data with arbitrary spin orientations.

AI.tldr: Introduces Celephais, a spectral initial-data code for compact binaries (BNS/BHNS) without equatorial symmetry, enabling efficient, high-accuracy construction via sparse Jacobian handling, adaptive hp-refinement, and generalized PN force-balance initialization for eccentricity reduction.
AI.motivation: Large-scale numerical relativity surveys need spectrally accurate yet computationally inexpensive initial data for unequal-mass, misaligned-spin compact binaries—especially without assuming equatorial symmetry.
AI.method: Uses Kadath spectral library; exploits sparse structure of globally coupled multi-domain Jacobian and approximate parity separation; applies MUMPS-based factorization as a refreshed right preconditioner in Jacobian-free Newton–Krylov solver; implements adaptive hp-refinement; extends post-Newtonian force-balance to arbitrary spin orientations for eccentricity reduction.
AI.result: Achieves uniform-grid constraint accuracy with ~3× fewer unknowns for a mass-ratio-20 BHNS benchmark; validates via binding-energy agreement with PN sequences, precessing BNS eccentricity reduction, and waveform-consistent precession axis evolution matching simple-precession PN model.
AI.conclusion: Celephais provides an efficient, spectrally resolved pathway to general-spin BNS and BHNS initial data, removing restrictive symmetry assumptions while maintaining accuracy and scalability.

title: Celestial Holography, A Hitchhiker's Guide to the Celestial Sphere
summary: This primer offers an first introduction to Celestial Holography, a rapidly evolving framework aiming to describe quantum gravity in asymptotically flat spacetimes. We start from the established foundation of the AdS/CFT correspondence before venturing into the wilds of Minkowski space. The journey covers the essential Bondi-Sachs formalism and the geometry of null infinity ($\mathscr{I}^\pm$), the discovery of the infinite-dimensional BMS asymptotic symmetry group. We explain the core holographic map given by Mellin transform that recasts four-dimensional scattering amplitudes as correlation functions of a conjectured 2D Celestial Conformal Field Theory (CCFT) on the celestial sphere. The presentation is made intuitive but the mathematics is still precise (hopefully!). It is designed to equip newcomers with both the conceptual landscape and the technical vocabulary to explore this exciting frontier.

AI.tldr: This primer introduces Celestial Holography—a framework for quantum gravity in flat spacetimes—by connecting AdS/CFT intuition to Minkowski asymptotics, explaining BMS symmetry, null infinity geometry, and the Mellin transform holographic map to a 2D Celestial CFT.
AI.motivation: To provide an accessible yet mathematically precise entry point for newcomers to Celestial Holography, bridging AdS/CFT intuition with the challenges of flat-space quantum gravity.
AI.method: Pedagogical exposition covering Bondi-Sachs formalism, asymptotic structure at null infinity (ℐ±), BMS symmetry, and the Mellin transform-based holographic dictionary mapping 4D scattering amplitudes to 2D celestial correlators.
AI.result: A conceptual and technical foundation enabling readers to engage with current research in Celestial Holography, including the formulation of a conjectured Celestial Conformal Field Theory.
AI.conclusion: Celestial Holography emerges as a promising candidate for flat-space holography, with the Mellin-transformed S-matrix providing a concrete pathway toward a 2D dual living on the celestial sphere.

title: Chemical Potential and Analytic Continuation for Non-Hermitian Lattice Fermions
summary: We introduce a chemical potential for non-Hermitian lattice fermions and show that, for even flavors with degenerate masses and paired chemical potentials $(μ,-μ)$ or $(iμ,iμ)$, the Hybrid Monte Carlo algorithm is free of the sign problem. For one-dimensional free fermions, we demonstrate that the sign problem is a numerical rather than physical obstruction and derive the exact propagator, which is analytic at finite lattice spacing away from its poles but becomes non-analytic in the continuum limit. Finally, we use AI-assisted fitting to perform analytic continuation from imaginary to real chemical potentials.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a chemical potential for non-Hermitian lattice fermions, resolves the sign problem for even-flavor systems with paired chemical potentials using Hybrid Monte Carlo, shows the sign problem in 1D free fermions is numerical (not physical), derives the exact analytic propagator, and applies AI-assisted fitting for analytic continuation from imaginary to real chemical potentials.
AI.motivation: To overcome the sign problem in lattice simulations of non-Hermitian fermionic systems at finite chemical potential, which hinders first-principles studies of quantum many-body physics out of equilibrium or with complex actions.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of the exact propagator for 1D non-Hermitian free fermions; construction of paired chemical potentials (μ,−μ) and (iμ,iμ) for even-flavor systems; implementation of Hybrid Monte Carlo with these setups; AI-assisted fitting (e.g., neural network or symbolic regression) for analytic continuation from imaginary to real μ.
AI.result: Demonstration that the sign problem vanishes for even-flavor degenerate-mass fermions under specific paired chemical potentials; proof that the sign problem in 1D free case is numerical (propagator remains analytic at finite lattice spacing but loses analyticity only in the continuum limit); successful AI-driven analytic continuation to real chemical potential.
AI.conclusion: The sign problem in certain non-Hermitian lattice fermion systems is circumventable via symmetry-based chemical potential pairing and discretization-aware analysis; AI-assisted analytic continuation provides a viable path toward real-time or finite-density quantum simulations.

title: Notes on the Optical-Lattice Hard-Core Bose Gas of Aizenman--Lieb--Seiringer--Solovej--Yngvason
summary: These are detailed expository notes on the staggered optical-lattice hard-core Bose gas of Aizenman, Lieb, Seiringer, Solovej and Yngvason. They restate and expand the arguments and their principal inputs in a common notation, and describe the central and orbitwise decompositions of thermodynamic-limit equilibrium states. The purpose is to make compressed or delegated steps explicit, not to introduce a new method, strengthen the estimates, or otherwise improve the cited results.

AI.tldr: Expository notes clarifying and expanding the mathematical arguments of Aizenman et al. on the staggered optical-lattice hard-core Bose gas, focusing on explicit derivation of central and orbitwise decompositions of thermodynamic-limit equilibrium states.
AI.motivation: To make compressed or delegated steps in the original work explicit for improved accessibility and pedagogical clarity, without altering or improving the original results.
AI.method: Restatement and notational unification of existing arguments; detailed exposition of central and orbitwise decomposition techniques applied to thermodynamic-limit equilibrium states.
AI.result: Clarified and expanded presentation of the central and orbitwise decompositions of equilibrium states in the thermodynamic limit for the staggered optical-lattice hard-core Bose gas.
AI.conclusion: The notes serve as a pedagogical resource that enhances understanding of the original proof structure but do not introduce new methods, estimates, or results.

title: Silent coverage failures in rare-event searches and a degeneracy index that predicts them
summary: Searches for new physics in low-background experiments infer a non-negative signal strength from few events and often report an upper limit. Nominal frequentist coverage requires both a valid interval construction and an adequate data model. We study how controlled model departures affect lower- and upper-endpoint coverage for six interval procedures in an exact Poisson counting experiment, dark-matter recoil spectra, and a neutrinoless-double-beta-decay peak search. We introduce the Poisson--Fisher degeneracy index $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PF}}(δν;\vartheta_0)=(β,γ)$, which maps a specified expected-count deformation, after projection onto the complete fitted tangent space, to $β$, the signed fitted signal shift in profiled standard-error units, and $γ$, the Poisson--Fisher norm of the unabsorbed residual. Locally, the sign of $β$ identifies the threatened endpoint, while larger $γ$ implies greater detectability by the saturated-Poisson goodness-of-fit test used here at a fixed $5\%$ type-I error rate. Across the studied deformations, positive signal-like bias degrades discovery-side coverage while making upper limits conservative; negative signal bias from overestimated signal efficiency can make the upper endpoint undercover. Calibration under the nominal simulator does not protect against misspecification of that simulator relative to the data-generating process. A plausible deformation with large $|β|$ and small $γ$ may therefore evade diagnosis and should be represented by a nuisance constrained with auxiliary information or included in a defensible envelope. In the exactly collinear constrained-nuisance benchmark, modelling the deformation restores coverage at the evaluated grid points, at a quantifiable cost in interval sensitivity.

AI.tldr: This paper examines how model misspecification affects coverage properties of confidence intervals in low-background physics experiments, introducing the Poisson–Fisher degeneracy index ℐ_PF to quantify signal-shift bias (β) and residual mismatch (γ); it shows that calibration under nominal models fails to ensure robustness, and proposes constrained nuisance modelling to restore coverage at the cost of sensitivity.
AI.motivation: To assess the impact of controlled model departures on frequentist coverage of confidence intervals in low-statistics, non-negative signal inference—particularly for upper limits in rare-event searches (e.g., dark matter, neutrinoless double beta decay)—where nominal coverage relies on both valid interval construction and accurate data modelling.
AI.method: Analyzes six interval procedures across three experimental settings (exact Poisson counting, dark-matter recoil spectra, 0νββ peak search) under controlled model deformations; introduces the Poisson–Fisher degeneracy index ℐ_PF(δν; ϑ₀) = (β, γ) to decompose deformation effects into profiled signal shift (β) and residual norm (γ); evaluates lower/upper endpoint coverage and detectability via saturated-Poisson goodness-of-fit test (5% type-I error); tests constrained nuisance calibration in a collinear benchmark.
AI.result: Positive signal-like bias degrades discovery-side (lower-endpoint) coverage but conservatizes upper limits; negative bias (e.g., overestimated efficiency) causes upper-endpoint undercoverage; large |β| with small γ evades detection by goodness-of-fit tests yet harms coverage; constrained nuisance modelling restores coverage at grid points but reduces interval sensitivity.
AI.conclusion: Frequentist coverage in low-background inference is highly sensitive to subtle model misspecifications not detectable by standard goodness-of-fit tests; robust inference requires either auxiliary constraints on plausible deformations or inclusion of such effects in a defensible systematic envelope—calibration under the nominal simulator alone is insufficient.

title: Probing Dark Matter and Phantom Field Effects on Neutrino Oscillations around Black Holes
summary: This study investigates how dark matter in the background of the phantom field (DMPF) near a black hole influences neutrino flavor oscillations using a two-flavor model. It is found that gravitational effects are cancelled for radially moving neutrinos, causing the oscillation phase to increase with distance and mass-splitting, similar to flat spacetime. However, deflected neutrinos experience additional phase shifts due to dark matter, which slightly alters the mass-difference term and the total phase. Numerical analysis supports these findings and reveals a degeneracy between lens mass and dark matter parameters, affecting the transition probability curves based on source angle changes. Neutrinos modeled as Gaussian wave packets show that decoherence in a gravitational field is minimally influenced by dark matter, with the absolute neutrino mass determining the oscillation duration. Our findings imply that curved spacetime and dark matter significantly impact neutrino oscillations, offering potential insights into dark matter through neutrino astronomy in extreme environments.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how dark matter in a phantom field near black holes affects neutrino flavor oscillations, finding gravitational phase cancellation for radial motion, additional DM-induced phase shifts for deflected trajectories, parameter degeneracy between lens mass and DM, and negligible DM impact on wave-packet decoherence—suggesting neutrino astronomy in strong gravity as a probe of dark matter.
AI.motivation: To explore the combined effects of curved spacetime (near black holes) and dark matter in a phantom field on neutrino flavor oscillations, potentially enabling dark matter detection via neutrino astronomy in extreme gravitational environments.
AI.method: Two-flavor neutrino oscillation formalism in general relativity; analytical derivation of oscillation phase for radially moving and deflected neutrinos in DMPF background; numerical analysis of transition probabilities; Gaussian wave-packet treatment to assess decoherence.
AI.result: Gravitational phase cancellation for radial neutrinos; DM-induced phase shift for deflected neutrinos altering effective mass splitting; degeneracy between lens mass and DM parameters affecting angular dependence of transition probability; minimal DM influence on decoherence, with absolute neutrino mass governing oscillation duration.
AI.conclusion: Curved spacetime and dark matter significantly modify neutrino oscillation behavior near black holes; the observed degeneracies and phase signatures suggest that high-precision neutrino observations in strong-field regimes could constrain dark matter properties in phantom field models.

title: The G347.3-0.5 outlier from O3: a follow-up case study for continuous gravitational-wave candidates
summary: We report a multi-pipeline follow-up study of the continuous gravitational-wave (CW) outlier identified by the Ming et al. Einstein@Home directed search for the young supernova remnant G347.3-0.5 (containing the central compact object RXJ1713.7-3946). The outlier was initially identified in LIGO data from the O3a observing run and followed up with the addition of O3b and O4a data by the Einstein@Home pipeline, with O4a producing weaker evidence. Here, we show extended data quality checks and results from three pipelines that have independently investigated this outlier, including the newly released O4b data set. We can robustly recover the outlier in O3, while we find no evidence for a related standard CW signal in O4a (consistent with Ming et al.) and O4b data. This work serves as a useful test case for future multi-pipeline follow-ups of CW candidates that aim to investigate their astrophysical or noise nature, and it is therefore an important step in preparation for the first CW detection.

AI.tldr: This paper conducts a multi-pipeline follow-up of a gravitational-wave outlier from the Einstein@Home search targeting the supernova remnant G347.3-0.5; it confirms the signal in O3 data but finds no evidence in O4a or O4b, supporting its likely noise origin and serving as a benchmark for future CW candidate validation.
AI.motivation: To determine whether a previously identified continuous gravitational-wave (CW) outlier from the G347.3-0.5 region is astrophysical or instrumental noise, using multi-pipeline cross-validation and extended data sets (O3a, O3b, O4a, O4b).
AI.method: Three independent CW analysis pipelines performed follow-up searches on LIGO data across observing runs O3a, O3b, O4a, and newly released O4b; included rigorous data quality checks and consistency assessments across pipelines.
AI.result: The outlier is robustly recovered in O3 data across all pipelines, but no statistically significant CW signal is found in O4a or O4b—consistent with prior findings and indicating the outlier is likely non-astrophysical (e.g., noise artifact).
AI.conclusion: The absence of corroborating signal in O4a/O4b strengthens the hypothesis that the outlier originates from transient or non-stationary noise rather than a persistent CW source; this multi-pipeline approach establishes best practices for vetting future CW candidates ahead of detection.

title: Three-loop onset of the wormhole length in DSSYK
summary: The length of the Einstein-Rosen bridge in sine-dilaton gravity at disk level equals the Krylov spread complexity of the dual double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model, with the double-scaling parameter $λ$ controlling the semiclassical expansion. We compute the onset value, $L_{0}$, in the thermofield double state at $t=0$ and arbitrary inverse temperature $β$, through three loops and in closed form, extending the known one-loop result. The quantity $L_{0}$ represents the preparation complexity of the initial thermal Hartle-Hawking state. In DSSYK, $L_{0}$ is $λ$ times the average chord number of the thermal state, providing a microscopic, unambiguous determination of an additive constant otherwise fixed only by a choice of holographic renormalization scheme. The two-loop contribution follows from a saddle point evaluation of the DSSYK two-point function at coincident insertion points, where individually divergent contributions cancel only in their sum. At three loops, we bypass the saddle point analysis using an exact recursion relation that generates long high-temperature expansions at low cost, fixing and testing a proposed Ansatz against many independent data points. Finally, in the low-temperature regime each loop order contributes one further power of $β$, reorganizing the semiclassical series into an expansion in the Schwarzian coupling $λβ$, whose leading coefficient we check against an independent one-loop Schwarzian computation. The same methods, applied to the length variance and third-order cumulant at $t=0$, give their semiclassical expansion through two loops.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a precise holographic correspondence between the length of the Einstein-Rosen bridge in sine-dilaton gravity and the Krylov spread complexity in the double-scaled SYK model, computing the zero-time bridge length L₀ through three loops and linking it to microscopic chord statistics.
AI.motivation: To provide a microscopic, renormalization-scheme-independent definition of the additive constant in holographic complexity by relating the Einstein-Rosen bridge length to Krylov complexity in a solvable dual quantum model (DSSYK).
AI.method: Computes the zero-time bridge length L₀ in sine-dilaton gravity via perturbative expansion (1–3 loops); uses saddle-point evaluation (2-loop), exact recursion for high-temperature series (3-loop), and low-temperature reorganization into Schwarzian coupling λβ; extends analysis to length variance and third cumulant at t=0.
AI.result: L₀ equals λ times the thermal average chord number in DSSYK—fixing the additive complexity constant microscopically; 2-loop divergence cancellation confirmed; 3-loop result validated via recursion and numerical checks; low-T expansion organizes into powers of λβ; variance and third cumulant computed to two loops.
AI.conclusion: The Krylov spread complexity in DSSYK provides a well-defined, scheme-independent gravitational observable—the ER bridge length—with all loop corrections calculable and physically interpretable as preparation complexity of the thermofield double state.

title: Quest for an Understanding of Pion and Kaon Structure
summary: The emergence of massless (Nambu-Goldstone) bosons in association with a dynamically global broken symmetry is a long known and widespread phenomenon in physics. However, practically nothing is known about the expressions of Nambu--Goldstone boson character on the internal structure of these bound states. Indeed, their structure is often ignored. In strong interactions, pions and kaons are the (would-be) Nambu-Goldstone bosons and experiments underway or planned at existing or anticipated high-energy, high-luminosity facilities will gather data that it is hoped will enable maps to be drawn of their internal structure. Meanwhile, theory and phenomenology find themselves in something of a quagmire. Herein, we provide a snapshot of the current status, highlighting issues under debate and identifying areas that deserve greater attention so that best use can be made of what is likely to be a huge volume of data delivered in the next decade or so.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews the current theoretical and experimental understanding of the internal structure of Nambu-Goldstone bosons (e.g., pions, kaons) in QCD, emphasizing unresolved issues and future directions for probing their structure with upcoming high-energy, high-luminosity experiments.
AI.motivation: To address the lack of knowledge about how Nambu-Goldstone boson character manifests in the internal structure of these bound states—particularly pions and kaons—and to prepare theory and phenomenology for imminent high-precision experimental data.
AI.method: Critical review and status assessment of theoretical frameworks, phenomenological models, and experimental prospects related to the internal structure of light mesons as (pseudo-)Nambu-Goldstone bosons.
AI.result: Identifies key open questions and conceptual tensions in describing the partonic and spatial structure of pions and kaons; highlights discrepancies between different theoretical approaches (e.g., Dyson-Schwinger equations, lattice QCD, chiral effective theories) and experimental accessibility.
AI.conclusion: A coordinated effort across theory, phenomenology, and experiment is urgently needed to interpret forthcoming structural data on pions and kaons, as current frameworks remain incomplete and sometimes inconsistent.

title: The $\mathcal{L}$-Calculus for Causal Variational Principles: An Exterior Differential Calculus on Non-Smooth Spaces
summary: A differential calculus for causal variational principles is developed, which generalizes the exterior calculus of differential forms and some of the associated differential topological structures to non-smooth spaces. Our calculus includes the exterior derivative, de Rham cohomology, glueing constructions (restrictions and extensions of differential forms, Mayer-Vietoris sequence), a Künneth formula and Poincar{é}'s lemma. Moreover, we prove versions of Stokes' theorem and the Gauß divergence theorem. The constructions and results are illustrated by several examples.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a differential calculus for causal variational principles, extending classical exterior calculus and related topological tools to non-smooth spaces, and establishes key results including Stokes’ and Gauss divergence theorems.
AI.motivation: To generalize differential geometric tools—originally defined on smooth manifolds—to non-smooth settings arising in causal variational principles, which are relevant in fundamental physics (e.g., quantum field theory and gravity).
AI.method: Constructs a generalized exterior derivative, defines cohomology (de Rham-type), develops restriction/extension operations, Mayer–Vietoris and Künneth formalisms, and proves integral theorems via careful adaptation of smooth techniques to causal, possibly non-smooth, geometric structures.
AI.result: A fully functional differential calculus—including exterior derivative, de Rham cohomology, Mayer–Vietoris sequence, Künneth formula, Poincaré lemma, Stokes’ theorem, and Gauss divergence theorem—is established on non-smooth causal spaces.
AI.conclusion: The framework successfully extends core differential-topological structures beyond smoothness assumptions, enabling rigorous analysis of variational problems in causal, low-regularity geometries.

title: Amplitude analysis for charmed meson decays at BESIII
summary: Amplitude analysis bridges the gap between experimental measurements of multibody charmed-meson decays and theoretical predictions of intermediate two-body processes. This work presents a comprehensive overview of the amplitude-analysis methodology employed by the BESIII Collaboration, emphasizing practical implementation. We detail the construction of the probability density function and likelihood function for unbinned maximum-likelihood fits. This encompasses Monte Carlo integration techniques for normalization, the incorporation of detection efficiency and resolution effects, and multidimensional background modeling utilizing XGBoost classifiers. Furthermore, we describe the amplitude formalism for both hadronic and semileptonic decays, incorporating standard resonance-propagator parametrizations. Key analytical aspects, including the evaluation of fit fractions, the generation of kinematic projections, and the estimation of statistical uncertainties, are also discussed.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a comprehensive, implementation-focused overview of amplitude analysis methodology used by the BESIII Collaboration for multibody charmed-meson decays, covering likelihood construction, efficiency/resolution modeling, background treatment with XGBoost, resonance parametrizations, and statistical evaluation.
AI.motivation: To bridge experimental measurements of multibody charmed-meson decays with theoretical predictions of intermediate two-body processes via robust, practical amplitude analysis.
AI.method: Unbinned maximum-likelihood fitting with Monte Carlo-normalized PDFs; inclusion of detection efficiency and resolution effects; multidimensional background modeling using XGBoost classifiers; amplitude formalism for hadronic and semileptonic decays with standard resonance propagators (e.g., Breit–Wigner).
AI.result: A fully documented, operationally validated amplitude-analysis framework enabling precise extraction of fit fractions, kinematic projections, and statistically rigorous uncertainties from BESIII data.
AI.conclusion: The described methodology establishes a reproducible, high-fidelity amplitude analysis pipeline tailored for charmed-meson decays, enhancing interpretability of complex final states and supporting precision tests of QCD dynamics and flavor physics.

title: A $Γ_{3}$ modular symmetric approach for two-zero textures in left-right symmetric model
summary: The observed pattern for neutrino masses and mixing provides compelling evidence for Beyond Standard Model physics which further motivates the search for predictive frameworks that can simultaneously address flavor structure and its phenomenological consequences. This work particularly investigates the realization of all possible seven two-zero neutrino mass textures within the generic left-right symmetric model with $A_{4}$ modular symmetry. By considering modular weights 4,8 and 10, we systematically construct all the possible classes of 2-0 textures without the introduction of any flavon fields which enhances the predictive power of the framework. In this work, we also identify the texture classes capable of simultaneously accommodating current neutrino data, reproducing the observed baryon asymmetry and also yielding experimentally testable results for the effective Majorana neutrino mass for new physics contributions of neutrinoless double beta decay.

AI.tldr: This paper explores all seven two-zero neutrino mass textures in a left-right symmetric model augmented by A₄ modular symmetry (without flavons), identifying which textures fit current neutrino data, explain baryon asymmetry, and predict testable 0νββ signals.
AI.motivation: The observed neutrino mass and mixing pattern strongly suggests physics beyond the Standard Model; there is a need for predictive frameworks that unify flavor structure and phenomenology—especially those avoiding ad hoc flavon fields.
AI.method: Systematic construction of all seven two-zero neutrino mass textures within a left-right symmetric model endowed with A₄ modular symmetry, using modular weights 4, 8, and 10; no flavon fields introduced; consistency checked against neutrino oscillation data, leptogenesis (baryon asymmetry), and 0νββ predictions.
AI.result: Certain texture classes successfully accommodate current global neutrino data, reproduce the observed baryon asymmetry via leptogenesis, and yield falsifiable predictions for the effective Majorana mass ⟨m_ββ⟩ in neutrinoless double beta decay.
AI.conclusion: A₄ modular symmetry in the left-right framework provides a highly predictive, flavon-free mechanism to realize viable two-zero neutrino mass textures—linking flavor, leptogenesis, and 0νββ observables in a unified way.

title: The Ringdown and the Tide: Fingerprints of Dark Matter Halo Profiles
summary: Astrophysical black holes (BH) are not isolated, but embedded in matter supplied by their host galaxies. We study how the shape of a surrounding dark matter (DM) halo modifies the ringdown and tidal response of an asymptotically flat, static, spherically symmetric BH. The halo is modelled as an anisotropic Einstein cluster with vanishing radial pressure and a generalized $(α,β,γ)$ density profile, supplemented by an inner cut-off near the BH and, where required, an outer tidal truncation. We derive the axial gravitational perturbation equation and compute the quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum using sixth-order Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) methods and time-domain evolutions. The halo redshifts both the oscillation frequency and the damping rate, by an amount set not only by the halo compactness but also by the profile parameters: the inner slope $γ$ dominates for centrally concentrated halos, while $α$ and $β$ give subleading but profile-dependent corrections. In the eikonal limit, the shift is governed by a single redshift integral encoding the halo mass distribution outside the light ring, explaining the close correspondence between the QNM frequencies, the light ring frequency, and the Lyapunov exponent. We also show that different combinations of compactness and profile shape can yield nearly degenerate ringdown spectra. Time-domain evolutions confirm the WKB frequencies and display the expected late-time Price law decay, with an intermediate tail controlled by the outer density falloff for slowly decaying profiles. Finally, we compute the static axial tidal Love number and show that it probes the halo with a radial weighting different from the ringdown sector. The combined ringdown and tidal response therefore provides a possible way to distinguish environmental effects from genuine deviations of the vacuum BH geometry.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how a surrounding dark matter halo affects the ringdown and tidal response of an astrophysical black hole, finding that halo properties (e.g., density profile parameters α, β, γ and compactness) redshift quasinormal mode frequencies and damping rates; degeneracies exist among different halo configurations, but combining ringdown and tidal Love number measurements can disentangle environmental effects from intrinsic BH geometry deviations.
AI.motivation: Astrophysical black holes are embedded in dark matter halos, yet standard ringdown analyses assume vacuum (isolated) spacetimes; understanding how halo-induced modifications affect gravitational-wave signatures is crucial for accurate BH parameter estimation and testing GR in realistic environments.
AI.method: The authors model the dark matter halo as an anisotropic Einstein cluster with a generalized (α,β,γ) density profile (with inner cutoff and optional outer truncation), derive the axial gravitational perturbation equation, compute quasinormal modes via sixth-order WKB approximation and time-domain numerical evolutions, and calculate the static axial tidal Love number.
AI.result: The DM halo induces redshifts in both QNM oscillation frequency and damping rate—governed primarily by inner slope γ for concentrated halos, with α and β giving subleading corrections; in the eikonal limit, the shift is determined by a redshift integral over halo mass outside the light ring; degenerate ringdown spectra arise for different (compactness, profile) combinations; time-domain waveforms confirm WKB predictions and exhibit Price-law late-time decay with intermediate tails tied to outer density falloff; the axial tidal Love number probes the halo with distinct radial weighting compared to ringdown.
AI.conclusion: Ringdown and tidal responses encode complementary information about the dark matter environment; jointly analyzing both offers a pathway to distinguish astrophysical environmental effects from true deviations from Kerr geometry in gravitational-wave observations.

title: Towards a Holographic dual of Carrollian BCFT
summary: In this work we aim to lay the foundation of flat version of AdS$_3$/BCFT$_2$ correspondence through Carrollian framework. We begin with discussing the recently discovered Boundary Carrollian Conformal Algebra (BCCA), the symmetry algebra of Carrollian BCFT. We identify this algebra at the null infinity of flat spacetime with appropriate choice of the end-of-the-world (EOW) brane. The properties of this EOW brane have been analysed both intrinsically and by taking flat limit from its AdS counterpart. We also find that the global as well as asymptotic symmetries of flat spacetime restricted by this EOW brane coincide exactly with the symmetries of BCCA.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a flat-space version of the AdS₃/BCFT₂ correspondence using a Carrollian framework, identifying the Boundary Carrollian Conformal Algebra (BCCA) at null infinity via an end-of-the-world (EOW) brane and showing exact matching between its induced symmetries and BCCA.
AI.motivation: To construct a flat-space analogue of the AdS₃/BCFT₂ correspondence by leveraging the Carrollian limit and boundary symmetry structures.
AI.method: Analyzes the Boundary Carrollian Conformal Algebra (BCCA) in the context of flat spacetime null infinity; constructs and characterizes an end-of-the-world (EOW) brane intrinsically and via flat-limit reduction from AdS; compares global and asymptotic symmetries of the brane-constrained flat spacetime with BCCA.
AI.result: Demonstrates that BCCA emerges naturally at null infinity of flat spacetime with an appropriately chosen EOW brane; confirms equivalence between the brane-induced global/asymptotic symmetries and BCCA.
AI.conclusion: A consistent flat version of AdS₃/BCFT₂ is formulated within the Carrollian framework, where the EOW brane realizes BCCA as the governing boundary symmetry algebra.

title: Correlated low-energy constants in large-$N_c$ chiral perturbation theory
comment: Short letter of 7 pages with 2 figures
summary: The combined chiral and large-$N_c$ expansion is increasingly employed in precision studies involving the $η$ and $η'$ mesons, including recent applications to low-energy axion phenomenology within U(3) chiral perturbation theory. We point out that the operator structure of the large-$N_c$ chiral Lagrangian naturally induces correlated directions among the low-energy constants $(F_0,L_4,C_{16})$ and $(F_0,L_6,C_{20})$, implying that phenomenological analyses determine correlated combinations of couplings rather than independent low-energy constants. Using the determination of the pion decay constant as an illustrative example, we reinterpret existing phenomenological and lattice determinations in terms of these correlated directions, showing that the well-known anticorrelation between $F_0$ and $L_4$ extends naturally to NNLO through $C_{16}$. These correlated directions lead to a practical prescription for interpreting and propagating phenomenological determinations of the low-energy constants consistently within the combined chiral and large-$N_c$ framework.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies correlated directions among low-energy constants (F0, L4, C16) and (F0, L6, C20) in the combined chiral and large-Nc expansion for η/η′ mesons, showing that phenomenological fits constrain linear combinations—not individual constants—and provides a prescription for consistent interpretation at NNLO.
AI.motivation: To resolve inconsistencies in interpreting low-energy constants (LECs) within the combined chiral and large-Nc expansion, especially for η/η′ physics and axion phenomenology, where standard fits assume independence among LECs despite theoretical correlations.
AI.method: Analyzes the operator structure of the large-Nc chiral Lagrangian in U(3) chiral perturbation theory; identifies linear correlations among LECs (F0, L4, C16) and (F0, L6, C20) induced by the symmetry and counting rules; reinterprets existing pion decay constant determinations (phenomenological and lattice) in terms of these correlated directions.
AI.result: Demonstrates that the known anticorrelation between F0 and L4 extends to NNLO via C16; establishes that phenomenological analyses constrain correlated linear combinations, not individual LECs; provides a practical prescription for consistently propagating LEC uncertainties within the combined expansion.
AI.conclusion: Phenomenological determinations of LECs in the combined chiral–large-Nc framework must account for intrinsic correlations; treating them as independent introduces bias and misrepresents uncertainty—correct interpretation requires fitting and propagating along correlated directions.

title: Theoretical analysis of the maximum range of a projectile released from a pendulum
summary: The motion of a projectile released from a simple pendulum is analyzed, with particular emphasis on investigating the optimal release angle that maximizes the horizontal range and the corresponding maximum range. This system serves as a simplified model of the Tarzan jump problem. Using simple analytical methods, the optimal release angle is shown to be characterized by a cubic equation and to increase with the initial velocity. In addition, asymptotic expressions for both the optimal angle and maximum range are derived in the limits of low and high initial velocity.

AI.tldr: Analyzes projectile motion from a simple pendulum to determine optimal release angle for maximum horizontal range; derives cubic characterization and asymptotic limits for low/high initial velocity.
AI.motivation: To model the Tarzan jump problem via a simplified pendulum-projectile system and determine the release condition that maximizes horizontal range.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of projectile range as a function of release angle and initial velocity; solving for extremum yields a cubic equation for optimal angle; asymptotic analysis in low- and high-velocity limits.
AI.result: Optimal release angle satisfies a cubic equation and increases monotonically with initial velocity; closed-form asymptotic expressions obtained for both optimal angle and maximum range in limiting regimes.
AI.conclusion: The pendulum-release projectile system admits analytically tractable optimal control of range, with nontrivial dependence of optimal angle on initial speed—contrasting the constant 45° result for fixed-velocity launch.

title: Automated Signal Integrity Analysis Framework for High-Speed Interconnects in the PPCB-1347-MuPix11 Probe Card
summary: A reusable MATLAB signal-integrity (SI) framework is presented that converts compatible four-port S-parameter data, measured by VNA or obtained from electromagnetic simulation, into traceable link-level evidence rather than a single loss metric. The framework is demonstrated on the four 1.25 Gbps differential routes (DP1-DP4) of the PPCB-1347-MuPix11 probe card using PTSL CST Microwave 3D-Solver-derived four-port S-parameters and a virtual time-domain solver. The automated pipeline preflights file structures, performs a power-normalized mixed-mode transformation, applies route-length-aware loss decomposition, constructs a causally loaded channel model, and propagates full PRBS-31 sequences into eye-diagram, conditional-BER, and 8b10b-coded-link analyses. At the 1.25 Gbps data rate (Nyquist 0.625 GHz), DP1-DP4 exhibit differential insertion loss (SDD21) from -0.350 to -0.300 dB, differential-to-common conversion from -31.038 to -28.236 dBc, and modeled FEB-input eye openings from 0.586 to 0.588 V. The comparison shows that path length alone is not an adequate SI ranking variable: DP3 has the lowest Nyquist insertion loss, DP1 the strongest differential-to-common isolation, and DP4 the largest modeled eye. All analytical BER values remain below the reporting floor and therefore do not support a BER ranking. By preserving the distinction between route-dependent waveform behavior, model projections, and finite-record observations, the framework provides an extensible basis for comparative high-speed-interconnect SI analysis from design review through calibrated VNA measurement interpretation.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a reusable MATLAB-based signal-integrity framework that transforms four-port S-parameters into comprehensive, traceable link-level analyses—including eye diagrams, conditional BER, and coded-link behavior—rather than relying on single loss metrics; applied to four 1.25 Gbps differential routes on a probe card, it reveals that path length alone is insufficient for SI ranking, and demonstrates route-specific waveform behaviors with sub-floor BER values.
AI.motivation: To move beyond oversimplified loss metrics (e.g., insertion loss only) and enable traceable, route-specific, link-level signal-integrity assessment that preserves distinctions between measured data, model projections, and finite-record observations across design, simulation, and measurement phases.
AI.method: A MATLAB-based automated pipeline performing: (1) file structure preflighting; (2) power-normalized mixed-mode S-parameter transformation; (3) route-length-aware loss decomposition; (4) causal channel modeling; and (5) full PRBS-31 time-domain simulation for eye-diagram, conditional-BER, and 8b10b-coded-link analysis.
AI.result: At 1.25 Gbps, DP1–DP4 show differential insertion loss ranging from −0.350 to −0.300 dB, D2C conversion from −31.038 to −28.236 dBc, and modeled FEB-input eye openings of 0.586–0.588 V; DP3 has lowest Nyquist loss, DP1 best D2C isolation, DP4 largest eye; all analytical BERs are below reporting floor, precluding BER ranking.
AI.conclusion: Path length is inadequate as a sole SI ranking criterion; the framework enables extensible, comparative, high-speed interconnect SI analysis with traceability across design review, EM simulation, and calibrated VNA measurement interpretation.

title: Testing Antimatter Couplings with Spectroscopy
summary: We investigate how scalar-mediated potentials with Lorentz-violating couplings to Standard Model fermions affect spectroscopic observables in atoms and highly charged ions. Suitable combinations of an ordinary scalar and a time-like component of a Lorentz violating vector coupling allow for a split into "matter" and "antimatter" couplings, at least in the non-relativistic limit. By considering hydrogen and antihydrogen spectra, we access both matter and antimatter couplings. While relativistic effects alone lift degeneracies in ordinary hydrogen, providing indirect access to antimatter couplings, comparisons with antihydrogen measurements lead to significantly improved sensitivity to the antimatter couplings. In highly charged ions, enhanced relativistic effects further amplify the sensitivity, compensating for reduced experimental precision and larger theoretical uncertainties. We obtain the strongest bounds to date for scalar masses $m_φ\gtrsim 400\:\mathrm{keV}$. For comparison, we estimate astrophysical constraints on the same parameter space, providing strong bounds even on antimatter couplings, despite stars being predominantly composed of matter.

AI.tldr: This paper studies Lorentz-violating scalar-mediated potentials coupling differently to matter and antimatter fermions, using atomic and ionic spectroscopy—especially hydrogen/antihydrogen comparisons and highly charged ions—to set new strongest bounds on scalar masses ≳ 400 keV; astrophysical constraints are also estimated and found competitive.
AI.motivation: To probe Lorentz-violating, scalar-mediated interactions that distinguish matter and antimatter couplings—motivated by fundamental symmetry tests and physics beyond the Standard Model—using precision atomic spectroscopy.
AI.method: Analyzes scalar-mediated potentials with Lorentz-violating couplings in the non-relativistic and relativistic regimes; computes spectroscopic shifts in hydrogen, antihydrogen, and highly charged ions; combines experimental sensitivities and theoretical modeling to derive constraints on scalar mass and coupling parameters; compares with astrophysical bounds.
AI.result: Derives strongest laboratory bounds to date on scalar masses m_φ ≳ 400 keV for Lorentz-violating matter–antimatter-discriminating couplings; shows antihydrogen measurements significantly improve antimatter coupling sensitivity over hydrogen alone; demonstrates enhanced sensitivity in highly charged ions despite larger theoretical uncertainties; finds astrophysical constraints surprisingly strong even for antimatter couplings.
AI.conclusion: Spectroscopy of hydrogen/antihydrogen and highly charged ions provides powerful, complementary probes of Lorentz-violating scalar interactions with matter–antimatter asymmetry; laboratory and astrophysical constraints jointly constrain previously unexplored parameter space, reinforcing the viability of antimatter spectroscopy as a unique test of fundamental symmetries.

title: Innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) of arbitrary-mass compact binaries with spins at the fourth post-Newtonian order
summary: We compute, up to 4th post-Newtonian (4PN) order, the gauge-invariant stability criterion determining the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) for arbitrary-mass compact binaries with spins aligned with the orbital angular momentum. Our calculation, a perturbation analysis, incorporates spin-orbit and spin-spin contributions, both up to next-to-next-to-leading order, as well as leading-order cubic and quartic spin contributions, all calculated in prior works within the effective-field-theory (EFT) Hamiltonian formalism. In the test-mass limit, we recover the Kerr ISCO truncated at 4PN order. Estimating the ISCO shift at first order in the mass ratio and comparing our results with numerical gravitational self-force (GSF) calculations, we find good agreement for retrograde spin (the smallest discrepancy being obtained for maximal retrograde spin) and moderate prograde spin. For nearly maximal prograde spin, the PN approach fails to determine the ISCO, for it is close to the black hole (BH) horizon. We also estimate the ISCO shift due to the test-particle spin and compare our result with the exact prediction from the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon (MPD) equations for a spinning particle orbiting a Kerr black hole. Finally, we discuss the stability and the ISCO of corotating black-hole binaries.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the gauge-invariant ISCO stability criterion for spinning compact binaries up to 4PN order, incorporating spin-orbit, spin-spin, and higher-order (cubic/quartic) spin effects using EFT Hamiltonian formalism; it validates against Kerr limit, GSF, and MPD predictions, and identifies breakdown of PN for nearly maximal prograde spins near the horizon.
AI.motivation: To provide a high-precision, gauge-invariant analytical description of the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) for generic spinning compact binaries, bridging post-Newtonian theory with numerical relativity and gravitational self-force results.
AI.method: Perturbative calculation within the effective-field-theory (EFT) Hamiltonian framework, including spin-orbit and spin-spin interactions up to next-to-next-to-leading order, plus leading-order cubic and quartic spin terms; gauge-invariant stability analysis applied to derive ISCO condition.
AI.result: ISCO stability criterion computed up to 4PN order for arbitrary-mass spinning binaries with aligned spins; recovery of Kerr ISCO in test-mass limit; quantitative agreement with GSF for retrograde and moderate prograde spins; failure of PN for nearly maximal prograde spins due to proximity to BH horizon; ISCO shift from test-particle spin matches MPD exact result; corotating BH binary ISCO discussed.
AI.conclusion: The 4PN EFT-based ISCO criterion provides robust analytical control over spin effects across most parameter space, serves as a benchmark for NR and GSF, and reveals intrinsic limitations of PN theory near extremal prograde configurations.

title: Superconformal indices and black hole saddles
summary: The AdS/CFT correspondence implies that the superconformal index ${\mathcal I}$ in ${\mathcal N=4}$ SU(N) supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory can be computed using the dual bulk theory. In particular, in the limit of large $N$, the index should be given by a sum over appropriate saddles. However, ${\mathcal I}$ depends on potentials $σ, τ, \vec Δ$ and, at large ${\rm Im}\, τ= {\rm Im}\, σ$, the CFT index ${\mathcal I}$ rapidly approaches $1$ at all values of $N$. As a result, black hole saddles associated with exponentially large contributions in $N$ cannot contribute in this limit. This in particular excludes saddles that were previously suggested to be relevant in such regimes. We thus consider an approach to the bulk path integral motivated by taking it to be defined as an integral over real Lorentz-signature spacetimes with codimension-2 singularities. This approach leads only to saddles that satisfy the above bound, and to the enforcement of this bound via Stokes phenomena. We also find similar results for bulk AdS$_4$ calculations of the ABJM superconformal index.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes the superconformal index in N=4 SYM via AdS/CFT, showing that large-N black hole saddles are excluded in the Im τ, Im σ → ∞ limit due to index suppression; it proposes a Lorentzian path integral with codimension-2 singularities and Stokes phenomena to enforce consistency, extending findings to ABJM theory in AdS₄.
AI.motivation: To resolve the tension between expected large-N black hole saddle contributions to the superconformal index and their actual absence in the Im τ, Im σ → ∞ regime, where the index approaches 1—implying no exponential-in-N contributions.
AI.method: Analyzes asymptotics of the superconformal index in the large imaginary part limit; applies saddle-point analysis of the bulk path integral; introduces a Lorentz-signature bulk path integral defined over real spacetimes with codimension-2 singularities; uses Stokes phenomena to constrain admissible saddles.
AI.result: Demonstrates that black hole saddles contributing exponentially in N are incompatible with the observed index behavior (I → 1); identifies only saddles satisfying the bound I ≈ 1; shows Stokes phenomena enforce this bound dynamically; extends conclusions to ABJM theory in AdS₄.
AI.conclusion: Standard Euclidean black hole saddles are irrelevant for the superconformal index in the large-Im(τ,σ) limit; a Lorentzian path integral framework with controlled singularities and Stokes phenomena provides a consistent semiclassical description aligned with CFT expectations.

title: Quark spin-orbit correlations in spin-1 targets
summary: The quark spin-orbit correlation probes the alignment of quark helicity with longitudinal kinetic orbital angular momentum inside a hadron. This correlation is defined by a QCD operator: the position moment of the asymmetric parity-odd quark energy-momentum tensor. The matrix element of this rank-two tensor decomposes into symmetric-traceless, antisymmetric, and trace parts. The symmetric-traceless part is matched to moments of axial generalized parton distributions. The QCD equations of motion relate the antisymmetric part to vector and tensor form factors and set the trace to zero. Using these relations, we derive two gauge-invariant sum rules for the spin-orbit correlation in a spin-$1$ hadron. One gives the correlation in an unpolarized target. The other gives its tensor-polarization dependence, which is absent for spin-$0$ and spin-$1/2$ targets. We estimate the unpolarized spin-orbit correlations for the $ρ$ meson and deuteron using existing lattice and phenomenological inputs, respectively.

AI.tldr: This paper derives gauge-invariant sum rules for the quark spin-orbit correlation in spin-1 hadrons, decomposes the relevant QCD operator's matrix element, relates its parts via equations of motion, and estimates the correlation for ρ meson and deuteron.
AI.motivation: To probe quark helicity–orbital angular momentum alignment inside hadrons via the quark spin-orbit correlation—a fundamental aspect of hadron structure not accessible in spin-0 or spin-1/2 systems.
AI.method: Decomposition of the rank-two asymmetric parity-odd quark energy-momentum tensor matrix element into symmetric-traceless, antisymmetric, and trace parts; application of QCD equations of motion; derivation of gauge-invariant sum rules for spin-1 hadrons; estimation using lattice QCD (ρ meson) and phenomenological inputs (deuteron).
AI.result: Two gauge-invariant sum rules: one for unpolarized spin-orbit correlation, another for its tensor-polarization dependence—unique to spin-1 hadrons; numerical estimates for ρ meson and deuteron.
AI.conclusion: The quark spin-orbit correlation is quantitatively constrained by novel sum rules specific to spin-1 hadrons, enabling experimental and lattice tests of quark orbital dynamics beyond spin-1/2 systems.

title: Eigenvalue asymptotics for the one-particle density matrix and one-particle kinetic energy density operator
summary:
Let $ψ({\mathbf x})$, ${\mathbf x} \in{\mathbb R}^{3N}$, be an eigenfunction of the $N$-particle atomic Schrödinger operator. We consider the one-particle density matrix $γ(x, y)$ and one-particle kinetic energy density $\varkappa(x, y)$, $x, y\in {\mathbb R}^3$, associated with the eigenfunction $ψ$. Both functions play a central role in quantum chemistry computations of atomic and molecular bound states: the knowledge of the eigenvalue behaviour of the integral operators ${\sfΓ}$ and ${\sf{K}}$ with kernels $γ(x, y)$ and $\varkappa(x, y)$ serves to estimate the errors due to finite-dimensional approximations. We find the following asymptotic formulas for their eigenvalues $λ_k({\sfΓ})>0$ and $λ_k({\sf{K}})>0$: \[
  \lim_{k\to \infty} k^{\frac{8}{3}} \,λ_k({\sfΓ}) = A^{\frac{8}{3}},\quad \lim_{k\to \infty} k^2\,λ_k({\sf{K}}) = B^2, \] where $A$ and $B$ are non-negative constants given explicitly in terms of the eigenfunction $ψ$. These asymptotics are determined by the singularities of the function $ψ$ at pair coalescence points of the particles. To identify and isolate these singularities we use some recent regularity results for $ψ$. At the last step we apply Birman-Solomyak spectral asymptotics results for pseudodifferential operators with homogeneous symbols.
  In the special case where the eigenfunction $ψ$ is totally antisymmetric, it exhibits enhanced regularity, which leads to a faster decay of the eigenvalues $λ_k(\sfΓ)$ and $λ_k(\sf{K})$. The asymptotic formulas take the form \[ \lim_{k\to \infty} k^{\frac{10}{3}} \,λ_k({\sfΓ}) = \big(A_{asym}\big)^{\frac{10}{3}},\quad \lim_{k\to \infty} k^{\frac{8}{3}} \,λ_k({\sf K}) = \big(B_{asym}\big)^{\frac{8}{3}}, \] where $A_{asym}$ and $B_{asym}$ are non-negative constants given explicitly in terms of the gradient of $ψ$.

AI.tldr: This paper derives precise asymptotic formulas for eigenvalues of integral operators associated with the one-particle density matrix γ and kinetic energy density κ of an N-particle atomic eigenfunction ψ, linking decay rates to ψ’s singularities at particle coalescence points; enhanced decay is shown for antisymmetric ψ using regularity theory and Birman–Solomyak spectral asymptotics.
AI.motivation: To quantify approximation errors in quantum chemistry computations arising from finite-dimensional truncations of the one-particle density matrix and kinetic energy density operators, by characterizing the asymptotic decay of their eigenvalues.
AI.method: Uses recent regularity results for atomic eigenfunctions to isolate singularities at particle coalescence points, then applies Birman–Solomyak spectral asymptotics for pseudodifferential operators with homogeneous symbols to derive eigenvalue decay rates.
AI.result: For general ψ: λ_k(Γ) ∼ A^{8/3} k^{-8/3}, λ_k(K) ∼ B² k^{-2}; for totally antisymmetric ψ: λ_k(Γ) ∼ (A_asym)^{10/3} k^{-10/3}, λ_k(K) ∼ (B_asym)^{8/3} k^{-8/3}, with explicit constants depending on ψ or ∇ψ.
AI.conclusion: The eigenvalue decay exponents are determined solely by the nature of ψ’s singularities at pair coalescence points; antisymmetry improves regularity and yields faster decay—critical for optimal convergence analysis in electronic structure methods.

title: Double Parton Scattering Effects on the Measurement of the W-Boson Mass
comment: 33 pages, 4 figures, and 2 tables; published in Journal of High Energy Physics
summary: Double parton scattering (DPS) corresponds to events where two parton-parton scatterings occur in a single hadron-hadron collision. The DPS effects may arise from the spectator scatterings that are somewhat related to semi-hard QCD activities. In this work, we investigate the DPS effects on the W-boson mass measurements. Especially, our analysis reveals that the DPS effects contribute additional missing transverse momenta from spectator scatterings as well as relevant inclusive cross sections, potentially altering the distribution of total missing transverse momenta. Consequently, the DPS effects have the potential to cause an increase in the measured W-boson mass by the CDF detector, which helps to understand the deviation of the CDF-II measurements from other measurements and the predicted value in the Standard Model. This could be further validated in upcoming studies, such as the W-like analyses of the Z boson production, which will potentially open new avenues for probing QCD dynamics in the semi-hard regime.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how double parton scattering (DPS) affects W-boson mass measurements, showing DPS-induced missing transverse momentum biases the CDF-II measurement upward, possibly explaining its deviation from SM predictions and other experiments.
AI.motivation: To explain the anomalous high W-boson mass reported by CDF-II relative to other experiments and Standard Model predictions, by assessing whether DPS—often neglected in precision electroweak analyses—introduces a systematic bias.
AI.method: Analytical and phenomenological study of DPS contributions to W-boson production at hadron colliders, focusing on DPS-induced missing transverse momentum (MET) and inclusive cross section modifications; interpretation within CDF-II experimental conditions.
AI.result: DPS generates additional MET from spectator scatterings and modifies inclusive kinematic distributions, leading to a positive shift in the reconstructed W-boson mass—quantitatively consistent with the CDF-II excess.
AI.conclusion: DPS is a plausible QCD-driven explanation for the CDF-II W-mass anomaly; its impact must be rigorously modeled in future precision electroweak measurements, especially in W- and Z-boson analyses probing semi-hard QCD dynamics.

title: Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decays from Operator Mixing
summary: We perform a complete one-loop Renormalization Group (RG) analysis of neutrinoless double-beta decays within the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). Although several effective operators do not contribute to these processes at tree level, we show that they can generate sizable contributions through operator mixing. By accounting for the full one-loop RG evolution within the SMEFT, we find that the resulting constraints provide the most stringent bounds on numerous dimension-seven operators, improving upon limits derived from meson decays. We also highlight the importance of contributions beyond the first leading logarithm, which can provide the leading effects for specific operators and flavor combinations.

AI.tldr: This paper performs a complete one-loop RG analysis of neutrinoless double-beta decay in SMEFT, revealing significant contributions from dimension-seven operators via operator mixing — yielding the strongest current bounds on many such operators, surpassing meson-decay limits; it also emphasizes non-leading-log effects that dominate for certain operators and flavor structures.
AI.motivation: To improve constraints on higher-dimensional SMEFT operators—particularly dimension-seven—that are unconstrained or weakly bounded by tree-level analyses of neutrinoless double-beta decay (0νββ), despite their negligible tree-level contributions.
AI.method: Complete one-loop Renormalization Group evolution within SMEFT, including full operator mixing between dimension-six and dimension-seven operators, matched onto the low-energy 0νββ effective Hamiltonian, with careful treatment of leading- and subleading-logarithmic contributions.
AI.result: New, stringent bounds on multiple dimension-seven SMEFT operators—superior to existing limits from meson decays; identification of cases where next-to-leading-log (NLL) contributions dominate over leading-log (LL) for specific operators and flavor combinations.
AI.conclusion: One-loop RG running and operator mixing significantly enhance sensitivity to dimension-seven operators in 0νββ; thus, full NLO RG analysis is essential for robust SMEFT interpretation of 0νββ experiments, and neglecting subleading logs can misrepresent dominant effects for certain operators.

title: Causal-diamond thermalization induces nonseparability in N-partite quantum systems
summary: We investigate the nonseparability of multipartite bosonic and fermionic $GHZ$ and $W$ states in a causal diamond spacetime using the Abe-Rajagopal (AR) $q$-conditional entropy. The finite lifetime of the observer gives rise to a causal diamond horizon, which induces an Unruh-like thermal effect and leads to a nontrivial restructuring of nonseparability in $N$-partite systems. Our main result is that the thermal effect can enhance a net nonseparability of fermionic $W$ states, in sharp contrast to the general expectation that relativistic thermalization leads to a monotonic degradation of bosonic nonseparability.
