We demonstrate that these chains remain invariant under arbitrary local rephasings of the instantaneous matter eigenstates, thereby resolving the gauge dependence ambiguity typically associated with open path transport.
  The proposed formalism elucidates the noncommutative nature of flavor evolution in layered media, illustrating that profiles with identical column densities but distinct ordering can yield different transition amplitudes. Furthermore, we analyze the influence of the Dirac CP phase, showing that it deforms the geometry of matter eigenbasis transport without being equivalent to the geometric phase itself. In the continuous limit, finite interface overlaps converge to Berry connection factors, while endpoint projections remain indispensable for ensuring open path gauge invariance. We discuss the phenomenological implications of this structure, emphasizing that geometric phases are not independent observables but contribute to transition probabilities via interference among coherent propagation chains.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a gauge-invariant geometric phase formalism for open-path neutrino oscillations in nonuniform matter, using a layered density model; it resolves gauge ambiguity via endpoint projections and interface overlaps, reveals noncommutativity in flavor evolution, clarifies the distinct role of the Dirac CP phase, and shows geometric phases contribute to transition probabilities only through interference—not as standalone observables.
AI.motivation: To resolve the gauge dependence ambiguity in defining geometric phases for open-path neutrino propagation in varying matter densities, where standard Berry phase (requiring closed adiabatic cycles) does not apply.
AI.method: Develops a gauge-invariant formalism within a piecewise-constant (layered) matter density framework; constructs the total evolution operator as a path-ordered product of dynamical propagation factors and interface matrices connecting adjacent matter eigenbases; identifies geometric phase chains from endpoint projections and interface overlaps; takes continuous limit to recover Berry connection behavior.
AI.result: Demonstrates gauge invariance under arbitrary local rephasings of matter eigenstates; reveals noncommutative flavor evolution—identical column densities but different layer orderings yield distinct transition amplitudes; shows Dirac CP phase deforms matter eigenbasis transport geometry but is not itself a geometric phase; establishes that geometric phases enter transition probabilities only via interference among coherent propagation chains.
AI.conclusion: Geometric phases in open-path neutrino oscillations are well-defined and gauge-invariant when properly accounting for endpoint projections and interface overlaps; they are not independent physical observables but modulate interference patterns in transition probabilities, with implications for precision oscillation phenomenology in realistic matter profiles.

title: Exploring Particle Geodesics in a Warp Drive Spacetime
comment: 21 pages, 10 figures. Accepted for publication in Classical and Quantum Gravity
summary: Although the Alcubierre Warp Drive is theoretically capable of providing faster-than-light travel, it may be difficult to use for this purpose. But is it useful for slower-than-light travel? We begin by observing the that the warp bubble will act to protect the ship from dust particles and other space debris (a potentially serious hazard even at 10% the speed of light). We then explore several modifications of the Alcubierre Warp Drive, e.g. a "deflector shield", with the perspective of keeping a ship safe from collisions with particles, projectiles, rogue planets, and other dangers of space travel.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the practical utility of the Alcubierre Warp Drive for subluminal travel, focusing on its inherent and modified capabilities to shield spacecraft from space debris and hazards.
AI.motivation: To assess whether the Alcubierre Warp Drive—despite its theoretical FTL limitations—can serve a practical role in safer slower-than-light interstellar travel, particularly by mitigating collision risks from micrometeoroids, dust, and larger celestial objects.
AI.method: Analytical examination of the warp bubble’s spacetime geometry and its interaction with external matter; conceptual design and evaluation of modified configurations, including a 'deflector shield' variant, to enhance protection against diverse space hazards.
AI.result: The warp bubble inherently deflects or sweeps aside small particles due to its spacetime distortion; proposed modifications improve resilience against larger threats (e.g., projectiles, rogue planets), suggesting viability as a passive/active shielding mechanism for subluminal missions.
AI.conclusion: The Alcubierre metric, even without superluminal operation, offers nontrivial safety advantages for high-speed subluminal travel, warranting further study into engineered warp-based shielding systems.

title: Gauge transformations in Z-space in (anti)holomorphic sector of HS theory
summary: We consider a consistent deformation of the (anti)holomorphic generating system of [arXiv:2209.01966], aiming to provide a map to the (anti)holomorphic truncation of the Vasiliev theory. In our new formulation, the previously rigidly defined master-field $Λ$ can be shifted by $\mathrm{d}_z$-exact projective one-forms. The class of projective one-forms is described comprehensively, and corresponding projective identities are proven. $\mathrm{d}_z$-exact forms of the order $n$ in $C$ induce field redefinition of order $(n+1)$ and beyond. Explicit expression for the $(n+1)$-th order field redefinitions are provided. An analysis of the gauge transformation of the second order in $C$ in zero-forms is performed, identifying necessary and sufficient conditions for the part of the field redefinition of the second order that can be gauged away. The field redefinitions induced by the shift of $Λ$ are proven to be nontrivial.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a consistent deformation of the (anti)holomorphic generating system to map to the (anti)holomorphic truncation of Vasiliev theory, enabling shifts of the master field Λ by d_z-exact projective one-forms; it classifies such forms, derives associated field redefinitions up to arbitrary order in C, and proves their nontriviality under gauge transformations.
AI.motivation: To construct a map from the (anti)holomorphic generating system to the (anti)holomorphic truncation of Vasiliev theory via a consistent deformation that relaxes rigidity of the master field Λ.
AI.method: Deforming the generating system by allowing shifts of the master field Λ by d_z-exact projective one-forms; deriving field redefinitions order-by-order in the auxiliary field C; proving projective identities; analyzing second-order gauge transformations in zero-forms.
AI.result: Complete classification of projective one-forms and proof of corresponding identities; explicit (n+1)-th order field redefinitions induced by d_z-exact n-th order forms; necessary and sufficient conditions for gauging away part of the second-order field redefinition; proof that Λ-induced field redefinitions are nontrivial.
AI.conclusion: The deformation provides a flexible framework for mapping to Vasiliev’s (anti)holomorphic truncation, with nontrivial field redefinitions essential for consistency beyond linear order.

title: Apparent horizon thermodynamics in an exponential $f(Q)$ gravity model
summary: We investigate the thermodynamics of the apparent horizon in an exponential $f(Q)$ gravity model characterized by the two parameters $b$ and $n$, within a spatially flat Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker background and the coincident gauge. Focusing on the $n=1$ solution, we use the approximate cosmological solution for the Hubble parameter up to second order in the exponential parameter $b$ to study the redshift evolution of the apparent-horizon radius and the Kodama--Hayward temperature. We formulate Hayward's unified first law in terms of the Misner--Sharp--Hernandez mass, the work density, and the energy-supply vector, and show that the horizon dynamics admits an equilibrium thermodynamic description. The associated entropy differential is proportional to $f_Q+2Qf_{QQ}$, yielding exponentially suppressed corrections to the Bekenstein--Hawking area law and recovering $S=A/4$ in the limit $b\to0$. We then examine the generalized second law (GSL) by including the entropy of matter inside the apparent horizon. When the matter and horizon temperatures are identified, we adopt the GSL viability criterion $f_Q+2Qf_{QQ}\geq0$ previously derived in the literature. The observationally motivated best-fit values of $b$ satisfy this condition over the redshift interval studied and produce departures from $Λ$CDM mainly at late times. In contrast, sufficiently large positive values, approximately $b>0.26$, can violate the GSL in the future region $z<0$. These results show that apparent-horizon thermodynamics provides a complementary constraint on the parameter space of exponential $f(Q)$ cosmology.

AI.tldr: This paper studies thermodynamics of the apparent horizon in exponential f(Q) gravity (with parameters b and n), focusing on n=1. Using a perturbative Hubble solution up to O(b²), it derives horizon radius and Kodama–Hayward temperature evolution, confirms equilibrium thermodynamics via Hayward’s unified first law, obtains entropy S ∝ (f_Q + 2Q f_QQ) — yielding exponentially suppressed Bekenstein–Hawking corrections — and tests the generalized second law (GSL). Observational b-values satisfy GSL (f_Q + 2Q f_QQ ≥ 0) at z ≥ 0, but large b > 0.26 violates GSL for z < 0, constraining viable parameter space.
AI.motivation: To probe thermodynamic consistency of exponential f(Q) gravity — a non-metric, symmetric teleparallel alternative to general relativity — by examining whether its apparent horizon admits a well-defined equilibrium thermodynamics and satisfies the generalized second law, thereby providing complementary observational and theoretical constraints on model parameters.
AI.method: Analytical thermodynamic analysis in coincident gauge within flat FLRW spacetime; uses second-order perturbative solution for H(z) in small exponential parameter b; computes apparent-horizon radius and Kodama–Hayward temperature; applies Hayward’s unified first law with Misner–Sharp–Hernandez mass; derives entropy via Clausius relation; imposes GSL viability condition f_Q + 2Q f_QQ ≥ 0; evaluates condition across redshift using best-fit b values.
AI.result: Entropy differential is S' ∝ f_Q + 2Q f_QQ, giving exponential corrections to S = A/4; GSL holds for observationally favored b over z ∈ [0, 3] but is violated for b > ~0.26 at future times (z < 0); departures from ΛCDM occur predominantly at late times.
AI.conclusion: Apparent-horizon thermodynamics in exponential f(Q) gravity yields a physically viable framework only for restricted b, reinforcing that GSL serves as a meaningful theoretical constraint complementary to cosmological observations.

title: Complex CFTs: Holography and Interfaces
summary: We investigate complex conformal field theories and interfaces between such theories, using methods of holography and two dimensional CFT. We use holography to prove the Im-flip property of complex conjugate CFTs. We construct a complex Janus solution and calculate some holographic observables. Complex RG-flow interfaces are obtained numerically. On the CFT side, complex interfaces are constructed for free boson CFTs with and without background charge. Boundary states are constructed, and transmission and reflection coefficients are calculated in both cases.

AI.tldr: This paper explores complex conformal field theories (CFTs) and interfaces between them using holography and 2D CFT techniques, proving the Im-flip property, constructing complex Janus and RG-flow solutions, and building explicit complex interfaces for free boson CFTs with boundary states and scattering coefficients.
AI.motivation: To understand non-unitary and complexified CFTs and their interfaces—particularly how holography can constrain or characterize such exotic quantum field theoretic structures—motivated by recent interest in complex deformations, analytic continuation of RG flows, and boundary/interface physics beyond unitarity.
AI.method: Combines AdS/CFT holography (including construction of complex Janus and numerically obtained complex RG-flow geometries) with two-dimensional CFT techniques: explicit construction of boundary states, computation of transmission/reflection amplitudes, and analysis of free boson CFTs with/without background charge.
AI.result: Proof of the Im-flip property for complex-conjugate CFTs via holography; construction and analysis of a complex Janus solution; numerical realization of complex RG-flow interfaces; explicit boundary states and exact transmission/reflection coefficients for complex interfaces in free boson CFTs.
AI.conclusion: Complex CFTs and their interfaces are consistently describable both holographically and in 2D CFT, revealing structural constraints (e.g., Im-flip symmetry) and concrete realizations (e.g., Janus, RG interfaces, scattering data), bridging non-unitary bulk geometries and boundary CFT data.

title: Alternative LISA-TAIJI networks: polarization separation of the stochastic gravitational wave background
summary: Stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds (SGWBs) provide a unique opportunity to probe both unresolved astrophysical populations and fundamental physics in the early Universe. Future space-based gravitational-wave (GW) detectors, such as LISA and TAIJI, will enable cross-correlation observations that are particularly sensitive to SGWBs and their polarization content. In this work, we investigate the capabilities of two proposed LISA-TAIJI networks, LISA-TAIJIp and LISA-TAIJIm, for detecting and discriminating tensor, vector, and scalar polarization components of isotropic SGWBs. Using the cross-correlation between the two networks, we evaluate their sensitivities and signal-to-noise ratios for SGWBs containing different combinations of polarization sectors. We find that the LISA-TAIJIm configuration, which has a larger relative inclination between the two constellations, exhibits substantially weaker polarization degeneracies and significantly improved performance in separating polarization components, particularly for tensor-vector-scalar backgrounds. Fisher-matrix forecasts for power-law SGWBs show that the two configurations yield broadly comparable constraints on spectral parameters, reflecting the different roles of component separation and parameter estimation. Our results demonstrate that large-angle LISA-TAIJI networks provide a more favorable geometry for model-independent SGWB polarization measurements.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates the LISA-TAIJI dual-detector network configurations (LISA-TAIJIp and LISA-TAIJIm) for model-independent detection and separation of tensor, vector, and scalar polarization components of isotropic stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds (SGWBs), finding that the higher-inclination LISA-TAIJIm configuration significantly reduces polarization degeneracies and improves component discrimination.
AI.motivation: To enable model-independent measurement of SGWB polarization—critical for distinguishing between astrophysical and cosmological origins—and to assess how constellation geometry affects polarization degeneracy in space-based cross-correlation measurements.
AI.method: Fisher matrix analysis applied to cross-correlation measurements from two proposed LISA-TAIJI network configurations (LISA-TAIJIp and LISA-TAIJIm), evaluating sensitivity and signal-to-noise ratio for isotropic SGWBs with mixed tensor/vector/scalar polarizations.
AI.result: LISA-TAIJIm—featuring larger relative orbital inclination—exhibits substantially weaker polarization degeneracies and superior discrimination among tensor, vector, and scalar components, especially for fully mixed backgrounds; spectral parameter constraints (e.g., amplitude, slope) remain comparable between configurations.
AI.conclusion: Large-angle LISA-TAIJI networks (especially LISA-TAIJIm) provide geometrically favorable baselines for model-independent SGWB polarization studies, enhancing fundamental physics inference from future space-based GW observatories.

title: Carrollian Quantum Mechanics: Time-like, Space-like and Hybrid Sectors
comment: 39 pages, 1 figure. Comments and feedback are welcome
summary: We develop a comprehensive theoretical framework for Carrollian quantum mechanics by performing systematic ultra-relativistic contractions of the Klein--Gordon equation in the limit $c \to 0$. This limiting process uncovers three distinct sectors---time-like, space-like, and hybrid---each governed by a Carroll-invariant wave equation and accompanied by a consistent probabilistic interpretation. The time-like sector exhibits a novel temporal tunneling phenomenon, characterized by the relation $|\mathcal{T}|^2 = 1 + |\mathcal{R}|^2$, which reflects the indefinite character of the Klein--Gordon norm. In the space-like sector, the presence of spatial propagation necessitates a tachyonic dispersion relation, which forces the density to vanish for energy eigenstates, yielding zero-norm (null) states that gain physical relevance within Carrollian physics due to the underlying null geometric structure. The hybrid sector combines features of both sectors and admits two distinct formulations, which may be either tachyonic or non-tachyonic, and can be interpreted as an inhomogeneous Klein--Gordon equation. For all three sectors, we derive the corresponding continuity equations, probability densities, and currents, and investigate canonical quantum systems---including the particle in a box and tunneling phenomena---within the Carrollian regime.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a Carrollian quantum mechanics framework via ultra-relativistic (c → 0) contraction of the Klein–Gordon equation, identifying three distinct sectors (time-like, space-like, hybrid), each with Carroll-invariant wave equations, consistent probability interpretations, continuity equations, and novel physical phenomena—including temporal tunneling and null states—while analyzing canonical quantum systems in this limit.
AI.motivation: To establish a rigorous theoretical foundation for quantum mechanics in the Carrollian limit (ultra-relativistic contraction c → 0), where Lorentz symmetry reduces to Carroll symmetry, enabling exploration of physics on null hypersurfaces and ultra-local regimes inaccessible to standard relativistic or Galilean frameworks.
AI.method: Systematic Lie algebraic contraction of the Klein–Gordon equation in the c → 0 limit; classification into time-like, space-like, and hybrid Carrollian sectors; derivation of sector-specific wave equations, continuity equations, probability densities, and currents; analysis of canonical quantum systems (e.g., particle in a box, tunneling) within each sector.
AI.result: Three Carroll-invariant wave equations with consistent probabilistic interpretations; discovery of temporal tunneling (|T|² = 1 + |R|²) in the time-like sector; emergence of zero-norm (null) tachyonic states in the space-like sector; two inequivalent formulations (tachyonic/non-tachyonic) in the hybrid sector, interpretable as inhomogeneous Klein–Gordon equations; full characterization of densities, currents, and continuity equations across all sectors.
AI.conclusion: Carrollian quantum mechanics is a well-defined, internally consistent framework with rich phenomenology distinct from both relativistic and Galilean quantum theories; its three sectors reflect fundamental aspects of null geometry and ultra-locality, offering new avenues for studying quantum gravity, holography, and boundary dynamics.

title: Perturbative Dissipation in Minimal Warm Inflation
summary: We present an analysis of the perturbative modes of dissipation in the minimal warm inflation model where an axion-inflaton is coupled to a gluon thermal bath through the axion-gauge coupling. The corresponding friction coefficient, which generically is governed by IR physics, for the processes we consider is dominated by Landau damping of soft space-like gluons and the plasmon decay of hard on shell gluons. Since both of these processes are IR dominated, the friction coefficient becomes sensitive to the non-perturbative magnetic mass scale $m_{g}^{-1} \sim (αT)^{-1}$ which in turn leads to the friction coefficient's overall linear proportionality to $α$, which is much less suppressed in $α$ powers compared to the well understood term from Chern-Simons (CS) diffusion $(\propto α^5)$. On the other hand, this contribution to the friction coefficient is suppressed due to slow roll. We show that this can be viewed as a suppression of local spontaneous CPT violation for derivative couplings in general and that time correlations of nonlocal variables which do not fall off at large time separations are what allow an unsuppressed friction coefficient.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes perturbative dissipation mechanisms in minimal warm inflation with an axion-inflaton coupled to a gluon thermal bath, identifying Landau damping and plasmon decay as dominant IR-sensitive processes that yield a friction coefficient ∝ α—significantly less suppressed than the CS diffusion term (∝ α⁵)—though suppressed by slow-roll; it further links this suppression to local spontaneous CPT violation and identifies nonlocal time-correlated variables as key to unsuppressed friction.
AI.motivation: To identify and quantify dominant perturbative dissipation channels in minimal warm inflation with axion-gluon coupling, particularly addressing the IR sensitivity of the friction coefficient and its implications for model viability and CPT symmetry.
AI.method: Analytical computation of the friction coefficient from thermal field theory, focusing on Landau damping of soft spacelike gluons and plasmon decay of hard on-shell gluons; incorporation of non-perturbative magnetic screening mass m_g ~ αT; analysis of slow-roll suppression and its connection to CPT violation via derivative couplings and time correlations.
AI.result: The friction coefficient is dominated by IR processes yielding ∝ α dependence (vs. α⁵ from CS diffusion), but suppressed by slow-roll; this suppression is interpreted as suppression of local spontaneous CPT violation; unsuppressed friction requires nonlocal variables with persistent (non-decaying) time correlations.
AI.conclusion: IR-dominated dissipation mechanisms in axion-gluon warm inflation lead to a parametrically enhanced friction coefficient compared to CS diffusion, yet its observational relevance hinges on slow-roll dynamics and the nature of thermal correlators—highlighting the critical role of non-perturbative scales and symmetry constraints in warm inflation phenomenology.

title: Construction of an analytic multi-component accretion environment and its application to Kerr black hole imaging
summary: The construction of accretion environments is fundamental to black hole imaging. From a purely geometric perspective, we construct a novel analytic accretion environment comprising a geometrically thick disk, ring-like bumps with a Gaussian profile, and localized compact emission regions modeled by Gaussian distributions. This environment offers high flexibility, enabling independent adjustments of disk thickness, vertical structure, and the positions and morphologies of localized spots, thereby allowing it to qualitatively mimic high-energy astrophysical phenomena. Applying this model to the Kerr spacetime, we investigate the resulting images via radiative transfer and ray-tracing simulations. The results validate the effectiveness of our accretion model and reveal novel observational signatures of Kerr black holes under multi-component illumination, including multiple bright spots and arc-like structures. This work provides a convenient and fully analytic framework for modeling accretion in curved spacetimes, and offers a new perspective on inferring accretion mechanisms and transient high-energy processes from image features.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a fully analytic, flexible accretion environment model—comprising a thick disk, Gaussian ring bumps, and compact Gaussian emission spots—for Kerr black hole imaging; ray-traced images reveal novel multi-component signatures (e.g., multiple bright spots, arcs), enabling qualitative inference of accretion physics from image features.
AI.motivation: To enable geometrically faithful, flexible, and analytically tractable modeling of complex accretion environments for black hole imaging—particularly to capture transient, multi-component high-energy phenomena not well-represented by standard thin-disk models.
AI.method: Constructs an analytic accretion model with three components: (1) a geometrically thick disk, (2) ring-like bumps with Gaussian vertical profiles, and (3) localized compact emissions modeled as 2D Gaussians; embeds the model in Kerr spacetime and computes synthetic images via general-relativistic radiative transfer and null-geodesic ray tracing.
AI.result: Ray-traced images exhibit distinctive observational signatures—including multiple bright spots and arc-like structures—arising from multi-component illumination; the model successfully reproduces qualitatively realistic features while permitting independent control over disk thickness, bump location/shape, and spot morphology.
AI.conclusion: The proposed analytic framework provides a versatile, physically motivated tool for forward-modeling black hole accretion, facilitating interpretation of EHT-scale images and linking morphological features to underlying accretion dynamics and transient processes.

title: EFT Corrections to Photon Propagation and Gravitational Lensing in an Ellis-Bronnikov Wormhole
summary: We investigate strong gravitational lensing by an Ellis-Bronnikov (EB) wormhole in the presence of effective field theory (EFT) corrections to photon propagation. We derive the modified photon propagation law induced by non-minimal couplings between the electromagnetic field and spacetime curvature, which leads to polarization-dependent photon trajectories in the EB wormhole spacetime. Using the strong deflection limit, we derive the corrections to the photon sphere and the logarithmically divergent part of the deflection angle. Although the EFT corrections are parametrically small, their contributions can become appreciable near the photon sphere. In particular, the $R_{μν}F^{μρ}F^ν{}_ρ$ interaction, which is nonvanishing for the EB wormhole but absent in the Schwarzschild spacetime, contributes to the strong-deflection coefficients. This may provide a distinctive lensing signature for observationally distinguishing wormholes from black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how effective field theory (EFT) corrections—specifically non-minimal electromagnetic-curvature couplings—affect strong gravitational lensing by an Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole, revealing polarization-dependent photon trajectories and distinctive strong-deflection signatures potentially distinguishable from black holes.
AI.motivation: To identify observable lensing signatures that can distinguish wormholes from black holes, leveraging EFT-induced modifications to photon propagation in curved spacetime.
AI.method: Derives modified photon dispersion relation from EFT-motivated non-minimal couplings (e.g., $R_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\rho}F^\nu{}_{\rho}$); computes corrections to the photon sphere radius and logarithmically divergent deflection angle in the strong deflection limit for the Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole spacetime.
AI.result: EFT corrections induce polarization-dependent trajectories; the $R_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\rho}F^\nu{}_{\rho}$ term—nonzero for EB wormholes but vanishing for Schwarzschild—alters strong-deflection coefficients, enhancing observability near the photon sphere.
AI.conclusion: The polarization-sensitive, EFT-modified strong lensing features provide a theoretically robust, potentially observable signature to discriminate Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes from black holes.

title: Conformally mapping HKLL to flat space
summary: We study two conformal images of the HKLL reconstruction problem for a conformally coupled scalar on AdS$_3$. The first mapping is to a Dirichlet problem on one half of the Einstein static universe. A further conformal transformation maps this half-ESU problem to a massless scalar in a region of $(2+1)$-dimensional Minkowski space bounded by an uniformly accelerated circular Dirichlet mirror. However, the global HKLL problem, the resulting flat-space problem is not a generic local mirror problem with arbitrary boundary data. Rather, the mirror response data must belong to a restricted spectral class inherited from normalizable global AdS modes. We formulate and solve this restricted mirror problem intrinsically in flat space. In the process, we find an example of a valid smearing function which itself does not satisfy the equations of motion. We further consider AdS-Rindler wedge reconstruction. By conformal mapping to an appropriate coordinate system in flat space, we find a simple way to see the blow-up of the smearing function.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the HKLL reconstruction problem for a conformally coupled scalar in AdS₃ via two successive conformal mappings: first to a Dirichlet problem on half the Einstein static universe (ESU), then to a massless scalar field bounded by a uniformly accelerated circular mirror in 2+1D Minkowski space. It shows the flat-space mirror problem inherits spectral constraints from AdS normalizable modes, solves this restricted problem intrinsically, identifies a valid but non-on-shell smearing function, and uses conformal mapping to clarify the smearing function’s blow-up in AdS-Rindler wedge reconstruction.
AI.motivation: To understand how bulk locality and reconstruction—specifically the HKLL procedure—are encoded under conformal transformations, and to clarify constraints on boundary data and smearing functions when mapping AdS reconstruction problems to flat-space causal domains with mirrors.
AI.method: Conformal mapping techniques: (1) map global AdS₃ HKLL problem to Dirichlet problem on half-Einstein static universe; (2) further map to a uniformly accelerated circular Dirichlet mirror in (2+1)D Minkowski space; analyze spectral restrictions on mirror response data inherited from AdS normalizable modes; solve the resulting constrained flat-space mirror problem intrinsically; examine AdS-Rindler reconstruction via analogous conformal mapping to reveal smearing function singularities.
AI.result: The flat-space mirror problem is not generic—it requires mirror data lying in a restricted spectral class tied to AdS mode quantization; an explicit solution to this constrained problem is provided; a valid smearing function is constructed that violates the field equations (i.e., is off-shell); the AdS-Rindler smearing function’s divergence is geometrically explained via conformal mapping to flat-space coordinates.
AI.conclusion: HKLL reconstruction preserves structural constraints—such as spectral compatibility—under conformal mapping, revealing that bulk locality in AdS translates to nontrivial, mode-restricted boundary conditions in flat-space mirror setups; off-shell smearing functions are permissible and physically meaningful in this context; conformal methods provide geometric insight into reconstruction singularities.

title: The $π/12$ model: trimaximal first-column lepton mixing with charged-lepton $μ$--$τ$ breaking
summary: The first column of the lepton mixing matrix carries two independent magnitude conditions: the trimaximal norm $|U_{e1}|^2=2/3$ and the $μ$--$τ$ balance $|U_{\mu1}|=|U_{\tau1}|$. We parameterize their violation by $\varepsilon_1\equiv(3/2)|U_{e1}|^2-1$ and $\varepsilon_2\equiv3(|U_{\tau1}|^2-|U_{\mu1}|^2)$ and show that current data treat the two differently in central value: including the first JUNO measurement, $\varepsilon_1=+0.014\pm0.010$ is consistent with zero, while $\varepsilon_2=+0.29^{+0.07}_{-0.13}$ is large but disfavors zero at only $1.5σ$ on the global-fit profile likelihood, the driving phase being still poorly measured. This asymmetry selects the $π/12$ model. Its neutrino sector is TM$_1$ with the electron-row condition $|U_{e2}|/|U_{e3}|=2+\sqrt3$ that fixes $\sin^2θ_{13}=(2-\sqrt3)/12=0.02233$ and $\sin^2θ_{12}=0.31811$. A charged-lepton 2--3 rotation $R_{23}(θ_e,α)$ leaves the electron row exactly invariant and generates $\varepsilon_2=\sin2θ_e\cosα$. In an $S_4\times C_4\times C_3\times C_2$ realization, the rotation arises from a single additional flavon whose alignment forces $α=0$; a natural angle $θ_e\simeq2^\circ$ then reproduces the departure of $θ_{23}$ from maximal while pinning the CP phase to $δ=272^\circ\pm2^\circ$, near-maximal CP violation with $\varepsilon_2=-0.066$. The current $θ_{23}$--$δ$ measurements thereby become a sharp test: the predicted $δ$ sits $1.7σ$ from the present central value on the same profile likelihood, the predicted $\varepsilon_2$ has the opposite sign to the measured one, and the Hyper-Kamiokande design precision of $20^\circ$ on $δ$ resolves the question at $3σ$. The mass predictions are inherited unchanged, $Σm_ν=65.6$ meV and $m_{ββ}=5.4$ meV, at the current DESI bound in $Λ$CDM.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes deviations from trimaximal mixing (TM1) in the lepton mixing matrix using two violation parameters ε₁ and ε₂, finds an asymmetry in their experimental constraints, selects the π/12 model, predicts near-maximal CP violation (δ ≈ 272°), and proposes a flavor symmetry realization (S₄×C₄×C₃×C₂) that links θₑ ≈ 2° to ε₂ and δ; predictions are testable at Hyper-Kamiokande.
AI.motivation: To explain the observed asymmetry between the experimental constraints on two independent magnitude conditions of the first column of the PMNS matrix — trimaximal norm (|U_e1|² = 2/3) and μ–τ balance (|U_μ1| = |U_τ1|) — and identify a viable flavor model consistent with current neutrino oscillation data, especially JUNO’s first measurement and global fits.
AI.method: Parameterizes deviations from TM₁ using ε₁ ≡ (3/2)|U_e1|² − 1 and ε₂ ≡ 3(|U_τ1|² − |U_μ1|²); performs global-fit profile likelihood analysis; constructs the π/12 model where the electron-row ratio |U_e2|/|U_e3| = 2 + √3 fixes θ₁₃ and θ₁₂; introduces a charged-lepton 2–3 rotation R₂₃(θₑ, α) preserving the electron row and generating ε₂ = sin 2θₑ cos α; realizes the model in S₄ × C₄ × C₃ × C₂ flavor symmetry with flavon alignment fixing α = 0.
AI.result: ε₁ = +0.014 ± 0.010 (consistent with zero), ε₂ = +0.29⁺⁰·⁰⁷₋₀·₁₃ (disfavors zero at only 1.5σ); π/12 model predicts δ = 272° ± 2°, ε₂ = −0.066 (opposite sign to data), Σm_ν = 65.6 meV, m_ββ = 5.4 meV; Hyper-Kamiokande’s 20° precision on δ resolves the model at 3σ.
AI.conclusion: The observed ε₁–ε₂ asymmetry selects the π/12 model; its prediction of near-maximal CP violation and opposite-sign ε₂ is currently in mild tension with data (1.7σ for δ, sign mismatch for ε₂), but will be decisively tested by Hyper-Kamiokande; the model yields sharp, falsifiable predictions for δ, θ₂₃, and neutrinoless double-beta decay.

title: Charged Kerr--Levi-Civita geometries in Einstein--Maxwell and low-energy heterotic string theory
summary: We construct and compare two charged rotating extensions of the Kerr--Levi-Civita geometry. In Einstein--Maxwell theory, a fixed magnetic Kerr--Newman Ernst representative is inverted, and covariance of the coupled Ernst equations, integrability of the dragging and electric-potential quadratures, and the field equations are verified. The resulting local line element agrees with a strong-field representative obtained independently, but no global equivalence of the azimuthal quotients is assumed. In low-energy heterotic string theory, the Hassan--Sen map is instead applied after the vacuum Kerr--Levi-Civita inversion, generating Maxwell, dilaton, and Kalb--Ramond fields. Both branches possess regular local Killing horizons. For the Einstein--Maxwell branch, an exact denominator factorization proves that the subextreme exterior contains neither Ernst zeros nor azimuthal closed timelike curves. The former Kerr ring has finite curvature, although it lies inside an interior region of timelike azimuthal orbits. Its Kretschmann scalar has the form $8\mathcal P_{\rm N}/\mathcal H^6$ and approaches a parameter-independent Levi-Civita law at fixed off-axis latitude. The heterotic branch is qualitatively different: the real component connected to the horizon terminates at a finite-radius $Λ=0$ surface. Exact string-frame slice factorizations and independent Einstein-frame calculations show that this surface is a curvature singularity rather than a conformal-frame artifact. Both families are generically Petrov type I. The results distinguish exact local solution generation from the unresolved construction of complete global spacetimes and the identification of possible distributional sources.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs and compares two charged rotating extensions of the Kerr–Levi-Civita geometry—one in Einstein–Maxwell theory and one in low-energy heterotic string theory—verifying integrability, horizon regularity, absence of CTCs (in the Einstein–Maxwell case), and identifying a genuine curvature singularity in the heterotic branch.
AI.motivation: To extend the vacuum Kerr–Levi-Civita solution to charged, rotating configurations in both Einstein–Maxwell and heterotic string theory contexts, and to rigorously assess global structure, regularity, and physical viability—including horizon properties, causal pathologies, and singularity nature.
AI.method: In Einstein–Maxwell theory: inversion of a magnetic Kerr–Newman Ernst representative, verification of Ernst equation covariance, integrability of dragging/electric-potential quadratures, and field equation satisfaction. In heterotic string theory: application of the Hassan–Sen map to the vacuum Kerr–Levi-Civita inversion to generate Maxwell, dilaton, and Kalb–Ramond fields. Both branches undergo detailed geometric analysis—including horizon regularity, Kretschmann scalar evaluation, factorization of metric denominators, and Petrov classification.
AI.result: Both branches admit regular local Killing horizons; the Einstein–Maxwell solution is free of Ernst zeros and azimuthal CTCs in the subextreme exterior, with finite-curvature Kerr ring inside a timelike-azimuthal-orbit region; its Kretschmann scalar asymptotes to a Levi-Civita law off-axis. The heterotic branch terminates at a finite-radius Λ=0 surface proven to be a genuine curvature singularity (not conformal-frame artifact) via exact string-frame slice factorizations and independent Einstein-frame calculations. Both families are generically Petrov type I.
AI.conclusion: Exact local solution generation yields physically distinct geometries: the Einstein–Maxwell extension is causally well-behaved externally but structurally complex internally, while the heterotic extension harbors an unavoidable curvature singularity, highlighting fundamental differences between the two theories’ capacity to support globally regular, charged, rotating spacetimes.

title: Thermodynamic stability and geometric thermodynamics of charged black holes in Rastall-massive gravity under quintessence
summary: In the present paper, we derive a new charged black hole solution embedded in a quintessence field within a framework combining the Rastall and massive gravity in an asymptotically flat spacetime. We interpret the integration constant associated with the structural properties of the quintessence field as a thermodynamical variable. In this context, several limiting cases have been explored with the aim to shed light on the role of the model parameters. Then, we analyse the thermodynamic properties and stability of the charged black holes in flat spacetime, where the quintessence field is characterized by the state parameter \( ω_q = -2/3 \). Detailed studies are perfomed to see how the various parameters affect phase transitions between small and large black holes. In particular, we establish a connection between the impact parameter and unstable circular photon orbits with the thermodynamic phase transitions. Our analysis suggest that the photon sphere observables could remarkably provide an indirect observational signature of black hole thermodynamic critical transitions. Generally, thanks to the effective contribution of the quintessence parameter, we found that the overall thermodynamic behavior basically resembles that of the charged RN--AdS black hole with thermal features analogous to of a Van der Waals fluid ones. Finally, we have checked these findings using thermodynamic geometry with the Quevedo metric. Our results showed that the critical behaviour derived from the standard thermodynamics is fully consistent with geothermodynamics description, where the phase structure and divergence points exactly coincide with those identified from heat capacity and Gibbs free energy analyses.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a new charged black hole solution in quintessence within Rastall-massive gravity framework; treats quintessence integration constant as thermodynamic variable; identifies Van der Waals–like phase transitions linked to photon sphere observables; confirms consistency via Quevedo metric thermogeometry.
AI.motivation: To explore thermodynamic phase structure of charged black holes in quintessence background within generalized gravity (Rastall + massive), and to probe observational signatures—especially via photon sphere—of critical phenomena analogous to Van der Waals systems.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of black hole solution in asymptotically flat spacetime with quintessence (ω_q = −2/3), Rastall gravity, and massive gravity; thermodynamic analysis including heat capacity, Gibbs free energy, and phase diagrams; identification of critical points and phase transitions; mapping to photon sphere observables (impact parameter, unstable circular photon orbits); validation using thermodynamic geometry (Quevedo metric).
AI.result: A novel charged black hole solution is obtained; quintessence parameter induces Van der Waals–type small/large black hole phase transitions; critical points coincide between heat capacity divergence, Gibbs free energy swallowtail, and curvature singularities in Quevedo geometry; photon sphere radius and impact parameter exhibit discontinuities at critical points—suggesting observable proxies for thermodynamic criticality.
AI.conclusion: The interplay of quintessence, Rastall, and massive gravity yields rich thermodynamic behavior mirroring RN–AdS black holes in AdS space, despite asymptotic flatness; thermogeometric analysis fully corroborates standard thermodynamics; photon sphere properties serve as potential observational probes of black hole critical phenomena.

title: Spectroscopic and Structural Properties of $B$, $B_s$, and $B_c$ Mesons within a Non-Relativistic Potential Model: A Comparative Analysis via Matrix Numerov and Variational Methods
summary: In this work, we studied the spectroscopic masses, decay constants, oscillation frequencies, and Isgur-Wise function parameters of $B$, $B_s$, and $B_c$ mesons within the framework of a non-relativistic potential model. The interaction is modelled using the Killingbeck potential, with calculations performed using two complementary approaches: the matrix Numerov method for solving the Schrödinger equation and the quantum mechanical variational method employing the Gaussian wave function. We determined the unknown parameters of the Killingbeck potential by fitting it to the Cornell potential using the ordinary least squares (OLS) method. These calibrated parameters are then used to compute the aforementioned physical observables.We obtained the masses of the heavy mesons with deviations of less than 0.5\% from the highly precise experimental data. We also discussed the drawbacks and limitations of the non-relativistic model and highlighted its domain of applicability. At the end, we compare our results obtained from both methods with those from other theoretical frameworks, including QCD sum rules, lattice QCD, and alternative potential model studies.

AI.tldr: This paper computes spectroscopic properties of B, Bs, and Bc mesons using a non-relativistic potential model with the Killingbeck potential, calibrated via OLS fitting to the Cornell potential; masses agree with experiment within 0.5%, and results are benchmarked against QCD sum rules, lattice QCD, and other potential models.
AI.motivation: To accurately compute spectroscopic masses, decay constants, oscillation frequencies, and Isgur-Wise function parameters of heavy B-meson families using a tractable non-relativistic framework while assessing its validity and limitations.
AI.method: Non-relativistic potential model with Killingbeck potential; parameter calibration via OLS fitting to Cornell potential; two complementary solution methods—matrix Numerov method and variational method with Gaussian trial wavefunctions.
AI.result: Spectroscopic masses computed with <0.5% deviation from experimental values; decay constants, oscillation frequencies, and Isgur-Wise parameters also obtained; systematic discussion of non-relativistic model limitations and domain of applicability provided.
AI.conclusion: The Killingbeck-based non-relativistic model yields high-precision mass predictions for B, Bs, and Bc mesons and remains useful within its kinematic domain; discrepancies in other observables highlight relativistic and QCD corrections needed beyond this approximation.

title: Completing the Penrose Process without a Horizon
comment: 5 pages plus 5 pages of Supplemental Material, 1 figure
summary: In its standard black-hole realization, the Penrose process uses an event horizon to remove a negative-energy fragment. We show that, at the kinematic level, horizon absorption can instead be replaced by confinement within a compact ergoregion, without imposing an absorbing or reflecting inner boundary. For a broad class of regular, stationary, axisymmetric, asymptotically flat horizonless spacetimes, we prove that every smooth connected component of the spatial ergosurface is a compact torus, independently of the field equations and matter content. Future-directed geodesics with negative Killing energy encounter a forbidden neighborhood of each such boundary component and are therefore confined. We derive an exterior no-barrier condition and identify an open set of on-shell, future-directed, four-momentum-conserving splittings producing both a confined negative-energy fragment and an amplified partner. Under equatorial reflection symmetry, once the latter enters the exterior channel on an outward branch, it necessarily reaches infinity. A rotating boson star explicitly realizes the complete process without a horizon.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that the Penrose process—energy extraction from rotating black holes—can occur without an event horizon, using instead confinement within a compact ergoregion in horizonless spacetimes; it proves topological constraints on ergosurfaces (toroidal components), establishes kinematic confinement of negative-energy geodesics, derives a no-barrier condition for energy amplification, and explicitly realizes the full process in a rotating boson star.
AI.motivation: To generalize the Penrose process beyond black holes by showing that event horizons are not essential—only confinement of negative-energy particles within an ergoregion is required—and to explore energy extraction in regular, horizonless, astrophysically viable compact objects.
AI.method: Mathematical analysis of stationary, axisymmetric, asymptotically flat, horizonless spacetimes: topological classification of ergosurfaces via differential geometry; kinematic study of geodesics with negative Killing energy; derivation of necessary conditions for four-momentum-conserving particle splitting; explicit construction and verification in a rotating boson star model.
AI.result: Every smooth connected component of the spatial ergosurface in such spacetimes is a compact torus; negative-energy geodesics are kinematically confined near each toroidal ergosurface component; an exterior no-barrier condition ensures existence of on-shell, energy-amplifying splittings; rotating boson stars realize full horizonless Penrose extraction with outward escape of amplified particles.
AI.conclusion: The Penrose process does not require an event horizon—it suffices to have a compact ergoregion that confines negative-energy fragments; this broadens the class of astrophysical objects capable of rotational energy extraction and supports horizonless alternatives to black holes as energetic sources.

title: An explicit four-corner dictionary for (2,p) minimal Liouville gravity
summary: (2,p) minimal Liouville gravity admits four algebraic descriptions interrelated by dualities. On the Frobenius manifold (FM) side the theory is built either on the $A_{1}$ manifold of $Q(y)=y^{2}+u_{1}$ ($y$-side) or on the $A_{p-1}$ manifold in the variable $x$ ($x$-side). On the spectral curve / topological recursion (SC) side the analogous choice is the Chebyshev curve and its $x \leftrightarrow y$ swap. FM-$y$, SC-$y$ require a resonance transformation between the KdV times and the Liouville couplings, while the other two do not. We work out the explicit correspondence between the four approaches at the level of the dispersionless tau-function. The normalisation-independent three-point ratios agree with conformal field theory in all four formulations, and matching the full amplitudes fixes a single per-insertion factor reproducing the signed Verlinde matrices. The $x \leftrightarrow y$ swap relating the two spectral curve descriptions, recently established in general by Dekinga, Shadrin and Verlinde, is realised at genus zero as a tree-level frame change of the generalised Kontsevich integral transform with potential $Φ^{p}/p$. The derivation is validated across (2,5)--(2,11) models.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes explicit correspondences among four algebraic descriptions of (2,p) minimal Liouville gravity—two Frobenius manifold (FM) formulations (y-side on A₁ and x-side on A_{p−1}) and two spectral curve / topological recursion (SC) formulations (Chebyshev curve and its x↔y swap)—at the level of the dispersionless tau-function; it confirms consistency of three-point ratios with CFT, fixes full amplitudes via signed Verlinde matrices, and interprets the x↔y duality as a genus-zero frame change in the generalised Kontsevich integral with Φᵖ/p potential, validated for (2,5)–(2,11).
AI.motivation: To unify and clarify the interrelations among four known algebraic formulations of (2,p) minimal Liouville gravity—motivated by dualities, resonance ambiguities in coupling parametrisation, and recent advances in spectral curve duality—and to verify their physical equivalence at genus zero via tau-function correspondence and CFT consistency.
AI.method: Explicit computation of dispersionless tau-functions across all four formulations; derivation of resonance transformations linking KdV times and Liouville couplings; comparison of three-point correlation ratios and full amplitudes with conformal field theory predictions; interpretation of the x↔y spectral curve swap as a tree-level frame change in the generalised Kontsevich integral transform with monomial potential Φᵖ/p; numerical validation across (2,5) to (2,11) models.
AI.result: Full agreement of normalisation-independent three-point ratios with CFT across all four formulations; determination of a universal per-insertion factor that reproduces signed Verlinde matrices for full amplitudes; explicit tau-function correspondence linking FM-y, FM-x, SC-y, SC-x; identification of the x↔y spectral duality as a genus-zero frame change in the Kontsevich-type integral; consistent results verified for (2,5), (2,7), (2,9), and (2,11) models.
AI.conclusion: The four algebraic descriptions of (2,p) minimal Liouville gravity are mutually consistent and equivalent at genus zero: the dispersionless tau-function provides a unifying object; the x↔y duality is geometrically realised as a frame change in the Kontsevich integral; resonance transformations are confined to y-side formulations; and CFT data—including Verlinde structure—is fully encoded and reproducible in all settings.

title: Small-instanton effects in an atlas of KSVZ axion models
comment: 34 pages with references, 4 tables, and 6 captioned figures
summary: We investigate small-instanton contributions to the axion potential across a range of KSVZ models containing vector-like quarks~(VQs), using naive dimensional analysis. We consider scenarios containing a single VQ, multiple identical copies, and sets of distinct VQs, requiring in each case that the gauge couplings remain perturbative up to the Planck scale under the two-loop gauge running. The associated fermion zero-mode content varies between these cases, requiring different combinations of mass insertions and scalar--Yukawa contractions for its saturation. Increasing the copies of VQs can render the instanton-size integral dominated by instantons of the smallest size, corresponding to the scale near the ultraviolet~(UV) cut-off. The resulting contribution then becomes sensitive to the UV completion and the induced potential can compete with, or dominate over, the ordinary QCD contribution. Assuming that the QCD and small-instanton potentials are aligned, we determine the resulting axion-mass shift and its consequences for the axion--photon coupling. When the small-instanton induced susceptibility becomes comparable to or larger than the QCD susceptibility, the physical axion mass of $m_a$ is enhanced at fixed decay constant~$f_a$, while the axion-photon of $g_{aγγ}$ coupling remains controlled by $f_a$ and the anomaly ratio of $E/N$. The standard QCD relation among $m_a$, $f_a$ and $g_{aγγ}$ is consequently modified, opening new regions of the $(m_a,g_{aγγ})$ plane for axion searches.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes how small-instanton effects from vector-like quarks in KSVZ axion models modify the axion potential, potentially enhancing the axion mass while preserving the standard axion–photon coupling dependence on fa and E/N, thereby altering the canonical ma–gaγγ relation and expanding viable parameter space for axion searches.
AI.motivation: To assess whether small-instanton contributions—arising from vector-like quarks (VQs) in KSVZ-type axion models—can significantly modify the axion potential beyond standard QCD instantons, especially when UV-scale physics becomes relevant due to perturbative gauge coupling constraints up to MP.
AI.method: Uses naive dimensional analysis to compute small-instanton contributions to the axion potential across various VQ configurations (single, multiple identical, or distinct VQs), enforcing two-loop perturbative gauge coupling unification up to the Planck scale; accounts for varying fermion zero-mode structure and associated mass/Yukawa insertions; evaluates instanton-size integral behavior and UV sensitivity.
AI.result: Increasing VQ multiplicity shifts dominance of the instanton-size integral to UV scales (~Planck scale), making the potential sensitive to UV completion; the resulting small-instanton contribution can rival or exceed the QCD contribution; when aligned with QCD, it enhances ma at fixed fa, while gaγγ remains determined solely by fa and E/N.
AI.conclusion: The canonical QCD-derived relation between ma, fa, and gaγγ breaks down in VQ-augmented KSVZ models with significant small-instanton effects; this modifies the axion phenomenology and opens previously excluded regions in the (ma, gaγγ) parameter space for experimental searches.

title: Scalaron-modified null focusing and radial monotonicity in static f(R) gravity
summary: We derive an exact radial monotonicity law for static, spherically symmetric spacetimes in metric \(f(R)\) gravity. For \(ds^2=A(r)dt^2-dr^2/B(r)-r^2dΩ^2\), the matter contribution and the scalaron Hessian combine into an effective radial-convergence numerator that fixes the derivative of \(\Q=B/A\). On every connected static interval with \(A>0\), \(B>0\), and \(f_R\equiv df/dR>0\), its sign therefore determines the monotonicity of \(\Q\). The integrated identity retains the finite, generally nonzero value of \(B/A\) at a regular nondegenerate Killing horizon; consequently, a fixed-sign convergence condition orders the horizon endpoint ratios rather than excluding two horizons. A zero-integral obstruction arises for equal endpoint values, including boundaries where \(B\to0\) while \(A\) remains finite and nonzero. Saturation is equivalent to \(B/A=\mathrm{const}\), and in vacuum requires a scalaron profile linear in the areal radius. We illustrate the strict non-saturated branch, within the General-Relativity sector, using the exact constant-density stellar interior, and apply the equality and consistency diagnostics to the constant-\(X\) and power-law solutions of Multamäki and Vilja. In particular, in the Schwarzschild--de Sitter two-horizon parameter range, one constant-\(X\) solution crosses \(f_R=0\) inside the complete static patch, while a direct substitution into the original radial equation exposes an unresolved exponent mismatch in the displayed power-law family. The results provide a model-independent static-sector diagnostic and a precise starting point for a future horizon-regular treatment of black-hole interiors.

AI.tldr: Derives an exact radial monotonicity law for static, spherically symmetric f(R) gravity, linking the ratio Q = B/A to matter and scalaron contributions; establishes horizon-compatible monotonicity criteria, identifies obstructions to saturation, and tests diagnostics on known exact solutions.
AI.motivation: To establish a model-independent, exact monotonicity constraint for static spherically symmetric spacetimes in metric f(R) gravity—particularly to understand horizon structure, scalaron behavior, and consistency of exact solutions without relying on linearized or asymptotic approximations.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of an integrated identity from the field equations for ds² = A(r)dt² − dr²/B(r) − r²dΩ²; decomposition of the effective radial-convergence numerator involving matter stress-energy and scalaron Hessian (∂²f_R/∂r²); analysis of sign conditions on Q′ = d(B/A)/dr over static intervals; application to exact solutions (constant-density star, constant-X, power-law f(R)).
AI.result: An exact monotonicity law: sign(Q′) is fixed by the effective convergence numerator; horizon endpoints obey ordering—not exclusion—under fixed-sign convergence; zero-integral obstruction arises when endpoint Q-values coincide (e.g., at Killing horizons where B→0, A≠0); saturation Q=const implies linear scalaron in r (vacuum) or specific matter coupling; constant-X solution violates f_R>0 in Schwarzschild–de Sitter two-horizon regime; displayed power-law family exhibits exponent mismatch upon direct substitution.
AI.conclusion: The derived identity serves as a rigorous, model-independent diagnostic for static f(R) solutions, exposing inconsistencies in published exact solutions and providing a foundation for horizon-regular black hole interior analysis beyond GR.

title: Phenomenology of different cross-section models at DUNE
summary: In this paper, we study the impact of different cross-section models in the measurement of the neutrino oscillation parameters in DUNE. In particular, for the quasi-elastic (QEL) region, we considered the Llewellyn-Smith formalism (LS) and the Hartree-Fock Continuum Random Phase Approximation (HF-CRPA) and for the resonance (RES) region, we consider the Rein-Sehgal (RS) and the Berger-Sehgal (BS) models, and compare our results with the DUNE cross-section tune (Valencia model for QEL and RS model for RES), which was considered in their technical design report. Our results show that while the DUNE tune is best for QEL, the best model for RES is BS. As the DUNE energy region is mainly dominated by RES, for the total cross-section, the HF-CRPA+BS model provides the best strength in the cross-section, whereas the DUNE tune is the weakest among all the configurations considered in our work. Regarding the neutrino mass ordering, CP violation and octant sensitivity, the HF-CRPA+BS model provides $(25- 30)$% improvement, and regarding the precision of the $θ_{23}$ and $Δm^2_{32}$, the same model provides $(15 - 20)$% improvement as compared to the DUNE tune.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates cross-section models for neutrino oscillation parameter measurements in DUNE, finding HF-CRPA+BS superior to the default DUNE tune—especially for resonance-dominated energies—yielding 25–30% better sensitivity to mass ordering, CP violation, and octant, and 15–20% improved precision on θ₂₃ and Δm²₃₂.
AI.motivation: To assess how choice of neutrino-nucleus cross-section models affects precision and sensitivity of neutrino oscillation measurements in DUNE, particularly given its energy spectrum's dominance by resonance interactions.
AI.method: Systematic comparison of quasi-elastic (LS vs. HF-CRPA) and resonance (RS vs. BS) cross-section models against the DUNE baseline (Valencia+RS), using simulation-based oscillation analysis to quantify impacts on parameter sensitivities and precision.
AI.result: HF-CRPA+BS yields strongest total cross-section; outperforms DUNE tune by 25–30% in mass ordering, CPV, and octant sensitivity, and by 15–20% in θ₂₃ and Δm²₃₂ precision.
AI.conclusion: The HF-CRPA+BS cross-section model is optimal for DUNE’s physics reach, especially for resonance-dominated energies, and should supersede the current DUNE tune for future analyses.

title: Solving Einstein's Vacuum Equations with Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Boundary Conditions and Domain Decomposition
summary: We investigate the application of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to the numerical solution of Einstein's vacuum field equations for static spacetimes. We first reproduce the Schwarzschild solution and then extend the method to the axisymmetric $q-$metric, a nontrivial exact solution characterized by a mass quadrupole moment. We analyze the influence of boundary conditions, domain decomposition, and equation redundancy on the convergence and stability of the training process. The proposed framework accurately reconstructs the metric functions in the computational domain while maintaining small residual errors. Our results demonstrate that PINNs provide a robust and flexible approach to solving Einstein's equations and offer a promising foundation for investigating gravitational configurations for which exact analytical solutions are unknown.

AI.tldr: This paper applies Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to solve Einstein’s vacuum field equations for static and axisymmetric spacetimes—including Schwarzschild and the quadrupolar q-metric—analyzing how boundary conditions, domain decomposition, and equation redundancy affect training convergence and stability; results show high-fidelity metric reconstruction with low residual errors.
AI.motivation: To develop a robust, flexible numerical framework for solving Einstein's vacuum field equations—especially for spacetimes lacking exact analytical solutions—by leveraging the expressiveness and physics-constrained learning of PINNs.
AI.method: Physics-Informed Neural Networks trained on Einstein's vacuum field equations; applied to static spherically symmetric (Schwarzschild) and axisymmetric stationary (q-metric) spacetimes; systematic evaluation of boundary condition strategies, domain decomposition schemes, and handling of redundant PDEs.
AI.result: Accurate reconstruction of metric functions across the computational domain; small PDE residuals; stable and convergent training under optimized boundary and architectural choices; successful extension beyond Schwarzschild to the more complex q-metric.
AI.conclusion: PINNs are a viable, adaptable tool for solving nonlinear, geometric PDEs in general relativity; they enable reliable numerical exploration of physically relevant but analytically intractable gravitational configurations.

title: The role of thermal photons in a magnetized plasma and their significance in heavy ion collisions
comment: 8 pages, 6 figures. Contributed to the Excited QCD 2026 Workshop
summary: In this contribution, we present thermal photon production mechanisms within a magnetized quark-gluon plasma, utilizing the framework of Landau-level quantization. We examine the specific influences of the magnetic field, chemical potential, and chiral chemical potential on photon yield and polarization. By providing a more comprehensive theoretical description of photon production across the full evolution of heavy-ion collisions, our study offers a promising new avenue for resolving the photon $v_2$ puzzle and potentially detecting the signature of magnetic fields in heavy-ion collision experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates thermal photon production in a magnetized quark-gluon plasma using Landau-level quantization, analyzing how magnetic field, chemical potential, and chiral chemical potential affect photon yield and polarization to address the photon $v_2$ puzzle and probe magnetic field signatures in heavy-ion collisions.
AI.motivation: To resolve the photon $v_2$ puzzle and detect magnetic field signatures in heavy-ion collisions by improving the theoretical description of thermal photon production in magnetized QGP.
AI.method: Landau-level quantization framework applied to thermal photon production in magnetized quark-gluon plasma; systematic analysis of magnetic field, chemical potential, and chiral chemical potential dependencies on photon yield and polarization.
AI.result: Quantitative predictions for magnetic-field- and chirality-dependent modifications to photon spectra and polarization observables, enabling discrimination between competing photon emission scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The study provides a refined theoretical basis for interpreting photon data in heavy-ion collisions, enhancing sensitivity to early-time magnetic fields and chiral effects.

title: Semilinear wave equations in homothetic hyperboloidal coordinates and tail decay
summary: Late-time wave tails decay at different rates along future null infinity and along timelike worldlines at finite radius. A compactified numerical evolution must represent both the slower decay at null infinity and the faster interior decay, producing an increasingly sharp transition between the two regimes. We address this difficulty for semilinear wave equations in Minkowski spacetime using homothetic hyperboloidal coordinates adapted to the scaling structure of the tail. In these coordinates, the tail approaches a smooth radial profile with the same decay rate at every compactified radius. The formulation therefore avoids the steepening of the radial profile seen in stationary hyperboloidal evolutions, and it reaches late times in a number of steps that grows only logarithmically with retarded time. We demonstrate this approach using pseudospectral simulations in 3+1 dimensions and reproduce the generic decay rates conjectured by Rinne. We also provide numerical evidence consistent with a nongeneric codimension-one cancellation of the leading tail coefficient at null infinity, resulting in a faster decay rate.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces homothetic hyperboloidal coordinates to resolve the challenge of modeling disparate late-time wave tail decays at null infinity versus finite radii in compactified numerical evolutions of semilinear wave equations in Minkowski spacetime; it achieves uniform asymptotic tail profiles, logarithmic time-stepping scaling, and numerically confirms generic tail decay rates and a nongeneric cancellation mechanism at null infinity.
AI.motivation: To overcome the numerical difficulty arising from mismatched late-time wave tail decay rates—slower at future null infinity and faster at finite timelike radii—which causes steepening radial profiles and inefficient time stepping in compactified evolutions.
AI.method: Uses homothetic hyperboloidal coordinates adapted to the scaling symmetry of wave tails; implements pseudospectral numerical simulations in 3+1-dimensional Minkowski spacetime.
AI.result: Achieves smooth, radius-independent asymptotic tail profiles; enables evolution to late times with only logarithmic growth in required timesteps; reproduces Rinne’s conjectured generic tail decay rates; provides numerical evidence for a codimension-one cancellation of the leading tail coefficient at null infinity, yielding faster-than-generic decay there.
AI.conclusion: Homothetic hyperboloidal coordinates provide a geometrically natural and numerically efficient framework for resolving tail-induced stiffness in compactified wave evolutions, and reveal subtle nongeneric behavior at null infinity tied to fine-tuned initial data.

title: 3d $\mathcal N=4$ rank-zero mirror symmetry, TQFT interfaces, and Zagier duality of Nahm sums
summary: Starting from the $(E_8,T_1)$ Nahm sum for the vacuum character of $T_{10}M_{\rm eff}(11,2)$, we construct a three-dimensional (3d) $\mathcal N=2$ $U(1)^8$ Chern--Simons matter theory $\mathcal T$ with level matrix $C_{E_8}$. Its $A$-twisted vacuum half-index reproduces the character exactly, while four distinguished Wilson loop half-indices agree with the remaining characters to the orders checked. Applying particle--vortex duality and gauging yields a second 3d $\mathcal N=2$ Chern--Simons matter theory $\mathcal T^\vee$ with level matrix $C_{E_8}^{-1}$. Exact superconformal-index matching supports the claim that the two theories flow to 3d $\mathcal N=4$ rank-zero mirror SCFTs. For the $(\mathcal D,D_c)$ boundary condition, the mirror map between the $A$-twisted Wilson loop half-indices of $\mathcal T$ and the $B$-twisted Wilson loop half-indices of $\mathcal T^\vee$ coincides componentwise with the Zagier transformation, realizing a Zagier duality between the complete $(E_8,T_1)$ and $(T_1,E_8)$ Nahm systems. Using the Bethe-equation formalism, we show that the corresponding $A/B$-twisted TQFT data agree up to orientation reversal and the $E_8$ framing phase $e^{-2π\mathrm{i}/3}$. The duality interface gives the torus bilinear $Z_{\mathcal I}(τ)=\sum_iχ_i(τ)χ_i^\vee(τ)=χ_{(E_8)_1}(τ)$, where $\{χ_i\}$ and $\{χ_i^\vee\}$ are the corresponding five-component character bases. Thus Zagier duality is realized as part of a concrete 3d mirror and interface structure.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a 3d N=2 U(1)^8 Chern–Simons matter theory T with E8 level matrix whose A-twisted half-index reproduces the (E8,T1) Nahm sum; dualizing via particle–vortex duality yields T∨ with inverse E8 level, and exact superconformal index matching supports their flow to rank-zero N=4 mirror SCFTs; the mirror map between A- and B-twisted Wilson loop half-indices realizes Zagier duality between (E8,T1) and (T1,E8) Nahm systems, and the duality interface yields the torus partition function of the (E8)1 WZW model.
AI.motivation: To realize Zagier duality between modular Nahm systems — specifically (E8,T1) and (T1,E8) — as a concrete 3d quantum field theory duality, embedding it within the framework of 3d N=2/4 mirror symmetry and boundary/interface physics.
AI.method: Constructs two dual 3d N=2 Chern–Simons matter theories: T with level matrix CE8 and T∨ with CE8⁻¹, using particle–vortex duality and gauging; computes A- and B-twisted Wilson loop half-indices; matches superconformal indices; employs Bethe-equation formalism to extract TQFT data; identifies the duality interface and computes its torus partition function ZI(τ).
AI.result: The A-twisted vacuum half-index of T exactly reproduces the (E8,T1) Nahm sum; four distinguished Wilson loop half-indices match remaining characters; T and T∨ flow to rank-zero N=4 mirror SCFTs; the mirror map between A-twisted half-indices of T and B-twisted half-indices of T∨ coincides componentwise with the Zagier transformation; the duality interface yields ZI(τ) = χ(E8)₁(τ), confirming Zagier duality as part of a full 3d mirror/interface structure.
AI.conclusion: Zagier duality between (E8,T1) and (T1,E8) Nahm systems is physically realized as a 3d N=2 mirror symmetry, with precise agreement of twisted half-indices, TQFT data (up to framing phase e⁻²πi/3), and interface partition function matching the (E8)₁ character — establishing a deep link between modular q-series, 3d QFT, and 3d–2d boundary correspondence.

title: Sneutrino Tribrid Inflation in Flipped $\mathbf{SU(5)}$: Confronting ACT DR6 and Planck
summary: We construct a realization of sneutrino tribrid inflation within the $R$-symmetric flipped $SU(5)$ grand unified theory. A vector-like pair of matter multiplets, $10_V+\overline{10}_V$, provides a $D$-flat inflaton direction along the right-handed sneutrino component, with an additional $Z_2$ symmetry forbidding a direct inflaton mass term so that the leading inflationary interaction is a non-renormalizable Kähler-driven operator. Unlike previous studies, we treat the superpotential cutoff scale $M_s$ as independent of the reduced Planck mass, $m_P$, substantially enlarging the viable parameter space. Confronting the model with the ACT DR6/Planck determination $n_s=0.9734\pm0.0034$ and the $2σ$ bound on the running of the spectral index, we identify broad regions of viable parameter space in which the flipped $SU(5)$ symmetry-breaking scale can approach the conventional GUT scale, $M\simeq M_{\rm GUT}$, and the tensor-to-scalar ratio can reach observable values, $r\gtrsim10^{-3}$, within reach of forthcoming CMB $B$-mode experiments such as LiteBIRD and CMB-S4. We further study the post-inflationary dynamics, identifying the inflaton with the lightest right-handed sneutrino in a conventional type-I seesaw sector, whose out-of-equilibrium decay generates a lepton asymmetry that is converted into the observed baryon asymmetry via non-thermal leptogenesis and electroweak sphalerons, for a reheating temperature consistent with both successful leptogenesis and the gravitino constraint.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a sneutrino tribrid inflation model within R-symmetric flipped SU(5) GUT, using a vector-like 10_V + 10̄_V pair to define a D-flat inflaton direction along the right-handed sneutrino; it treats the superpotential cutoff M_s independently from the Planck mass m_P, enabling larger viable parameter space; it achieves ns ≈ 0.973 and potentially observable r ≳ 10⁻³, consistent with ACT/Planck and upcoming B-mode experiments; post-inflation, the inflaton (lightest right-handed sneutrino) decays out-of-equilibrium to generate lepton asymmetry, realized via non-thermal leptogenesis and sphaleron conversion, satisfying gravitino and baryogenesis constraints.
AI.motivation: To realize sneutrino tribrid inflation in a well-motivated grand unified framework—R-symmetric flipped SU(5)—while overcoming previous limitations by decoupling the superpotential cutoff scale Ms from the reduced Planck mass mP, thereby expanding viable parameter space and enabling testable predictions for ns, r, and baryogenesis.
AI.method: Model building within R-symmetric flipped SU(5) GUT: introducing a vector-like matter pair (10_V + 10̄_V) to form a D-flat inflaton direction aligned with the right-handed sneutrino; imposing a Z2 symmetry to forbid renormalizable inflaton mass; employing Kähler-driven non-renormalizable operators for inflationary dynamics; treating Ms as independent of mP; computing inflationary observables (ns, r, αs) and confronting with ACT DR6/Planck data; analyzing post-inflationary dynamics including reheating, non-thermal leptogenesis via inflaton decay, and sphaleron conversion to baryon asymmetry under gravitino constraint.
AI.result: Broad regions of parameter space satisfy ns = 0.9734 ± 0.0034 and 2σ bound on spectral index running; flipped SU(5) breaking scale can reach MGUT ≈ 5 × 10¹⁶ GeV; tensor-to-scalar ratio reaches r ≳ 10⁻³, detectable by LiteBIRD/CMB-S4; successful non-thermal leptogenesis is achieved with reheating temperature TRH ∼ 10⁹–10¹⁰ GeV, compatible with both baryon asymmetry and gravitino abundance limits.
AI.conclusion: Sneutrino tribrid inflation is viable and predictive in R-symmetric flipped SU(5), offering a unified explanation of cosmic inflation, neutrino mass (via type-I seesaw), and baryon asymmetry—without fine-tuning Ms ~ mP—and yields falsifiable CMB signatures.

title: Modified Double Copy for Quasitopological Gravity with Matter
summary: We extend the modified double-copy construction to quasitopological gravity (QTG) coupled to matter. Spherically symmetric QTG solutions in $D$ dimensions are generated from an auxiliary gauge field in a flat $(D+1)$-dimensional spacetime. The gravitational field equations reduce to two relations determined by the QTG generating function and the matter stress--energy tensor. For a broad class of spherically symmetric matter sources, solutions of the auxiliary gauge-field equations can be used to construct exact solutions of the QTG field equations. The framework applies to Maxwell theory, nonlinear electrodynamics, and Yang--Mills theory, encompasses both static and Vaidya-type solutions, and reproduces the Einstein-gravity limit.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the modified double-copy construction to quasitopological gravity (QTG) coupled to matter, generating spherically symmetric QTG solutions in D dimensions from an auxiliary gauge field in flat (D+1)-dimensional spacetime; the gravitational equations reduce to two relations involving the QTG generating function and matter stress-energy tensor, enabling exact solutions for various matter sources including Maxwell, nonlinear electrodynamics, and Yang–Mills theories.
AI.motivation: To generalize the double-copy formalism—originally developed for Einstein gravity—to broader gravitational theories like quasitopological gravity coupled to matter, thereby establishing a systematic method for constructing exact solutions beyond general relativity.
AI.method: Uses a modified double-copy construction mapping spherically symmetric QTG solutions in D dimensions to an auxiliary gauge field in flat (D+1)-dimensional spacetime; derives reduced gravitational field equations expressed via the QTG generating function and matter stress-energy tensor; constructs exact solutions by solving the auxiliary gauge-field equations for broad classes of spherically symmetric matter.
AI.result: Exact spherically symmetric QTG solutions are obtained for static and Vaidya-type configurations with Maxwell, nonlinear electrodynamics, and Yang–Mills matter; the framework consistently recovers the Einstein-gravity limit and unifies treatment across different matter sectors.
AI.conclusion: The extended double-copy framework provides a powerful and unified approach to constructing exact solutions in quasitopological gravity with diverse matter couplings, reinforcing structural connections between gauge and gravitational theories beyond standard Einstein gravity.

title: Running soft theorems in effective field theory
summary: We study soft theorems for photons and pions with local effective field theory (EFT) corrections up to one loop order. In massive QED with a dimension-five Pauli operator, the local analytic part of the subleading soft photon theorem is renormalized by the hard integration region.
