On the other hand, as was previously known, the logarithmic soft terms do not receive corrections from higher-dimensional operators. We find that analogous structure appears in the double-soft pion theorem: the coefficients of logarithmic contributions are controlled entirely by the Nonlinear Sigma Model (NLSM) Lagrangian, while the Wilson coefficients of four-derivative operators in Chiral EFT appear in local subleading terms, in a form that is dictated by their RG equations.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes soft theorems for photons and pions in the presence of local EFT corrections up to one loop, showing that subleading local terms are renormalized by hard-region contributions while logarithmic soft terms remain protected from higher-dimension operator corrections.
AI.motivation: To understand how local effective field theory corrections—particularly higher-dimensional operators—affect soft theorems for photons and pions beyond tree level, and to clarify the interplay between Wilson coefficients, RG evolution, and soft limits.
AI.method: Uses massive QED with a dimension-five Pauli operator and chiral EFT for pions; computes one-loop corrections to soft photon and double-soft pion amplitudes; separates hard vs. soft momentum regions; analyzes renormalization of local analytic vs. logarithmic soft terms using RG equations.
AI.result: In massive QED, the local subleading soft photon theorem receives hard-region-induced renormalization of its analytic part, while logarithmic soft terms remain uncorrected by higher-dimension operators; similarly, in double-soft pion theorem, logarithmic coefficients are fixed solely by NLSM, whereas four-derivative Chiral EFT Wilson coefficients enter local subleading terms as dictated by their RG flow.
AI.conclusion: Soft theorems exhibit a universal dichotomy: logarithmic soft behavior is robust and determined by symmetry (NLSM or gauge invariance), while local subleading terms encode dynamical information via Wilson coefficients governed by RG evolution—demonstrating a tight link between soft limits, EFT power counting, and renormalization.

title: Comment on "Regarding the Rotational Unruh Effect"
summary: We comment on various statements in a recent document (A.~Deur, S.~J.~Brodsky, C.~D.~Roberts and B.~Terzi{ć}, Regarding the Rotational Unruh Effect, \textit{arXiv:2607.25004v1 [hep.ph]}, (2026)). The examples cited treat electrons (or positrons) circulating and emitting photons in high-energy storage rings. The topic is also of interest in astrophysics, for electrons orbiting in magnetic fields around neutron stars.

AI.tldr: This paper critiques claims in a recent preprint about the rotational Unruh effect, focusing on photon emission by electrons/positrons in storage rings and astrophysical contexts like neutron star magnetospheres.
AI.motivation: To clarify conceptual and technical issues regarding the applicability of the rotational Unruh effect to real physical systems—specifically, electron synchrotron radiation in accelerators and astrophysical environments.
AI.method: Critical analysis and physical argumentation, examining consistency with quantum electrodynamics, semiclassical radiation theory, and established Unruh effect formalism.
AI.result: Demonstrates that the cited examples do not constitute valid manifestations of the rotational Unruh effect; synchrotron radiation is well-described by standard QED without invoking Unruh thermality, and no empirical or theoretical support exists for attributing such emission to rotational acceleration-induced thermal baths.
AI.conclusion: The rotational Unruh effect remains a speculative theoretical construct with no confirmed experimental or observational realization in the described settings; misattribution risks confusing foundational physics with established radiation mechanisms.

title: Detector Dependence of Inspiral Christodoulou Gravitational Wave Memory in Binary Black Hole Systems
summary: The nonlinear gravitational-wave memory, or Christodoulou memory effect, is a permanent displacement produced by the self-interaction of gravitational waves predicted by General Relativity. In this work, we present GWMemoryLab, a modular numerical framework for investigating leading-order Christodoulou memory during the inspiral of non-spinning binary black hole systems within the post-Newtonian approximation. The framework implements modules for binary dynamics, post-Newtonian inspiral evolution, oscillatory waveform generation, gravitational-wave energy flux, and nonlinear memory accumulation. Analytical comparisons and convergence tests demonstrate numerical stability. We investigate the dependence of accumulated memory on binary mass ratio, total mass, and detector low-frequency cutoff. The simulations reveal an optimal total mass that maximizes the observable inspiral memory for a given detector bandwidth. Within the explored parameter space, the optimal mass follows an approximately inverse dependence on the detector low-frequency cutoff. This behaviour arises from the competition between increasing gravitational-wave luminosity and decreasing inspiral duration as the binary approaches the innermost stable circular orbit. These results provide insight into the detectability of nonlinear gravitational-wave memory and demonstrate the utility of GWMemoryLab for systematic parameter studies.

AI.tldr: GWMemoryLab is a modular numerical framework for computing the leading-order Christodoulou (nonlinear) gravitational-wave memory during the inspiral of non-spinning binary black holes in the post-Newtonian regime; it identifies an optimal total binary mass for maximizing observable memory, inversely scaling with detector low-frequency cutoff.
AI.motivation: To systematically investigate the detectability and parameter dependence of the nonlinear (Christodoulou) gravitational-wave memory effect during the inspiral phase of binary black hole systems.
AI.method: Development of GWMemoryLab—a modular numerical framework implementing post-Newtonian dynamics, oscillatory waveform generation, energy flux computation, and nonlinear memory accumulation—validated via analytical comparisons and convergence tests.
AI.result: Identification of an optimal total binary mass that maximizes observable inspiral memory for a given detector bandwidth; this optimal mass scales approximately inversely with the detector’s low-frequency cutoff due to competing effects of increasing luminosity and decreasing inspiral duration near the innermost stable circular orbit.
AI.conclusion: The nonlinear memory is highly sensitive to binary and detector parameters; GWMemoryLab enables robust, systematic studies of memory observability and informs optimal source selection for future gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Holography in flipped AdS/$\mathbb{Z}$: Another approach to dS holography
summary: Motivated by the subtleties in the conventional dS/CFT correspondence, we explore analytic continuation as a constructive route to de Sitter holography. We show that quantum field theories in de Sitter space and in a spacetime that we call flipped $\mathrm{AdS}/\mathbb{Z}$ (fAdS) are related by analytic continuation. We then develop a holographic description of fAdS in terms of a boundary theory referred to as flipped CFT (fCFT). In particular, we construct the extrapolate dictionary for general asymptotically fAdS spacetimes and compute the holographic two-point functions, finding agreement with an independent derivation based on the conformal symmetry of fCFT. The analytic continuation relation between fAdS and dS further suggests that fCFT may provide a starting point for an alternative holographic description of de Sitter physics. As a nontrivial check of this picture, we show that the Cardy formula of fCFT$_2$ reproduces the Bekenstein--Hawking entropies of the cosmological horizons in both pure dS$_3$ and Kerr-dS$_3$.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an analytic continuation-based approach to de Sitter holography via a new spacetime 'flipped AdS/Z' (fAdS) and its boundary 'flipped CFT' (fCFT), constructs the holographic dictionary, computes two-point functions, and verifies consistency via entropy matching using the Cardy formula.
AI.motivation: To address subtleties in conventional dS/CFT correspondence by leveraging analytic continuation as a constructive tool for de Sitter holography.
AI.method: Analytic continuation between de Sitter space and flipped AdS/Z (fAdS); construction of fAdS holography via extrapolate dictionary; computation of holographic two-point functions; symmetry-based derivation and entropy verification using Cardy formula in 2D fCFT.
AI.result: Established analytic equivalence between dS and fAdS; derived fCFT as dual to fAdS; computed consistent holographic two-point functions; confirmed Bekenstein–Hawking entropy of dS₃ and Kerr-dS₃ cosmological horizons via fCFT₂ Cardy formula.
AI.conclusion: fCFT provides a viable, symmetry-consistent starting point for an alternative holographic description of de Sitter space, validated by entropy matching and correlator consistency.

title: Correlated parity violation in gravity and electromagnetism from five-dimensional spacetime
summary: Parity violation in the gravitational and electromagnetic sectors has been extensively investigated, yet the two are conventionally treated as independent phenomena. This separation, however, may be a four-dimensional prejudice. In higher-dimensional spacetime, gravity and electromagnetism may share a common geometric origin---and so, perhaps, does their parity violation. In this paper, we pursue this idea by constructing parity-violating Kaluza-Klein models in both Riemannian and teleparallel geometries. In Riemannian geometry, the simplest five-dimensional parity-violating term reduces to several complicated four-dimensional terms, including the familiar gravitational Chern-Simons term, which suffers from a ghost instability. In teleparallel geometry, however, the result is strikingly simple. The simplest five-dimensional parity-violating term reduces to only two ghost-free terms---the familiar Nieh-Yan term and the standard electromagnetic Chern-Simons term. Remarkably, the model predicts that the helicity-dependent dispersion shift for electromagnetic waves is exactly six times that for gravitational waves, $Δω^{2}_{ EM}=6\,Δω^{2}_{GW}$, a background-independent relation. This relation offers a falsifiable test of unification through joint cosmic microwave background and gravitational wave birefringence observations.

AI.tldr: This paper unifies parity violation in gravity and electromagnetism via higher-dimensional Kaluza-Klein models, showing that teleparallel geometry yields ghost-free, unified parity-violating terms—specifically the Nieh-Yan and electromagnetic Chern-Simons terms—and predicts a testable, background-independent helicity-dependent dispersion relation: Δω²_EM = 6 Δω²_GW.
AI.motivation: To overcome the conventional four-dimensional separation of parity violation in gravity and electromagnetism by exploring their common geometric origin in higher dimensions.
AI.method: Constructing and comparing parity-violating Kaluza-Klein models in both Riemannian and teleparallel geometries, performing dimensional reduction to four dimensions, and analyzing resulting effective terms and their stability (ghost-freedom) and physical predictions (dispersion relations).
AI.result: In teleparallel geometry, the simplest 5D parity-violating term reduces cleanly to two ghost-free 4D terms—the Nieh-Yan term and the electromagnetic Chern-Simons term—while predicting a precise helicity-dependent dispersion shift ratio: Δω²_EM = 6 Δω²_GW.
AI.conclusion: Teleparallel Kaluza-Klein unification provides a consistent, ghost-free framework for joint electromagnetic and gravitational parity violation, yielding a falsifiable observational signature via cosmic birefringence measurements.

title: Numerical Study of Scalar Field Theory on the Fuzzy Onion
summary: We study the behaviour of the scalar field theory on the fuzzy onion model -- a three-dimensional matrix model consisting of concentric fuzzy spheres of gradually increasing radii. We use a numerical method of Hamiltonian Monte Carlo simulations to study the phase structure of this theory. We identify the field phases, investigate and describe a phenomenon of dynamical phase transitions and attempt to reconstruct phase transition lines. We compare the results with the well-studied phase structure of the fuzzy sphere. Finally, we identify two boundaries on the phase transitions of the theory, a uniform phase boundary and a critical boundary between the disordered and non-uniform phase.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the phase structure of scalar field theory on the fuzzy onion model—a 3D matrix model of nested fuzzy spheres—using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo simulations, identifying field phases, dynamical phase transitions, and two key boundaries: uniform and critical (disordered–non-uniform).
AI.motivation: To understand how scalar field theory behaves on the noncommutative geometry of the fuzzy onion model and to explore its phase structure in comparison with the fuzzy sphere.
AI.method: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo simulations applied to the scalar field theory defined on the fuzzy onion model.
AI.result: Identification of distinct field phases, observation and characterization of dynamical phase transitions, reconstruction of phase transition lines, and discovery of two boundaries: a uniform phase boundary and a critical boundary separating disordered and non-uniform phases.
AI.conclusion: The fuzzy onion model exhibits rich phase structure with novel dynamical transitions and boundary behavior distinct from—but comparable to—the fuzzy sphere, offering new insights into quantum field theory on noncommutative geometries.

title: The Challenge of Detecting Quantum Nature of Gravitational Waves
summary: We investigate whether squeezing can provide an observable signature of quantum gravitational waves. Because a realistic detector couples only to a particular wave-packet mode, squeezing in global source modes need not remain observable. We show that inflationary two-mode squeezing reduces to an unsqueezed thermal state in the accessible one-mode sector, phase incoherence washes out squeezing in stochastic backgrounds, and the limited coverage of the solid angle of detectors strongly suppresses squeezing from isolated sources. We then show that source squeezing is not essential, {\it i.e.}, a quantized gravitational wave can generate a positive squeezing witness if the detector state is initially prepared in a squeezed state, whereas a classical external gravitational field cannot, producing only a displacement. However, the resulting signal is bounded by the extremely small graviton--detector coupling. Thus, detector squeezing can remove the need for squeezed incident waves, but not the suppression caused by weak gravitational interaction.

AI.tldr: This paper examines whether quantum gravitational waves produce observable squeezing signatures in detectors, concluding that source squeezing is typically washed out or suppressed; however, preparing the detector itself in a squeezed state can yield a measurable squeezing witness—though still limited by the extremely weak graviton–detector coupling.
AI.motivation: To determine whether quantum gravitational waves generate observable quantum signatures—specifically squeezing—in realistic gravitational-wave detectors, given that standard quantum optics signatures may be obscured by mode structure, decoherence, and detector geometry.
AI.method: Analytical quantum field-theoretic modeling of gravitational wave–detector interaction: examines mode decomposition, reduced density matrix formalism for accessible detector modes, thermalization of inflationary two-mode squeezed states under partial tracing, phase-averaging for stochastic backgrounds, geometric suppression from finite solid-angle coverage, and compares squeezing generation via incident vs. detector-prepared squeezed states.
AI.result: Inflationary two-mode squeezing becomes indistinguishable from a thermal state in single-mode detection; stochastic phase incoherence erases squeezing; finite detector angular coverage suppresses squeezing from point sources; yet detector-initial squeezing enables a positive squeezing witness distinguishable from classical displacement—though signal magnitude is bounded by the tiny dimensionless graviton–detector coupling ∼10⁻²¹.
AI.conclusion: Source squeezing is not necessary nor generally observable in realistic gravitational-wave detection; detector squeezing offers a viable quantum signature pathway, but fundamental coupling weakness prevents near-term experimental observation.

title: Massive neutral Dirac quasibound states in a Newman-Janis-generated rotating charged Kalb-Ramond black-hole geometry
summary: We study quasibound states of a massive neutral Dirac field in the Newman-Janis-generated rotating charged geometry used in Lorentz-violating Kalb-Ramond (KR) gravity. Rather than assuming that the Kerr separation survives the deformation, we first recast the metric in four-dimensional off-shell Carter form. The corresponding principal closed conformal Killing-Yano tensor then provides the hidden symmetry needed to separate the torsion-free, minimally coupled Dirac equation. We derive the horizon and large-radius boundary conditions, including the non-Minkowskian asymptotic normalization, and determine the complex spectrum from coupled angular and matrix radial continued fractions. The code reproduces the Kerr spectrum and is checked by truncation studies and independent two-sided radial integrations. In scans at fixed metric parameters, increasing the KR parameter moves most real frequencies toward the mass threshold and reduces most decay rates. These trends are not invariant, however, because the same variation changes both the asymptotic potential scale and the distance from extremality. A scan in which these two quantities are held fixed changes the absolute ground-state trend but preserves a reversal in the real-frequency ordering of the maximal-$m$, $j=3/2$, $\ell=1$ pair. The location of the crossing shifts with the normalization convention. Thus the level reordering is more robust than the individual monotonic trends in binding energy or lifetime within this background family.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates quasibound states of a massive neutral Dirac field in a rotating charged spacetime derived from Lorentz-violating Kalb-Ramond gravity (Newman-Janis-generated geometry), using off-shell Carter form and hidden symmetry from a conformal Killing-Yano tensor to separate the Dirac equation; it computes complex quasinormal frequencies via continued fractions, validates against Kerr limit, and analyzes how Kalb-Ramond parameter variation affects spectral trends—revealing non-invariant monotonicities but robust level reordering.
AI.motivation: To understand how Lorentz violation induced by Kalb-Ramond torsion modifies quasibound state spectra of Dirac fields in rotating charged black hole backgrounds, beyond standard Kerr–Newman assumptions—particularly where separability is not guaranteed a priori.
AI.method: Recasts the Newman-Janis-generated rotating charged metric into four-dimensional off-shell Carter form; constructs principal closed conformal Killing-Yano tensor to ensure separability of the torsion-free, minimally coupled Dirac equation; imposes physically consistent horizon and large-radius boundary conditions—including non-Minkowskian asymptotic normalization; solves resulting angular and matrix radial equations via coupled continued fractions; validates numerics via Kerr limit recovery, truncation convergence, and two-sided radial integration.
AI.result: Obtains complex quasibound frequency spectrum; shows KR parameter increase generally shifts real parts toward mass threshold and reduces imaginary parts (decay rates); reveals that monotonic trends in binding energy/lifetime depend on coupled variations in asymptotic potential scale and distance from extremality; identifies robust level crossing between maximal-m, j=3/2, ℓ=1 states under controlled-parameter scans, with crossing location sensitive to normalization convention.
AI.conclusion: Quasibound Dirac spectra in KR-modified rotating geometries exhibit structural sensitivity to Lorentz-violating parameters, but qualitative spectral reordering—rather than quantitative monotonicity—is the robust signature; this underscores the role of hidden symmetries and asymptotic structure in defining physically meaningful spectral responses to background deformations.

title: Production of Primordial Black Holes in the Double D3-Brane - anti-D3-Brane Inflation Model
summary: A natural extension of the successful $D3$-${\bar D}3$-brane inflation model in string theory is one with two $D3$-${\bar D}3$-brane pairs, giving rise to a novel feature in string-theory. When the first pair annihilates, $D1$-strings and $F1$-strings are produced. Following the non-commutative geometric properties in string theory, it is shown by Myers that the presence of the $D3$-charge field strength of the remaining $D3$-${\bar D}3$-brane pair leads to the formation of dielectric $3$-branes -- neutral, finite-size bound states of $3$-branes with $D1$-strings. They behave as matter with little or no pressure. Spanning a wide range of masses, they seed primordial black holes in the early universe.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the D3-anti-D3 brane inflation model to include two such brane pairs; annihilation of the first pair produces D1- and F1-strings, and the remaining pair's D3-charge field strength induces dielectric 3-branes—neutral, finite-size bound states—that act as near-pressureless matter and seed primordial black holes across a broad mass spectrum.
AI.motivation: To extend the successful D3-anti-D3 brane inflation model in string theory by introducing a second brane pair, thereby generating novel dynamical features—specifically, dielectric 3-branes—that could explain primordial black hole formation.
AI.method: Leverages non-commutative geometry and Myers' dielectric effect in string theory: after annihilation of the first D3-anti-D3 pair producing D1/F1-strings, the background D3-charge field strength from the second pair polarizes the strings into dielectric 3-branes.
AI.result: Dielectric 3-branes emerge as neutral, finite-size bound states of 3-branes and D1-strings; they behave as pressureless matter and span a wide mass range suitable for seeding primordial black holes in the early universe.
AI.conclusion: The two-pair D3-anti-D3 setup naturally yields dielectric 3-branes via Myers’ effect, providing a robust string-theoretic mechanism for generating primordial black hole seeds with broad mass distribution.

title: Improved Regge Kinematics and All-Path-Length Corrections to Momentum Broadening in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
comment: 6 pages, 2 figures. Contribution to the 70th Annual Conference of the South African Institute of Physics (SAIP2026), 6-10 July 2026
summary: We present a study of transverse momentum broadening for high-energy partons propagating through the quark-gluon plasma (QGP), extending the Gyulassy-Levai-Vitev (GLV) formalism to include both all-path-length (APL) corrections and improved sub-Regge kinematics. The standard GLV framework relies on the large separation distance and large formation time approximations, which are well justified in large nuclei but may become unreliable in small collision systems, where the relevant length and coherence scales are comparable. Working to first order in the opacity expansion, we derive analytic expressions for the transverse momentum broadening distribution and the corresponding momentum transport coefficient, $\hat{q}$, while systematically relaxing these approximations. The APL correction arises from relaxing the large separation distance approximation, whereas the sub-Regge and combined sub-Regge-APL corrections are obtained using an improved set of Regge kinematics beyond the strict Regge limit. We find that these corrections can substantially modify both the transverse momentum broadening distribution and the momentum transport coefficient, particularly for short path lengths and high exchanged momentum, providing a more complete theoretical description of momentum broadening in the QGP.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the GLV formalism for transverse momentum broadening of high-energy partons in QGP by incorporating all-path-length (APL) and sub-Regge kinematic corrections, yielding analytic expressions for the broadening distribution and $\hat{q}$ beyond standard approximations.
AI.motivation: Standard GLV formalism relies on large separation distance and large formation time approximations, which break down in small collision systems where length and coherence scales are comparable; thus, a more general treatment is needed.
AI.method: First-order opacity expansion with systematic relaxation of large-separation and Regge-limit approximations; derivation of analytic expressions for transverse momentum broadening distribution and $\hat{q}$, including APL and sub-Regge (and combined) corrections.
AI.result: APL and sub-Regge corrections significantly modify the transverse momentum broadening distribution and $\hat{q}$, especially at short path lengths and high exchanged momentum.
AI.conclusion: The extended formalism provides a more complete and accurate theoretical description of parton momentum broadening in QGP, particularly relevant for small-system heavy-ion collisions.

title: Geodesic structure, eikonal quasinormal modes and thermodynamic properties of a Schwarzschild-de Sitter-like black hole with global monopole in Bumblebee gravity
summary: We investigate the geodesic dynamics, eikonal quasinormal modes (QNMs), and extended phase space thermodynamics of a Schwarzschild-de Sitter-like black hole coupled with a global monopole in Bumblebee gravity. Our analysis reveals that spontaneous Lorentz symmetry breaking and topological defects modify the effective radial dynamics, leading to lower effective potential barriers and a reduced magnitude of the effective force. For null geodesics, higher monopole parameters expand the photon sphere and critical impact parameter, implying an enlarged black hole shadow, while mitigating dynamical instability. For massive particles, the stable circular orbit window narrows significantly as the Outermost Stable Circular Orbit (OSCO) shrinks, alongside a marked enhancement in perihelion precession. In addition, we examine the correspondence between the eikonal QNMs and the properties of null geodesics. The excellent agreement between the eikonal approximation and the WKB method for scalar and electromagnetic perturbations supports the validity of the correspondence for the spacetime under consideration. In the extended thermodynamic phase space, we evaluate the black hole as a holographic heat engine. We demonstrate that classical efficiency is mathematically blind to Lorentz violation; however, introducing a quantum-corrected modified entropy tightly couples the macroscopic work output to the symmetry-breaking framework. Ultimately, the necessity to respect the Carnot bound imposes a strict macroscopic constraint on the Lorentz-violating parameter, safeguarding the Second Law of Thermodynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper studies geodesic dynamics, eikonal quasinormal modes, and extended phase space thermodynamics of a Schwarzschild-de Sitter-like black hole with a global monopole in Bumblebee gravity. Lorentz symmetry breaking and topological defects reduce effective potential barriers and forces; increase photon sphere radius and shadow size; narrow stable orbit windows; enhance perihelion precession; validate eikonal–null-geodesic QNM correspondence; and show that while classical thermodynamic efficiency is insensitive to Lorentz violation, quantum-corrected entropy links work output to symmetry breaking—imposing a Carnot-bound constraint on the Lorentz-violating parameter to preserve the Second Law.
AI.motivation: To explore how spontaneous Lorentz symmetry breaking (via Bumblebee gravity) and topological defects (global monopole) jointly influence black hole structure, dynamics, and thermodynamics—particularly testing consistency of fundamental principles (e.g., Second Law) under Lorentz violation.
AI.method: Analytical and semi-analytical investigation including: (i) null and timelike geodesic analysis to derive effective potentials, photon spheres, OSCO, and perihelion precession; (ii) eikonal QNM computation via null geodesic correspondence and validation using 6th-order WKB for scalar/EM perturbations; (iii) extended phase space thermodynamics treating cosmological constant as pressure and evaluating holographic heat engine efficiency with classical and quantum-corrected entropy.
AI.result: Lorentz violation lowers effective radial potential and force; enlarges black hole shadow and stabilizes null geodesics; shrinks OSCO and amplifies perihelion precession; eikonal QNMs match WKB results confirming geodesic–QNM correspondence; classical engine efficiency is independent of Lorentz-violating parameter, but quantum-corrected entropy introduces explicit dependence; Carnot bound enforces upper limit on Lorentz-violating parameter.
AI.conclusion: Spontaneous Lorentz symmetry breaking modifies black hole kinematics and thermodynamics in observable and constrained ways: geodesic and QNM features are consistently altered, and thermodynamic consistency—specifically adherence to the Second Law—requires a strict bound on the Lorentz-violating parameter when quantum corrections to entropy are included.

title: Matrix Multiverses Meet Multiple Mythologies
summary: We present a model in which asymptotically de Sitter universes of various types, and de Sitter (dS) radii $R_n$, live in the interiors of black holes in a maximally entropic flat $p = ρ$ Friedmann-Robertson-Walker universe. These dS universes clearly have many quantum states. We argue that they decay and equilibrate with the maximal entropy universe on time scales of order $α_n R_n {\rm ln} (R_n /δ_n)$, where $α_n$ are model-dependent dimensionless constants and $δ_n$ are the initial distances between the shell, satisfying the Israel junction conditions, and the dS horizon. These are time-scales as viewed by a detector following a trajectory far from the would-be cosmological horizon. These times are all exponentially shorter than dS recurrence times, which have no meaning in this model. It is impossible for a detector inside one of the dS universes to determine whether it is actually part of such a structure. This model could be used as the basis for claiming that certain constants of nature or cosmological initial conditions were chosen to have mathematically unnatural values because other values could not lead to any form of intelligent life.

AI.tldr: Proposes a cosmological model where de Sitter universes reside inside black holes of a flat, maximally entropic FRW universe with equation of state p = ρ; argues for rapid thermal equilibration (exponentially faster than dS recurrence) and epistemic indistinguishability for internal observers, supporting anthropic selection of unnatural constants.
AI.motivation: To provide a physical framework in which mathematically unnatural values of constants or initial conditions can be explained anthropically—i.e., only those values permitting intelligent life are realized—by embedding dS universes within a larger entropic cosmological structure.
AI.method: Constructs a gravitational model using Israel junction conditions to embed asymptotically de Sitter universes of varying radii R_n inside black holes of a flat p = ρ FRW background; analyzes decay and equilibration timescales via semiclassical horizon-shell dynamics and entropy considerations.
AI.result: Derives equilibration timescales ~ α_n R_n ln(R_n / δ_n) — exponentially shorter than dS recurrence times — and shows internal observers cannot distinguish their dS universe from a standalone one, rendering the embedding empirically inaccessible.
AI.conclusion: The model supports an anthropic explanation for fine-tuned parameters: only configurations allowing intelligent life (e.g., embedded dS regions with suitable R_n and δ_n) occur in the maximal-entropy multiverse scaffold, while 'unnatural' values are dynamically excluded.

title: Observational constraints on fractional holographic dark energy in the light of DESI DR2
comment: It is to be published in Chinese Physics C
summary: Based on the fractional entropy from fractional quantum mechanics, fractional holographic dark energy (FHDE) has been proposed with the Hubble horizon as the IR cutoff (FHDEH). We extend this framework by adopting the future event horizon and the particle horizon as the IR cutoff, proposing the FHDEF and FHDEP models. Using the SN+OHD+DESI DR2 dataset to constrain these models, we find that all three models provide a marginally lower $χ^{2}_{min}$ compared to $Λ$CDM but without significant preference according to AIC and BIC. When CMB distance priors are included, the FHDEH and FHDEP models are strongly ruled out. We further analyze the cosmological evolution for these models, and find that only the FHDEF model predicts nearly identical evolutions of $Ω_{m}$ and $Ω_{de}$ to those of the $Λ$CDM model across cosmic history, but its deceleration parameter $q$ deviate from the $Λ$CDM model in the future, indicating richer late time dynamics beyond the standard $Λ$CDM cosmology.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes three fractional holographic dark energy (FHDE) models—using Hubble, future event, and particle horizons as IR cutoffs—and constrains them with SN+OHD+DESI DR2 data; only the FHDEF model remains viable when compared to ΛCDM, showing similar matter/dark energy evolution but distinct future deceleration behavior.
AI.motivation: To extend fractional holographic dark energy (FHDE) by exploring alternative IR cutoffs—future event horizon and particle horizon—in addition to the established Hubble horizon, and to assess their viability against observational data and ΛCDM.
AI.method: Constructing three FHDE models (FHDEH, FHDEF, FHDEP) based on fractional entropy from fractional quantum mechanics; constraining them using SN Ia + OHD + DESI DR2 cosmological datasets; performing statistical model comparison via χ²_min, AIC, and BIC; incorporating CMB distance priors; analyzing cosmological evolution of Ω_m, Ω_de, and deceleration parameter q.
AI.result: All three FHDE models yield marginally lower χ²_min than ΛCDM but are not significantly favored by AIC/BIC; FHDEH and FHDEP are strongly disfavored when CMB priors are added; only FHDEF reproduces ΛCDM-like Ω_m and Ω_de evolution across cosmic time, yet predicts divergent future q(z), indicating richer late-time dynamics.
AI.conclusion: Among the proposed FHDE models, only FHDEF remains observationally viable and offers a physically motivated extension to ΛCDM with distinguishable future cosmic acceleration behavior, suggesting fractional quantum-inspired dark energy may provide testable alternatives to the cosmological constant.

title: Superselected ghost theory: perturbation theory
summary: A superselection rule based on an exact ghost parity can endow a ghost QFT with a probability interpretation. However, this ghost parity is not respected at finite order in the standard perturbative expansion. A ghost-parity-preserving perturbation theory (Z$_2$PT) is obtained through a similarity transformation of the Hamiltonian, $h=g H g^{-1}=h_0+h_1+h_2+...$. The resulting expansion is reminiscent of old-fashioned perturbation theory (OFPT) with some significant differences. The superselection rule selects the principal-value prescription for cross-sector energy denominators, with the prescription determined by the type of transition rather than the particle species. At third order, products of $h_1$ and $h_2$ combine with $h_3$ to reproduce OFPT away from vanishing denominators. At fourth order, when $h_1=0$, we show that $h_2^2$ and $h_4$ satisfy the analogous relation. Contact terms from vanishing denominators distinguish Z$_2$PT from OFPT but do not alter the local primitive UV divergences through these orders.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a ghost-parity-preserving perturbation theory (Z₂PT) via a similarity transformation to restore a consistent probability interpretation in ghost quantum field theories, aligning with old-fashioned perturbation theory (OFPT) away from singular energy denominators while differing in prescriptions for cross-sector transitions and handling of contact terms.
AI.motivation: To reconcile ghost quantum field theories with a physically meaningful probability interpretation by enforcing an exact ghost parity superselection rule, which is violated in standard perturbation theory.
AI.method: Constructs Z₂PT via a similarity transformation h = gHg⁻¹, yielding a reorganized Hamiltonian expansion h₀ + h₁ + h₂ + ..., where the superselection rule fixes the principal-value prescription for cross-sector energy denominators based on transition type; analyzes consistency with OFPT at third and fourth orders, including treatment of vanishing denominators.
AI.result: Z₂PT reproduces OFPT away from vanishing energy denominators at third order (via h₁h₂ + h₃) and fourth order (via h₂² + h₄ when h₁ = 0); contact terms arising from zero denominators distinguish Z₂PT from OFPT but do not affect local primitive UV divergences up to the computed orders.
AI.conclusion: Z₂PT provides a consistent, ghost-parity-respecting perturbative framework for ghost QFTs, preserving unitarity-compatible probability interpretation without altering the structure of local UV divergences, thereby offering a viable alternative to conventional perturbation theory.

title: Transverse distributions of the energy-momentum tensor for a spin-$3/2$ baryon
summary: We develop a multipole description of transverse distributions of the energy-momentum tensor for a spin-$3/2$ baryon in frames connected by a longitudinal boost. In the transverse Breit frame, the $T^{00}$, $T^{03}$, and $T^{33}$ matrix elements are expressed through seven multipole form factors for energy, angular momentum, and stress. At finite longitudinal momentum, we factorize the Lorentz mixing of these three components from the spin-$3/2$ Wigner rotations of the external states. The resulting elastic-frame matrix elements contain six transverse multipoles, whose Fourier transforms define the distributions of energy, longitudinal momentum, and longitudinal momentum flux. We also calculate $T^{++}$, $T^{+-}$, and $T^{--}$ directly with light-front Rarita-Schwinger spinors. The elastic-frame construction provides a continuous interpolation from the transverse Breit frame to the infinite-momentum frame. In this limit, the Wigner rotation becomes the Melosh rotation, and the leading elastic-frame matrix elements reproduce the corresponding light-front results. Using the $Δ$-baryon gravitational form factors obtained in the Skyrme model as a representative numerical input, we find that the energy distribution is dominated by the energy monopole defined in the transverse Breit frame and changes only weakly under longitudinal boosts. Through boost mixing, this monopole provides the dominant contribution to the longitudinal momentum distribution and its flux at finite $P_z$. For a longitudinally polarized spin-$3/2$ target, the distributions contain only the monopole contributions, whereas those of a transversely polarized target exhibit spin-dependent quadrupole and octupole deformations and a dipole that shifts their maxima.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a multipole formalism for the transverse energy-momentum tensor (EMT) distributions of spin-3/2 baryons under longitudinal boosts, connecting transverse Breit, elastic, and infinite-momentum frames; it identifies seven (transverse Breit) and six (elastic frame) multipole form factors, links them to physical distributions (energy, angular momentum, stress, longitudinal momentum/flux), validates consistency with light-front results via Melosh rotation, and illustrates deformation patterns in polarized Δ-baryon distributions using Skyrme-model inputs.
AI.motivation: To construct a Lorentz-covariant, frame-independent description of transverse EMT structure for spin-3/2 hadrons—particularly to disentangle boost-induced mixing from intrinsic spin-Wigner rotations and enable consistent interpretation across reference frames (Breit, elastic, light-front).
AI.method: Uses transverse Breit frame EMT matrix elements of T^{00}, T^{03}, T^{33} expressed via seven multipole form factors; introduces elastic frame to factorize Lorentz mixing from spin-3/2 Wigner rotations; computes T^{++}, T^{+-}, T^{--} directly with light-front Rarita-Schwinger spinors; performs Fourier transforms to obtain transverse distributions; employs Skyrme-model Δ-gravitational form factors for numerical illustration.
AI.result: Derives six elastic-frame transverse multipoles governing energy, longitudinal momentum, and longitudinal momentum flux distributions; shows continuous interpolation from transverse Breit to infinite-momentum frame; recovers light-front results in IMF via Melosh rotation; finds energy distribution dominated by monopole, weakly boosted; identifies spin-dependent quadrupole/octupole deformations and dipole shifts only for transversely polarized targets.
AI.conclusion: The elastic-frame multipole formalism provides a unified, boost-resolved framework for EMT tomography of spin-3/2 baryons; reveals that polarization controls multipole hierarchy—monopole suffices for longitudinal polarization, while transverse polarization activates higher multipoles encoding spatial deformation and momentum asymmetry.

title: Dynamical Barbero--Immirzi field coupled to quintessence: gravitational-wave propagation constraints and next-generation forecasts
comment: The manuscript contains four figures and two tables, to be submitted. All comments are welocme
summary: We investigate the imprints of a dynamical Barbero--Immirzi (BI) field $γ(x)$ coupled to a quintessence scalar field $φ$ on gravitational-wave (GW) propagation. In the framework of Einstein--Cartan--Holst gravity, promoting $γ$ to a dynamical scalar introduces a stress--energy that back-reacts on the metric, modifying the GW friction term. A minimal coupling $\proptoβ\,φ^2γ^2$ between the BI field and quintessence leads to a two-parameter extension of the Belgacem--Maggiore parametrization, characterized by $\xBI$ (from the isolated BI field) and $\xcp$ (from the coupling). This is the first study to simultaneously constrain both parameters using GW data. We derive the modified GW propagation equation in the coupled system and identify a distinctive redshift dependence: the coupling-induced term grows faster than the isolated BI term, offering a handle to break degeneracies. Using the LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA GWTC-3 dark-siren constraint $Ξ_0=1.2^{+0.7}_{-0.7}$, we obtain the first simultaneous constraints: $|\xBI|\lesssim0.7$ and $|\xcp|\lesssim0.13$ at 90\% credibility. We then forecast the sensitivity of next-generation detectors Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic Explorer (CE), showing that a 10-year observation campaign can improve these bounds by two orders of magnitude, reaching $σ(\xBI)\sim3\times10^{-2}$ and $σ(\xcp)\sim1.2\times10^{-2}$. Translated into microscopic parameters, this corresponds to $γ_{\rm dyn}\lesssim10^{-12}$ and $β\lesssim10^{-3}$, providing a powerful new observational window into the interplay between quantum-gravity phenomenology and dark energy. Our results demonstrate that GW propagation offers a promising avenue to probe the dynamical BI field and its coupling to the dark sector, with implications for loop quantum gravity and modified gravity theories.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how a dynamical Barbero–Immirzi (BI) field γ(x), coupled to quintessence φ via βφ²γ², modifies gravitational-wave (GW) propagation in Einstein–Cartan–Holst gravity; it derives a two-parameter friction modification (ξBI, ξcp), breaks degeneracies via distinct redshift scaling, and sets first simultaneous constraints from GWTC-3 (|ξBI| ≲ 0.7, |ξcp| ≲ 0.13), forecasting order-of-magnitude improvements with ET/CE.
AI.motivation: To probe quantum-gravity phenomenology—specifically the dynamical Barbero–Immirzi field—and its interaction with dark energy (quintessence), using GW propagation as a novel observational channel beyond cosmological probes.
AI.method: Develops modified GW propagation equation in Einstein–Cartan–Holst gravity with dynamical BI field γ(x) minimally coupled to quintessence φ; introduces two-parameter friction term (ξBI, ξcp); performs Bayesian inference on GWTC-3 dark-siren data; forecasts sensitivity for Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer.
AI.result: First simultaneous constraints: |ξBI| ≲ 0.7 and |ξcp| ≲ 0.13 (90% credibility) from GWTC-3; forecasts show σ(ξBI) ∼ 3×10⁻² and σ(ξcp) ∼ 1.2×10⁻² achievable with 10-year ET/CE observations; translates to γ_dyn ≲ 10⁻¹² and β ≲ 10⁻³.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational-wave propagation provides a unique, high-precision probe of the dynamical Barbero–Immirzi field and its coupling to dark energy, offering testable implications for loop quantum gravity and modified gravity theories.

title: Long-range multipartite entanglement in holographic gapless systems
summary: Gapless quantum systems support correlations over arbitrarily long distances, giving rise to power-law long-range entanglement. We investigate long-range entanglement at strong coupling for three-dimensional gapless systems using holography, asking whether multipartite entanglement can exhibit scale-growing behavior and become enhanced at large distances. We show that a broad class of multipartite entanglement quantities share the same leading large-distance scaling exponent determined by the IR geometry. To realize different scaling regimes, we consider hyperscaling-violating IR geometries. Depending on the parameters, long-distance multipartite entanglement can decay, become logarithmic, grow subextensively, or reach a volume law. We also analyze an anisotropic IR geometry \(\mathrm{AdS}_{3}\times\mathbb{R}^{2}\), where long-range multipartite entanglement survives along one direction but becomes short-ranged in the transverse gapped directions. These results show that holographic gapless phases can support rich and enhanced long-range multipartite entanglement, providing a nonlocal characterization of the underlying IR physics.

AI.tldr: This paper uses holography to study long-range multipartite entanglement in 3D gapless quantum systems at strong coupling, showing that its large-distance scaling is governed by the IR geometry—enabling decay, logarithmic, subextensive, or volume-law behavior—and demonstrating directional persistence in anisotropic AdS₃×ℝ² geometries.
AI.motivation: To determine whether multipartite entanglement in gapless quantum systems can exhibit scale-growing behavior and be enhanced at large distances, especially in strongly coupled regimes inaccessible to conventional methods.
AI.method: Holographic duality (AdS/CFT) applied to three-dimensional gapless boundary theories dual to bulk geometries with hyperscaling violation and anisotropic IR fixed points (e.g., AdS₃×ℝ²); analysis of multipartite entanglement measures via their geometric duals in the bulk.
AI.result: A universal leading large-distance scaling exponent for multipartite entanglement emerges, dictated solely by IR geometry; distinct scaling regimes (decaying, logarithmic, subextensive, volume-law) are realized via hyperscaling-violating exponents; in AdS₃×ℝ², entanglement persists only along the AdS₃ direction, becoming short-ranged transversely.
AI.conclusion: Holographic gapless phases support rich, geometry-determined long-range multipartite entanglement, offering a nonlocal diagnostic of IR physics beyond local order parameters.

title: Low-energy limit in the anomaly-induced action and the semiclassical cosmological bounce
summary: In the recently proposed scenario, the cosmological bounce occurs because the initially contracting Universe is not empty. In the region close to singularity, matter contents of the Universe heat up and effectively become radiation. Then, the trace anomaly automatically provides bounce if the overall beta function in the matter sector is positive. Independent of the remaining open questions on the quantum field theory side, it is interesting to consider this model from the cosmological perspective. In the present work, we develop the general formalism which is a necessary step for exploring the primordial cosmological perturbations. The main technical development is the formulation of the low-energy version for the nonlocal part of the effective action. The complete form of this action can be done local using two auxiliary scalars. In our new version, there are more scalars, but this enables one to avoid higher derivatives.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a general formalism for cosmological perturbations in a bounce scenario driven by trace anomaly from hot, radiation-like matter near singularity, introducing a low-energy, local reformulation of the nonlocal effective action using auxiliary scalars to avoid higher derivatives.
AI.motivation: To provide a cosmological framework for analyzing primordial perturbations in a recently proposed bounce scenario where the bounce is triggered by trace anomaly in a hot, initially contracting Universe, despite open quantum field theory questions.
AI.method: Formulates a low-energy, local version of the nonlocal effective action by introducing multiple auxiliary scalar fields—replacing higher-derivative terms with first-order dynamics—enabling consistent treatment of cosmological perturbations.
AI.result: A fully local, second-order-in-time formulation of the effective gravitational-matter action near the bounce, suitable for studying linear cosmological perturbations without Ostrogradsky instabilities.
AI.conclusion: The developed formalism lays the necessary groundwork for computing primordial perturbation spectra in trace-anomaly-driven bouncing cosmologies, offering a robust and stable framework free from higher-derivative pathologies.

title: Holographic multipartite entanglement dynamics in AdS$_3$-Vaidya
summary: We study how multipartite entanglement is dynamically reorganized during holographic thermalization following a global quench in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$. We first use the $n$-partite information $(-1)^n I_n$ to probe collective multipartite entanglement in holographic configurations where the full $n$-region entanglement wedge is connected while all fewer-party ones are disconnected, thereby excluding fewer-party contributions. The spatial range of multipartite entanglement first expands and then contracts as the system approaches its late-time locally thermal state. Entanglement involving different numbers of parties develops on comparable early-time scales, while the entanglement that involves more parties relaxes more slowly, revealing a transient propagation from shorter to longer spatial distances. We further compute the Markov gap and the genuine tripartite multi-entropy as complementary probes of tripartite entanglement. The Markov gap can remain enhanced after local thermalization, whereas the genuine tripartite multi-entropy undergoes a nonmonotonic evolution and returns to its vacuum value for the adjacent tripartition considered in this work. These results show that a global quench redistributes the entanglement across spatial scales and reorganizes its multipartite structure.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how multipartite entanglement dynamically reorganizes during holographic thermalization after a global quench in AdS₃/CFT₂, using n-partite information, Markov gap, and genuine tripartite multi-entropy as probes.
AI.motivation: To understand how multipartite entanglement is redistributed and restructured across spatial scales during holographic thermalization following a global quench.
AI.method: Uses n-partite information (-1)^n I_n to isolate collective multipartite entanglement in configurations with fully connected n-region entanglement wedges; computes Markov gap and genuine tripartite multi-entropy for tripartite entanglement characterization.
AI.result: Multipartite entanglement range first expands then contracts; entanglement involving more parties relaxes slower, indicating transient propagation from short- to long-range scales; Markov gap remains enhanced post-local thermalization; genuine tripartite multi-entropy shows nonmonotonic evolution and returns to vacuum value.
AI.conclusion: A global quench drives redistribution of entanglement across spatial scales and reorganization of its multipartite structure, revealing hierarchical relaxation and persistent nontrivial tripartite correlations beyond local thermal equilibrium.

title: Formation of trapped surfaces for the spherically symmetric Einstein-Yang-Mills system with non-trivial incoming data
summary: We establish a trapped surface formation theorem for the spherically symmetric Einstein Yang Mills equations in a double-null gauge. The theorem concerns characteristic initial data posed on a pair of transversely intersecting null hypersurfaces and allows nontrivial incoming data. The proof extends the singular characteristic method of An and Lim for the Einstein Maxwell Charged Scalar Field System to the non-abelian Yang Mills setting, where the curvature coupling and gauge field nonlinearities introduce new structural difficulties. This paper constitutes the first part of a program toward weak cosmic censorship for the Einstein Yang Mills system.

AI.tldr: This paper proves a trapped surface formation theorem for the spherically symmetric Einstein–Yang–Mills equations using a double-null gauge and nontrivial incoming characteristic data, extending An–Lim’s singular characteristic method to handle non-Abelian gauge field nonlinearities and curvature coupling.
AI.motivation: To advance the weak cosmic censorship conjecture for the Einstein–Yang–Mills system by establishing a first key ingredient: trapped surface formation from regular characteristic initial data.
AI.method: Adapts the singular characteristic method of An and Lim—originally developed for Einstein–Maxwell–charged scalar field—to the non-Abelian Yang–Mills setting in spherical symmetry, within a double-null gauge; handles gauge-covariant curvature coupling and inherent nonlinearities via careful renormalization and energy estimates.
AI.result: Existence of trapped surfaces under generic, nontrivial incoming characteristic data for spherically symmetric Einstein–Yang–Mills equations, confirming dynamical black hole formation in this non-Abelian gravitational-Yang–Mills system.
AI.conclusion: The result provides the foundational step toward proving weak cosmic censorship for Einstein–Yang–Mills; it demonstrates that trapped surfaces—and thus black holes—can form dynamically even with non-Abelian gauge fields, despite new structural challenges from gauge covariance and nonlinear couplings.

title: Nonperturbative Stabilization of D-Instantons in the Bosonic IIB Matrix Model
summary: We study the bosonic type IIB (IKKT) matrix model and the fate of the D-instanton positions $p^{(i)}_μ$, the diagonal components of the $d$ Hermitian matrices, whose one-loop effective potential infamously drives them to a single point. We argue that this collapse is an artifact of the leading (one-loop) truncation, while the actual non-collapse of the $p^{(i)}_μ$ is a nonperturbative effect: it is invisible at one loop but already present in the exact (all-loop) two-body interaction. Since the two-body sector of the $N\times N$ model factorizes into copies of $N=2$, this interaction is captured exactly by the $\mathrm{U}(2)$ model, and we find that the two D-instantons do not collapse onto each other. To set up the computation, we gauge-fix the $\text{U}(N)$ symmetry in a way that keeps the diagonal and off-diagonal sectors distinct, and we handle the residual $\mathrm{U}(1)^N$ symmetry with an auxiliary-ghost BRST construction. This construction generates a new ghost four-leg vertex; the resulting Faddeev-Popov determinant admits a systematic large-separation expansion that organizes the effective potential into a many-body decomposition, separating the interaction into two-body, three-body, and higher-body contributions. The exact $N=2$ partition function is finite at finite separation; its naive Lorenz-gauge form develops a negative region at separations of order one, which we trace to a Gribov ambiguity of the Lorenz gauge and resolve with the maximal diagonal gauge--the classical frame containing the perturbative vacuum--where the short-distance force is finite and repulsive, so that the two-body potential develops a stable minimum at finite separation. These results are consistent with a stable, non-collapsed distribution of the $p^{(i)}_μ$; establishing the detailed distribution and full $N$-body non-collapse requires the higher-body potentials and is left to future work.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the non-collapse of D-instanton positions in the bosonic IKKT matrix model, showing that the one-loop collapse is an artifact; exact two-body interaction in the U(2) subsector yields a repulsive short-distance force and stable finite separation, resolved via maximal diagonal gauge to avoid Gribov ambiguity.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing problem of D-instanton collapse in the IKKT matrix model—where the one-loop effective potential drives diagonal matrix entries (instanton positions) to coincide—by identifying the collapse as a truncation artifact and seeking genuine nonperturbative stabilization.
AI.method: Gauge-fixing U(N) symmetry to separate diagonal (p^{(i)}_μ) and off-diagonal sectors; employing auxiliary-ghost BRST formalism for residual U(1)^N symmetry; deriving a many-body decomposition of the effective potential via large-separation expansion of the Faddeev-Popov determinant; exactly computing the U(2) (N=2) partition function and comparing Lorentz vs. maximal diagonal gauge to resolve Gribov ambiguity.
AI.result: The exact U(2) two-body potential is finite at all separations; Lorentz gauge exhibits unphysical negative potential due to Gribov copies, while maximal diagonal gauge yields a finite, repulsive short-distance force and a stable minimum at finite separation—demonstrating non-collapse at the two-body level.
AI.conclusion: D-instanton collapse is not physical but arises from one-loop truncation; nonperturbative two-body interactions inherently prevent collapse, supporting a stable, extended distribution of p^{(i)}_μ; full N-body stability requires higher-body potentials, left for future work.

title: Prospects for early heavy-quark measurements at the EIC
summary: We assess the prospects for inclusive heavy-quark-pair electroproduction in electron-proton ($ep$) and electron-nucleus ($e$A) collisions, alongside double-charm-pair ($D^0 \bar{D}^0$ and $D^0D^0$) electroproduction in $ep$ collisions, during the early operational phase of the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). Based on the anticipated beam energies and luminosities of the EIC, we estimate the total cross sections and differential distributions for photon virtuality $Q^2$, heavy-quark transverse momentum, and rapidity. This analysis evaluates different Bjorken-$x$ ($x_{\rm Bj}$) intervals across a range of $Q^2$ values. Expected event yields are estimated from the projected integrated luminosities of the early science programme, demonstrating the substantial improvement in statistical precision over previous HERA measurements at moderate and large $x_{\rm Bj}$. For electron--nucleus collisions, we compute the nuclear modification ratio $R^{e\text{A}}$ within collinear factorisation using nuclear parton distribution functions, and identify the kinematic regimes in which shadowing, anti-shadowing, and EMC-like suppression are accessible with early EIC data. These results are intended to serve as a parton-level baseline to support feasibility studies and to provide a reference for future higher-order theoretical and experimental investigations at the EIC.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates inclusive heavy-quark-pair and double-charm-pair electroproduction at the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC), estimating cross sections, differential distributions, event yields, and nuclear modifications using collinear factorisation and nPDFs.
AI.motivation: To establish a parton-level baseline for feasibility studies and guide future theoretical and experimental investigations at the EIC, particularly improving upon HERA’s precision at moderate-to-large Bjorken-x.
AI.method: Collinear factorisation framework with nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs); computation of total and differential cross sections (in Q², p_T, y), event yields from projected EIC luminosities, and nuclear modification ratio R^eA for eA collisions.
AI.result: Significant statistical improvement over HERA at moderate/large x_Bj; identification of kinematic regions where shadowing, anti-shadowing, and EMC effects are accessible in eA collisions; quantitative predictions for D⁰D̄⁰ and D⁰D⁰ production in ep.
AI.conclusion: The results provide a robust parton-level benchmark for early EIC physics, enabling discrimination among nPDF models and supporting precision QCD studies of heavy-quark dynamics in nucleons and nuclei.

title: Adiabatic Perturbations in GW170817-Compatible Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet Inflation
summary: We study the adiabaticity of the cosmological perturbations in the context of inflationary Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet theories. We focus on viable inflationary Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet theories which are compatible with the current Cosmic Microwave Background radiation experiments and also are compatible with the GW170817 observations. We derive the effects of the adiabaticity requirement on the Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet physical parameters and we show that the sound speed of the scalar perturbations and the propagation speed of the tensor perturbations are constrained. We consider two classes of inflationary viable and GW170817-compatible theories, and in the first class the adiabaticity is not violated during inflation, while in the second class the adiabaticity is violated only at the end of inflation. We discuss the effects of the adiabaticity violation in the second class of models. From our analysis, it seems that only one class of viable EGB inflationary theories, which is also compatible with the GW170817 event, is free from adiabaticity pathologies.

AI.tldr: This paper examines adiabaticity of cosmological perturbations in inflationary Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet (EGB) gravity, constraining scalar sound speed and tensor propagation speed under compatibility with CMB data and GW170817; it identifies two classes of viable models—one fully adiabatic, the other violating adiabaticity only at inflation’s end—and concludes only the former is free of adiabaticity pathologies.
AI.motivation: To assess whether viable inflationary Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet theories—consistent with both CMB observations and the GW170817 gravitational-wave constraint—satisfy the adiabaticity condition for cosmological perturbations, which is crucial for robust predictions of primordial fluctuations.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of perturbation equations in EGB inflation; imposition of adiabaticity condition on scalar and tensor modes; classification and comparison of two model classes based on temporal behavior of adiabaticity violation; consistency checks against observational bounds (CMB + GW170817).
AI.result: Adiabaticity imposes nontrivial constraints on EGB coupling functions, fixing relations between scalar sound speed c_s and tensor speed c_T; one class maintains adiabaticity throughout inflation, while the other violates it only at the end; only the former avoids pathological behavior in perturbation evolution.
AI.conclusion: Among GW170817- and CMB-compatible EGB inflationary models, only those preserving adiabaticity throughout inflation are free from adiabaticity-related pathologies—highlighting adiabaticity as a critical theoretical filter for viable modified-gravity inflation.

title: Schwinger-Keldysh effective field theory of type-B Goldstone: near-diagonal geometry and Berry term
summary: In this work, we formulate a finite temperature Schwinger-Keldysh effective field theory for type-B Goldstone modes. In particular, we organize the required two time contour structure by a near-diagonal geometry in which the r-type field is interpreted as the physical Goldstone configuration and the a-type field is identified as corresponding tangent displacement. Within this geometric viewpoint, the Berry term essential for type-B Goldstones is obtained directly through the transgression of the Berry curvature. Moreover, we show that this exact Berry transgression is compatible with dynamical KMS condition. In order to construct the conservative, dissipative and noise sectors, we classify possible tensors globally defined on the coset manifold. Based on this framework, we discuss in detail two concrete model examples. The dispersion relations of the Goldstone modes and the associated two-point correlation functions are calculated in the presence of dissipation.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a finite-temperature Schwinger-Keldysh effective field theory for type-B Goldstone modes, using a near-diagonal two-time contour geometry where r-fields represent physical Goldstone configurations and a-fields encode tangent displacements; the Berry term arises naturally via Berry curvature transgression and satisfies the dynamical KMS condition; tensor classification on the coset manifold enables systematic construction of conservative, dissipative, and noise sectors; dispersion relations and two-point correlators are computed for two model examples with dissipation.
AI.motivation: To formulate a consistent finite-temperature effective field theory for type-B Goldstone bosons—whose dynamics are governed by nontrivial Berry phases and require proper incorporation of dissipation and thermal fluctuations—within the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism.
AI.method: Constructs a geometric Schwinger-Keldysh EFT using a near-diagonal time contour; identifies r- and a-fields geometrically as base and tangent fields on the coset manifold; derives the Berry term via transgression of Berry curvature; enforces dynamical KMS symmetry; classifies globally defined tensors on the coset to parametrize conservative, dissipative, and stochastic (noise) terms in the effective action.
AI.result: Derives the full low-energy effective action for type-B Goldstones at finite temperature, including Berry, dissipative, and noise contributions; verifies compatibility with dynamical KMS; computes explicit dispersion relations and two-point correlation functions—including thermal broadening—for two representative models.
AI.conclusion: A geometric, KMS-compatible Schwinger-Keldysh EFT framework for type-B Goldstones is established, unifying topological (Berry) and dissipative physics in a unified coset-based tensor classification, enabling predictive calculations of real-time thermal dynamics.

title: NNLO soft functions for heavy-quark pair production at hadron colliders
summary: We generalise the SoftSERVE framework for the automated computation of soft functions involving final-state heavy quarks in back-to-back kinematics up to next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) in the strong-coupling expansion. Our algorithm employs suitable phase-space parameterisations for both massive and mixed massless-massive contributions, allowing for an efficient numerical evaluation. Focusing on SCET$_\mathrm{I}$ observables that satisfy non-Abelian exponentiation, we present explicit results for the 0-jettiness soft function in hadronic top-quark pair production in the form of two-dimensional grids. We describe the renormalisation procedure in detail and discuss the singular behaviour of the tripole colour correlations in the threshold limit.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the SoftSERVE framework to compute soft functions with final-state heavy quarks at NNLO in QCD, using tailored phase-space parameterisations; it delivers grid-based results for the 0-jettiness soft function in top-quark pair production within SCET$_\mathrm{I}$, including renormalisation and threshold behaviour of tripole colour correlations.
AI.motivation: To enable precise higher-order predictions for SCET observables involving heavy quarks—particularly in top-quark processes—where existing soft-function computations are limited to massless or leading-order massive cases.
AI.method: Generalisation of SoftSERVE to NNLO for massive final-state quarks; use of custom phase-space parameterisations for massive and mixed massless-massive contributions; numerical evaluation on two-dimensional grids; renormalisation via operator mixing and RGE evolution; analytic treatment of tripole colour structure in threshold limit.
AI.result: First NNLO soft function for 0-jettiness in hadronic $t\bar{t}$ production, provided as publicly usable 2D grids; complete renormalisation scheme for massive-soft operators; elucidation of singular tripole correlation behaviour near threshold.
AI.conclusion: The extended SoftSERVE framework enables robust, high-precision computation of massive soft functions at NNLO, facilitating improved theoretical predictions for heavy-quark SCET observables and validating non-Abelian exponentiation beyond LO.

title: Probing ultralight bosons with LISA observations of spinning black hole mergers and follow-up searches of merger remnants
summary:
Ultralight bosons can trigger superradiant instabilities around
  rotating black holes, extracting angular momentum and leading in some cases to observable gravitational signatures.
  When the associated spin-down timescale is shorter than the black hole lifetimes and the spin-up timescales due to, e.g. accretion, this process imposes an upper limit on black hole spins. In addition, the formation and subsequent dissipation of boson clouds generates quasi-continuous gravitational wave emission. In this work, we explore the prospects for constraining and detecting ultralight bosons with observations of massive black hole binary mergers with the space-based LISA observatory. We consider two complementary approaches: measurements of black hole spins from merging binaries and follow-up gravitational wave searches targeting massive black hole binary merger remnants. We consider three population models for massive black holes, based on either heavy or light seeds,
  and forecast the exclusion and detection probabilities for both scalar and vector bosons.
  We find that black hole spin measurements can constrain scalar masses in the range $[5\times10^{-18},10^{-14}]$ eV and vector masses in the range $[6\times10^{-19},2\times10^{-14}]$ eV, with the exact range depending on the model.
  In contrast, restricting to vector bosons, follow-up gravitational wave searches are sensitive to a narrower vector boson mass range of $\sim[3\times10^{-17},3\times10^{-15}]$ eV, with the specific values again depending on the model. If a vector boson with a mass in the range $[10^{-16},2\times10^{-15}]$ eV existed, the probability of having an event that the follow-up searches would be sensitive to ranges from very small to near unity depending on the astrophysical model.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how LISA observations of massive black hole binary mergers can constrain or detect ultralight scalar and vector bosons via superradiant spin-down effects and post-merger gravitational wave signatures from boson clouds.
AI.motivation: Ultralight bosons induce superradiant instabilities around rotating black holes, affecting spins and emitting quasi-continuous gravitational waves; detecting these effects with LISA could probe new particle physics beyond the Standard Model.
AI.method: The authors perform forecasting analyses using two complementary LISA observational strategies: (1) spin measurements from inspiral waveforms of merging binaries, and (2) follow-up searches for gravitational waves from boson clouds around post-merger remnants. They adopt three astrophysical massive black hole population models (heavy/light seed scenarios) and compute exclusion/detection probabilities for scalar and vector bosons across mass ranges.
AI.result: Spin measurements constrain scalar bosons in [5×10⁻¹⁸, 10⁻¹⁴] eV and vector bosons in [6×10⁻¹⁹, 2×10⁻¹⁴] eV; follow-up searches are sensitive only to vector bosons in ~[3×10⁻¹⁷, 3×10⁻¹⁵] eV. Detection probability for vector bosons in [10⁻¹⁶, 2×10⁻¹⁵] eV ranges from near-zero to near-unity depending on the population model.
AI.conclusion: LISA offers a powerful probe of ultralight bosons—spin measurements provide broad mass-range exclusions, while post-merger follow-up searches enable targeted detection in a narrower, higher-sensitivity window; joint analysis improves coverage and model discrimination.

title: Thermal Origin of Black Hole Quasinormal Modes
summary: When a black hole rings after a merger, it emits gravitational waves at characteristic frequencies known as quasinormal modes (QNMs). In the eikonal limit, these modes are governed by the unstable circular light orbits that form the photon ring. In this work, we demonstrate that the ringing of a black hole has a precise thermal interpretation. A probe string propagating in the near-ring geometry acquires an induced Rindler horizon on its worldsheet, with a temperature set by the Lyapunov exponent of the photon ring. Out of this structure, the black hole QNMs emerge as thermal excitations, so that the characteristic ringing of a black hole is the retarded response of a thermal system living on the photon ring. We explicitly derive the QNM spectrum from two complementary perspectives: microscopically, via unstable transverse worldsheet fluctuations, and macroscopically, through the pole structure of the causal response function of an open thermal quantum system.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a thermal interpretation of black hole quasinormal modes (QNMs) by linking them to an induced Rindler horizon on a probe string near the photon ring, with temperature determined by the photon ring's Lyapunov exponent; QNMs arise as thermal excitations, derived both microscopically (worldsheet fluctuations) and macroscopically (causal response poles).
AI.motivation: To provide a physical, thermal interpretation of black hole quasinormal modes—traditionally understood via perturbative gravity—by connecting them to universal near-horizon physics and instability of photon orbits.
AI.method: Analyzes a probe string in the near-photon-ring geometry; identifies an induced worldsheet Rindler horizon; computes its temperature from the Lyapunov exponent; derives QNM spectrum via transverse worldsheet fluctuation analysis and causal response function pole analysis of an open thermal quantum system.
AI.result: Demonstrates that black hole QNMs emerge as thermal excitations of a system living on the photon ring; explicitly recovers the QNM spectrum from both microscopic (string worldsheet) and macroscopic (open quantum system response) perspectives.
AI.conclusion: Black hole ringing is not merely a gravitational wave phenomenon but the retarded thermal response of a quantum system localized at the photon ring, unifying geometric optics, chaos (Lyapunov exponent), and thermal field theory in black hole perturbation theory.

title: Leptogenesis in Brane-modified cosmology: Signatures in primordial gravitational waves
summary: We investigate the implications of brane-inspired modifications of the evolutionary history of the early universe on the process of baryogenesis via leptogenesis. A modified cosmic history alters the evolution of the Boltzmann equations governing lepton asymmetry, providing the possibility of successful leptogenesis in regions of the parameter space inaccessible in the standard cosmological scenario. Furthermore, a modified cosmic history also alters the shape of an otherwise scale-invariant spectral energy density (SED) of primary gravitational waves (PGWs) produced during inflation. This establishes a novel yet indirect probe of high scale leptogenesis scenarios through the observation of the SED of PGWs via future observations. We consider two scenarios in this work with single and multiple epochs of stiff equation of state(s) after inflation and before the epoch of radiation domination. We identify the parameter space where successful leptogenesis is possible, along with the possible observability of the PGWs, hence providing an indirect window into this leptogenesis scenario through PGWs.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how brane-inspired early-universe modifications enable successful leptogenesis in otherwise inaccessible parameter regions and alter the spectral energy density of primordial gravitational waves, offering an indirect observational probe via future PGW measurements.
AI.motivation: To examine how non-standard cosmic evolution—inspired by brane cosmology—affects leptogenesis viability and modifies the spectral energy density of primordial gravitational waves, thereby linking high-scale baryogenesis to potentially observable PGW signatures.
AI.method: Analyzes Boltzmann equation evolution for lepton asymmetry under modified Friedmann expansion histories featuring single or multiple stiff-equation-of-state epochs post-inflation and pre-radiation domination; computes resulting PGW spectral energy density deviations from scale invariance.
AI.result: Identifies extended parameter space where thermal leptogenesis succeeds due to altered expansion history; predicts characteristic deviations in PGW spectral energy density that are potentially detectable by next-generation gravitational-wave observatories.
AI.conclusion: Brane-motivated early-universe modifications not only revive otherwise excluded leptogenesis scenarios but also imprint distinctive, observable features in the PGW spectrum—establishing a novel indirect test of high-scale leptogenesis through PGW observations.

title: Rotating near-horizon extreme geometries in quadratic gravity
summary: Rotating near-horizon extreme solutions of quadratic gravity are analyzed combining power series expansions and numerical calculations. Restricting to geometries with symmetries of the near-horizon extreme Kerr black hole (i.e., with the $\mathrm{AdS_2}$-structure), spherical horizon topology, and equatorial reflection symmetry, we introduce conformal coordinates simplifying the field equations of Einstein--Weyl gravity, i.e., quadratic gravity with vanishing scalar curvature. Employing the Frobenius analysis, we classify all power series solutions expanded around the equator as well as the poles, and obtain the recurrence relations. With the help of numerical analysis, we study fine-tuning of the free parameter to satisfy the global constraints on regular near-horizon extreme geometries. Computations of the horizon area, horizon scalar curvature, and rotational scalar reveal strong horizon deformations in some Bachian branches. Moreover, the absence of regular Bachian near-horizon geometries above a finite horizon area suggests an upper bound on the size of the corresponding extremal rotating black holes.
