AI.tldr: This paper analyzes rotating near-horizon extreme solutions in quadratic (Einstein–Weyl) gravity using power series expansions and numerical methods, under AdS₂-symmetric, spherical, and equatorially symmetric assumptions; it classifies local Frobenius solutions, identifies fine-tuning requirements for global regularity, and finds horizon deformation bounds implying an upper limit on extremal black hole size.
AI.motivation: To explore whether rotating near-horizon extreme geometries beyond general relativity—specifically in quadratic (Einstein–Weyl) gravity—can remain regular and physically viable, motivated by the role of higher-curvature corrections in quantum gravity and black hole uniqueness.
AI.method: Combines analytic Frobenius power series expansions (around equator and poles) with numerical shooting methods to enforce global regularity constraints; uses conformal coordinates adapted to AdS₂ × S² near-horizon structure and imposes vanishing scalar curvature for Einstein–Weyl gravity.
AI.result: Classification of local power series solutions with recurrence relations; identification of Bachian solution branches exhibiting strong horizon deformations; numerical evidence that regular near-horizon geometries cease to exist beyond a finite horizon area, implying an upper bound on extremal black hole size.
AI.conclusion: Regular rotating near-horizon extreme geometries in Einstein–Weyl gravity are highly constrained: only finely tuned parameters yield global solutions, and their existence terminates at a maximal horizon area—suggesting a fundamental size limit for corresponding extremal black holes.

title: Closed-form thermal threshold functions for the proper-time renormalisation group
summary:
We derive closed-form expressions for the thermal threshold functions of the finite-temperature proper-time renormalisation group (PTRG): until now these have been evaluated numerically, Matsubara mode by Matsubara mode. For the standard one-parameter regulator family, Poisson resummation of the Matsubara sum yields a rapidly convergent winding-number series of modified Bessel functions, and a single algebraic identity reduces every higher threshold function to this same closed form at a shifted kernel parameter. The sharp proper-time regulator, recovered as the exact $m\to\infty$ endpoint of the family with a controlled $O(1/m)$ approach, factorises into a field-dependent and a purely thermal piece.
  Built on them, the local potential approximation (LPA) and its refinement to a running anomalous dimension (LPA$'$) for the $O(N)$-symmetric theory reduce to established results, all cross-checked against the exact Wetterich equation with the optimised regulator. Two findings go beyond reduction. First, the known zero-temperature anomalous-dimension construction is extended here to finite temperature. Second, because the closed form holds for any real regulator parameter, the refined truncation's fixed point can for the first time be tracked as a continuous function of the regulator, rather than at a handful of isolated points, and is found to vary smoothly and remain bounded, with no special or pathological point anywhere on the line.

AI.tldr: This paper derives closed-form analytical expressions for thermal threshold functions in the finite-temperature proper-time renormalisation group (PTRG), replacing previous numerical Matsubara-mode summations. Using Poisson resummation and Bessel functions, it generalises results across the one-parameter regulator family—including the sharp proper-time limit—and enables continuous tracking of fixed points in LPA′ truncations for O(N) theory.
AI.motivation: To replace computationally expensive, mode-by-mode numerical evaluation of thermal threshold functions in PTRG with efficient, analytically tractable closed-form expressions—enabling deeper insight into regulator dependence, thermal effects, and fixed-point structure.
AI.method: Poisson resummation of the Matsubara sum yields a winding-number series of modified Bessel functions; algebraic identities reduce all higher threshold functions to a single closed form with shifted kernel parameter; the sharp proper-time regulator is recovered as the m→∞ limit of the one-parameter family; LPA and LPA′ truncations for O(N) theory are implemented and cross-validated against the exact Wetterich equation with optimised regulator.
AI.result: Closed-form thermal threshold functions for the entire one-parameter regulator family; extension of zero-temperature anomalous dimension construction to finite temperature; first continuous tracking of LPA′ fixed points across regulator parameter space—showing smooth, bounded behavior without pathologies.
AI.conclusion: Analytical tractability of thermal PTRG is significantly enhanced: closed forms enable robust, regulator-continuous analysis of thermal quantum field theories; the absence of singularities in fixed-point trajectories suggests structural stability of the LPA′ approximation across regulator choices.

title: On the Renormalization in Conformal Quantum Gravity
summary: One-loop divergences in classically conformal theory in curved spacetime is a nontrivial issue if the theory under consideration possesses gauge invariance. In this case, quantization involves introducing the gauge-fixing term and the action of ghosts, both of which are not conformal. The formal proof of the conformal invariant renormalizability in this situation, including interacting theories, has been given in the paper from 1984 by one of the present authors. Owing to BRST symmetry, the contributions of the gauge-fixing and ghost sectors to the conformal variation of the effective action cancel each other. This cancellation does not hold in the finite part of the one-loop and higher-loops effective action, that results in the anomaly. In this paper, we extend the early results on conformal matter fields in external gravitational field and apply them to conformal quantum gravity, including the case of conformal gravity coupled to other conformal matter fields. The gauge-fixing in the Weyl-squared gravity is more complicated, nevertheless, the proof of the one-loop conformal invariant renormalization using BRST symmetry is possible. As a preliminary to conformal quantum gravity, we also present a detailed general proof of conformal invariant one-loop divergences in the corresponding semiclassical theory.

AI.tldr: This paper extends prior work on conformal invariance in quantum field theory to conformal gravity, proving one-loop conformal-invariant renormalizability using BRST symmetry despite non-conformal gauge-fixing and ghost terms; it addresses anomalies arising in finite parts and provides a general proof for semiclassical conformal gravity coupled to matter.
AI.motivation: To resolve the nontrivial issue of one-loop divergences in classically conformal theories in curved spacetime—particularly gauge-invariant ones—where gauge-fixing and ghost actions break classical conformal symmetry, yet BRST symmetry ensures cancellation of conformal anomalies in divergent parts.
AI.method: Leverages BRST symmetry to demonstrate cancellation between gauge-fixing and ghost sector contributions to the conformal variation of the effective action at the divergent (one-loop) level; extends this framework to Weyl-squared gravity and conformal gravity coupled to conformal matter; includes rigorous semiclassical analysis.
AI.result: Establishes one-loop conformal-invariant renormalizability for conformal quantum gravity—including Weyl-squared gravity—and proves that divergences remain conformally invariant despite non-conformal quantization artifacts; identifies that anomalies persist only in finite parts beyond divergences.
AI.conclusion: Conformal invariance of one-loop divergences holds in gauge-invariant conformal theories in curved spacetime—including conformal quantum gravity—due to BRST-induced cancellation; however, finite quantum corrections break conformal symmetry, producing anomalies.

title: The quadratic growth of Krylov spread complexity in the BTZ black hole
comment: v1: 22 (main text) + 15 pages (appendices), 10 figures, Research data available at https://uj.rodbuk.pl/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.57903/UJ/CESIIM
summary: The boundary quantity that captures the growth of black-hole interiors quantified by holographic complexity remains unknown beyond 2d dilaton gravity. We provide a critical analysis of a partition-function construction of Krylov spread complexity for thermofield-double states that provides a dimension-independent boundary reconstruction from semiclassical holographic partition functions, while developing the present dynamical and bulk construction for the BTZ saddle. In the double-scaled Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model, where exact and semiclassical results can be compared, we show that the classical limit is reliable only when taken after the complexity has been reconstructed; taking this limit at the level of individual Lanczos coefficients discards essential information. Applying the construction to a large-central-charge two-dimensional conformal field theory above the Hawking-Page temperature dual to a Bañados-Teitelboim-Zanelli black hole, we find an intermediate departure from early-time quadratic growth followed by behavior compatible with a return toward asymptotically quadratic growth, rather than the linear late-time behavior of the volume and the standard finite-functional complexity = anything class. We then match this boundary behavior to a generalized complexity = anything bulk object built from an infinite series of extrinsic-curvature invariants. The construction provides a systematic route from black-hole thermodynamics to Krylov dynamics and can naturally be extended to higher-dimensional holographic black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a dimension-independent boundary reconstruction of holographic complexity using Krylov spread complexity for thermofield-double states, validates its semiclassical reliability in the double-scaled SYK model, applies it to 2D CFT/BTZ holography revealing non-linear late-time complexity growth, and matches the result to a bulk 'complexity = anything' functional built from extrinsic-curvature invariants.
AI.motivation: To identify the boundary quantity capturing black-hole interior growth (i.e., holographic complexity) beyond 2D dilaton gravity, where the boundary dual remains unknown.
AI.method: Constructs Krylov spread complexity from semiclassical holographic partition functions; analyzes its classical limit in the double-scaled SYK model; applies it to large-c 2D CFT at temperatures above Hawking-Page transition dual to BTZ black holes; matches boundary complexity dynamics to a generalized bulk complexity functional expressed as an infinite series of extrinsic-curvature invariants.
AI.result: Reveals intermediate deviation from early-time quadratic complexity growth followed by asymptotic return to quadratic (not linear) behavior—contrasting volume and standard finite-functional complexity = anything proposals—and establishes a systematic mapping from black-hole thermodynamics to Krylov dynamics.
AI.conclusion: Krylov spread complexity provides a robust, dimension-independent boundary characterization of black-hole interior growth; its semiclassical reconstruction must preserve quantum corrections until after complexity is computed; the resulting dynamics are captured by a novel bulk complexity functional involving extrinsic-curvature invariants, enabling extension to higher-dimensional holographic black holes.
